---
id: "wiki-data-pipeline"
title: "Data Pipeline Guide"
emoji: "Flow"
cluster: guide
derived: true
connections: []
---

How content flows from sources to rendered views — the [content pipeline](content-pipeline) from a user perspective.

## The Flow

```
Markdown → Parser → Providers → Orchestrator → Graph Engine → Views
```

## Step 1: Author Content

Create markdown in `content/` with YAML frontmatter. Use `[text](node-id)` links to create edges — [inline link extraction](inline-link-extraction) handles the rest.

## Step 2: Map Source Files

Add entries to `nodemap.yaml`. The [node mapping](node-mapping) system supports five modes. The [Node Mapping Spec](spec-node-mapping) has the schema.

## Step 3: Generate Manifest

```bash
npm run prebuild
```

The [build scripts](build-scripts) capture everything the [local loader](local-loader) needs.

## Step 4: Inspect the Graph

```bash
node scripts/assess-graph.js
```

Evaluates connectivity (4-8 links/node target), cluster balance, orphans, and hub reachability.

## Providers

| Provider | Input | Output |
|----------|-------|--------|
| [Authored](authored-provider) | Markdown + nodemap | Content nodes |
| [Files](files-provider) | File tree | Directory/file nodes |
| [Work](work-provider) | Issues/PRs/commits | Work nodes |

## Troubleshooting

- **Broken links** — check target node IDs exist; the [parser](parser) drops invalid links
- **Missing edges** — use `[text](node-id)` format, not full URLs
- **Stale graph** — re-run `npm run prebuild` and restart [Vite](vite-config)
authoredContent.content/wiki-deep-dive.md:
---
id: "wiki-deep-dive"
title: "Architecture Deep Dive"
emoji: "Search"
cluster: guide
derived: true
connections: []
---

Full architecture trace from startup to rendering. Read the [overview](overview) first, or the [welcome page](wiki-overview) for a user-oriented introduction.

## Startup Sequence

1. [Application shell](app-shell) mounts, calls the [KB loader hook](kb-loader)
2. Hook detects mode — [local loader](local-loader) or [GitHub API](github-api)
3. [Providers](providers-overview) are registered and run by the [orchestrator](orchestrator)
4. [Parser](parser) processes markdown, issues, file trees into `KBNode[]`
5. [Graph engine](graph-engine) computes edges, clusters, related nodes
6. Shell renders the appropriate view

## The Type Foundation

Everything builds on the [type system](type-system). `KBNode`, `KBEdge`, `KBGraph`, `Cluster` flow through every module.

## The Identity Problem

Multiple providers can produce nodes for the same entity. The [identity system](identity) assigns URN strings so the graph recognizes duplicates. The [multi-layer identity spec](multi-layer-identity) explains the design.

## Edge Discovery

Edges come from: frontmatter connections, [inline links](inline-link-extraction), issue cross-references, import analysis via [node mapping](node-mapping), and structural containment. The [typed edges spec](typed-edges) categorizes each.

## Rendering Stack

The [visual system](visual-system) coordinates seven surfaces. The [node renderer](node-renderer) draws Fluent icons on canvas. The [theme system](theme-system) provides three palettes. The [style system](style-system) handles layout.

## Design Rationale

Key decisions are in the [design decisions](design-decisions) node. The [link assessment spec](spec-link-assessment) defines quality metrics for graph health.

This guide walks you through setting up kbexplorer for local development.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js 18+** and npm
- **Git** for cloning
- Optional: `gh` CLI for fetching GitHub data into the manifest

## Step 1: Clone and Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template.git
cd kbexplorer-template
npm install
```

## Step 2: Generate the Manifest

The [build scripts](build-scripts) create a local manifest:

```bash
npm run prebuild
```

This runs the [manifest generator](manifest-generator) which walks the file system and optionally calls `gh` for issue data. Output goes to `src/generated/repo-manifest.json`.

## Step 3: Start Development

```bash
npm run dev
```

Vite starts on `http://localhost:5173`. The [Vite configuration](vite-config) auto-regenerates the manifest on build start.

## Step 4: Explore

- Open the browser — land on the [overview grid](overview-view)
- Click a card to enter the [reading view](reading-view)
- Pick a theme from the paint-palette menu in the [HUD](hud) — or press `t` to cycle [themes](theme-system)
- Open the [HUD](hud) minimap to see the full constellation

## Troubleshooting

- **`$RefreshReg$ is not defined`** — Vite HMR stale cache. Kill Vite, delete `node_modules/.vite`, restart
- **Empty graph** — run `npm run prebuild` to regenerate
- **Rate limited** — the [local loader](local-loader) bypasses the [GitHub API](github-api) entirely

Bird's-eye view of the constellation. Current node highlighted. Click to jump. Uses [graph network](graph-network)'s `computeGraphPositions()`.

## Related Panel

Up to 12 connected nodes as [NodeVisual](node-visual) cards. Click to navigate. Ranking prioritizes strongly-typed edges over high-degree weak connections (#52).

## Layer Toggles

Four buttons show/hide node groups: Content ([authored provider](authored-provider)), File ([files provider](files-provider)), Work ([work provider](work-provider)), Concept. Added in #55.

## Cluster Collapse

Click cluster label to collapse all nodes into one summary node. The [node renderer](node-renderer) draws a stacked appearance. Click again to expand. From #57.

## Dock Positions

Drag to any screen edge. The [style system](style-system) adapts layout. Persists in localStorage. Added in PR #28 alongside depth controls.

plus any host-repo themes) for direct selection.

Press `t` to cycle [themes](theme-system), arrows to navigate nodes — handled by [keyboard navigation](keyboard-nav).

npm run build      # Production build to dist/

title: "My Knowledge Base"

Defines how source files become graph nodes. See the [Node Mapping Spec](spec-node-mapping). The [node mapping](node-mapping) system processes five modes.

Configures Azure Static Web Apps SPA routing. The [application shell](app-shell) uses hash-based routing.

emoji: "Color"

Three built-in visual themes ship with the app, and your host repo can add more.

## Available Themes

| Theme | How to switch | Best For |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| **Dark** | paint-palette menu or `t` | Code reading, low light |
| **Light** | paint-palette menu or `t` | Bright environments, presentations |
| **Sepia** | paint-palette menu or `t` | Extended reading, reduced eye strain |

Named themes defined in `config.yaml` (see [External Theming](theming-overview))
join the same list. Switch between any of them from the **paint-palette menu**
in the HUD (it lists every available theme with the active one checked), or press
**`t`** to cycle through them.

## How Themes Propagate

The [theme system](theme-system) returns a Fluent `Theme` object that the [application shell](app-shell) passes to `<FluentProvider>`. Every Fluent component picks up correct colors automatically.

Custom components use Fluent tokens via the [style system](style-system). The [node renderer](node-renderer) reads `isDark` to adjust canvas rendering. The [graph network](graph-network) uses theme colors for edges and backgrounds.

## The Sepia Theme

Custom `createLightTheme()` with amber brand ramp, overriding 20+ tokens:

```typescript
colorNeutralBackground1: '#F5ECD7'  // warm paper
colorNeutralForeground1: '#2A2520'  // warm dark text
```

## Customizing

You no longer need to edit the `.kbexplorer` submodule to restyle the site.
Everything is driven from your host repo's `config.yaml` (plus optional companion
files). The fastest path: add a `theme.brand` seed to recolor the whole app, or
add entries under `theme.themes` to grow the paint-palette menu (and the `t` cycle)
with your own variants.

See **[External Theming](theming-overview)** for the full picture:
[brand, tokens & named themes](theming-named-themes),
[branding assets](theming-branding),
[scoped per-cluster/per-page theming](theming-scoped), and the
[modular escape hatches](theming-escape-hatches) (external theme file, raw CSS,
custom JS module).

## Persistence

Stored in localStorage under `kbe-theme`. The [visual system](visual-system) and [overview view](overview-view) respect the theme automatically.

| Constellation | [Graph Network](graph-network) | Canvas via [Node Renderer](node-renderer) |
| Minimap | [HUD](hud) | Colored dots |
| Breadcrumbs | Navigation | Inline icon + text |
| Search | Filter panel | Compact list items |

## Icons

Fluent icons colored with cluster color — never monochrome. The [node renderer](node-renderer) embeds 150+ SVG paths.

## Cluster Colors

| Cluster | Color |
|---------|-------|
| Engine | #4A9CC8 |
| Interface | #8CB050 |
| Visual | #E8A838 |
| Data | #C07840 |
| Infrastructure | #5A98A8 |
| Design | #A86FDF |
| Guide | #39FF14 |

## Emphasis and Fading

Hover a node → [graph network](graph-network)'s `setEmphasis()` highlights it and neighbors, fading everything else.

## Sizing Rules

Per AGENTS.md: no pixels for layout dimensions. Use viewport units, percentages, or Fluent tokens. The [style system](style-system) enforces this. The [theme system](theme-system) provides the color foundation.

readme:
# kbexplorer-template

Interactive Knowledge Base Explorer — turn any GitHub repository into a navigable knowledge graph.

[![Deploy to GitHub Pages](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/actions/workflows/github-pages.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/actions/workflows/github-pages.yml)

**Live demo:** [anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer-template](https://anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer-template/)

---

## What is kbexplorer?

**kbexplorer** is a React + TypeScript application by [Anokye Labs](https://github.com/anokye-labs) that presents knowledge as an interactive, explorable graph. Point it at any GitHub repository and it transforms issues, pull requests, source files, and documentation into an interconnected constellation — navigable through a [card grid](overview-view), a force-directed [constellation graph](graph-network), or deep-dive [reading views](reading-view).

The project draws inspiration from three systems: **Claws**, a structured knowledge-base browser designed for fast retrieval; **Mukaase**, a narrative-first reader that treats content as linked prose; and **Okoto walkthrough**, an interactive tutorial engine that guides learners through a topic graph step by step. kbexplorer synthesizes these ideas into a single tool — exploration, narrative reading, and guided walkthrough in one interface.

Everything runs client-side. Content is fetched at runtime from the [GitHub API](github-api) with no build step required for content changes. Deploy once, and the knowledge graph stays current with the repository it explores. For offline or CI workflows, [local mode](local-loader) uses a pre-built [manifest](manifest-generator) instead.

## Features

- **[Card grid overview](overview-view)** — topics grouped by cluster with [visual identity](visual-system) cards
- **[Constellation graph](graph-network)** — force-directed network visualization with [custom node rendering](node-renderer) and typed edges
- **[Reading view](reading-view)** — full markdown prose with inline links that navigate the graph
- **Persistent [HUD](hud)** — minimap, related-nodes panel, layer toggles, and reading tools visible across views
- **[Theme switching](theme-system)** — dark, light, and sepia modes with customizable fonts
- **[Keyboard navigation](keyboard-nav)** — full keyboard support for view switching and node traversal
- **Responsive design** — adapts from desktop to mobile via the [CSS style system](style-system)
- **Runtime content** — fetches from the [GitHub API client](github-api) with [localStorage caching](cache-system) (no rebuild needed)

## Content Modes

kbexplorer supports [two content modes](wiki-content-modes), configured by the presence of a `source.path` in `config.yaml`.

### Repo-aware (default)

When no content path is set, kbexplorer treats the target GitHub repository itself as the knowledge base. The [content pipeline](content-pipeline) fetches issues, pull requests, the README, and source files, then maps them into a graph. Issue labels become clusters; cross-references become [typed edges](spec-typed-edges).

For a live example, explore this project's own [issues](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer/issues) — each one becomes a navigable node in the graph.

### Authored

When `source.path` points to a directory of markdown files (e.g., `content/`), kbexplorer parses each file's YAML frontmatter to build a hand-curated knowledge base. The [content pipeline](content-pipeline) extracts [inline links](spec-inline-link-extraction) from the markdown body to create graph edges automatically — frontmatter connections are supplementary.

## Visual Identity System

kbexplorer's [visual system](visual-system) provides four modes for presenting nodes. Each mode determines what asset type the [node renderer](node-renderer) draws across seven surfaces in the UI.

### Modes

| Mode | Assets | Best For |
|------|--------|----------|
| `sprites` | Character illustrations | Technical walkthroughs, branded docs |
| `heroes` | Full-bleed photography | Essays, narratives, editorial |
| `emoji` | Unicode emoji | Lightweight, text-focused |
| `none` | Text only | Minimal deployments |

### Surfaces

Visuals appear on these surfaces throughout the application:

| Surface | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| [Overview cards](overview-view) | Card thumbnails in the [card grid](overview-view) |
| [Graph nodes](graph-network) | Node icons in the [constellation](graph-network) view |
| [Reading header](reading-view) | Hero image or sprite at the top of a [reading view](reading-view) |
| [HUD](hud) minimap | Miniature node representations in the [HUD](hud) minimap |
| [HUD](hud) related | Thumbnails in the [related-nodes panel](hud) |
| [Loading screen](loading-error-screens) | Visual shown during initial content fetch |
| Page favicon | Dynamic favicon reflecting the active node |

A `fallback` mode activates when the primary mode's asset is missing for a given node (e.g., a node without a `sprite` field falls back to `emoji`).

## Getting Started

For a comprehensive guide, see [Getting Started](wiki-getting-started). For a deeper look at internals, see the [Architecture Deep Dive](wiki-deep-dive).

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js 18+** and npm

### Install and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template.git
cd kbexplorer-template
npm install
npm run dev
```

The [Vite](vite-config) dev server starts at `http://localhost:5173`. By default, kbexplorer explores its own GitHub repository.

### Build for production

The [build scripts](build-scripts) run TypeScript type-checking (`tsc -b`) before bundling with [Vite](vite-config):

```bash
npm run build
```

Output is written to `dist/`.

### Lint

```bash
npm run lint
```

## Configuration

kbexplorer loads a `config.yaml` from the target repository at runtime. See the [configuration reference](wiki-configuration) for full details. Place it at the root of the content path (or repo root for repo-aware mode).

```yaml
title: "My Knowledge Base"
subtitle: "An explorable guide"
author: "Your Name"
date: "2025"

source:
  owner: your-org
  repo: your-repo
  path: content          # omit for repo-aware mode
  branch: main

structuredContent:
  path: content-model    # optional; defaults to top-level content-model/

clusters:
  concept:
    name: Concepts
    color: "#4A9CC8"
  tutorial:
    name: Tutorials
    color: "#8CB050"
  reference:
    name: Reference
    color: "#E8A838"

visuals:
  mode: emoji            # sprites | heroes | emoji | none
  fallback: emoji
  hero:
    overlay: dark-gradient
    height: "300px"
    animation: reveal
  graph:
    nodeImages: true
    nodeSizeByConnections: true

theme:
  default: dark          # dark | light | sepia
  font:
    heading: "Instrument Serif"
    body: "General Sans"
    mono: "JetBrains Mono"

graph:
  physics: true
  layout: force-atlas-2  # force-atlas-2 | manual

features:
  hud: true
  minimap: true
  readingTools: true
  keyboardNav: true
  sparkAnimation: false
  search: true           # optional — unset means enabled; false hides the Ctrl-K palette

bluf:
  quote: "Knowledge is the path."
  duration: "5s"
```

## Content Authoring

In authored mode, each markdown file in the content directory becomes a node. The [content pipeline](content-pipeline) parses YAML frontmatter and extracts [inline links](spec-inline-link-extraction) from the body to create graph edges automatically. Use frontmatter to define metadata:

```markdown
---
id: intro-to-graphs
title: Introduction to Graphs
emoji: "🕸️"
cluster: concept
image: assets/graphs-hero.jpg    # heroes mode
sprite: assets/graphs-sprite.png # sprites mode
parent: fundamentals
connections:
  - to: graph-traversal
    description: "prerequisite for"
  - to: adjacency-matrix
    description: "introduces"
---

# Introduction to Graphs

A graph is a set of **nodes** connected by **edges**...
```

### Frontmatter fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | Yes | Unique node identifier used in [inline links](spec-inline-link-extraction) |
| `title` | Yes | Display title shown in the [reading view](reading-view) and [HUD](hud) |
| `emoji` | No | Fluent icon name or Unicode emoji for the [visual system](visual-system) |
| `cluster` | No | Cluster ID (must match a key in `config.yaml` [clusters](wiki-configuration)) |
| `image` | No | Hero image path for the [visual system](visual-system) heroes mode |
| `sprite` | No | Sprite illustration path for sprites mode |
| `parent` | No | Parent node ID for hierarchical grouping |
| `connections` | No | Supplementary `{ to, description }` edges (prefer [inline links](spec-inline-link-extraction)) |
| `access` | No | Label-only access descriptor (`classification`, `visibility`, `labels`) — see [Access labels](#access-labels-minimal-render-gate) |

### Access labels (minimal render-gate)

Authored docs may declare a core-v0.3.0 `KBAccessLabel` in frontmatter:

```yaml
access:
  classification: restricted   # public | internal | confidential | restricted | unknown
  visibility: private          # public | internal | private
```

A node whose label marks it `restricted`, `confidential`, explicitly
`unknown`, or `visibility: private` is **withheld**: it is excluded from the
assembled graph (never rendered) and from client-side search. An absent label
means public — unlabeled nodes behave exactly as before.

**Honesty note — what is NOT enforced yet:** this is the minimal render-gate
only. Core's full access contract is not implemented: `AccessConfig.redactionBoundary`
is not read (the gate always withholds; `label-only` and `redact` modes are
unsupported), no redaction stubs are emitted (`commitRedactionStubs` is
ignored), edge-level `access` labels are not evaluated, and core's stricter
default-safe stance (withhold *unlabeled/unknown-classified* resources by
default) is deliberately relaxed to "absent label = public" for this template.
Labels also do not protect the underlying sources — anyone with repo read
access can read the files; the gate only keeps labeled nodes out of the
rendered graph and search index.

### Clusters

Clusters group nodes by topic. Define them in `config.yaml` with a display name and color. Nodes reference clusters by key in their `cluster` frontmatter field.

### Connections

Connections create edges between nodes. In repo-aware mode, the [content pipeline](content-pipeline) infers connections from issue cross-references and PR links as [typed edges](spec-typed-edges). In authored mode, [inline links](spec-inline-link-extraction) in the markdown body (`[text](target-id)`) are the primary way to create edges — the parser extracts them automatically. Frontmatter `connections:` are supplementary for relationships that can't be expressed inline.

## Using in Another Repo

Install the CLI tool and run [init](init-script):

```bash
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer init
```

This adds `.kbexplorer/` as a submodule, installs agents and skills to `.github/agents/` and `.github/skills/`, runs an interactive [config wizard](init-script), and sets up npm scripts.

### CLI Commands

```bash
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer init        # Setup: submodule + agents + skills + config
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer generate    # Generate content from code analysis
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer dev         # Start dev server (local mode)
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer build       # Production build
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer manifest    # Regenerate repo manifest
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer update      # Pull latest template + refresh agents/skills
```

The `manifest` command runs the [manifest generator](manifest-generator) to pre-build a snapshot of the repo's content, issues, and file tree for [local mode](local-loader). The `generate` command uses the [catalogue transformer](catalogue-transformer) to convert AI-generated analysis into authored content nodes.

Or install locally: `npm install -D @anokye-labs/kbexplorer`

### Updating

```bash
npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer update
```

For more details, see the [CLI documentation](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli).

## Deployment

kbexplorer deploys to **Azure Static Web Apps** via GitHub Actions.

### Setup

1. Create an Azure Static Web App resource in the [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com)
2. Copy the deployment token from the Azure resource
3. Add it as a repository secret named `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN`
4. Push to `main` — the workflow builds and deploys automatically

Pull requests get automatic staging environments. The `staticwebapp.config.json` in the repo root handles SPA routing, rewriting all paths to `index.html` (excluding static assets).

### Workflow

The GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/azure-static-web-apps.yml`) triggers on:

- **Push to main** — builds and deploys to production
- **Pull request** — builds and deploys a staging preview
- **PR closed** — cleans up the staging environment

## Architecture

The [application shell](app-shell) boots the UI and sets up routing. The [KB loader](kb-loader) hook fetches content — either from the [GitHub API client](github-api) at runtime or from a pre-built [manifest](manifest-generator) in [local mode](local-loader).

```
src/
├── api/          GitHub API client with localStorage caching
├── engine/       Graph engine, content pipeline, and parser
├── components/   HUD, NodeVisual, LoadingScreen, ErrorScreen
├── views/        OverviewView, GraphView, ReadingView
├── hooks/        useKnowledgeBase, useTheme, useKeyboardNav
├── styles/       CSS style system
└── types/        Core type definitions: KBNode, KBGraph, KBConfig
```

**Data flow:** The [KB loader](kb-loader) fetches content via the [GitHub API client](github-api) with [localStorage caching](cache-system) → the [content pipeline](content-pipeline) normalizes it into `KBNode[]` using the [type system](type-system) → the [graph engine](graph-engine) computes [typed edges](spec-typed-edges), clusters, and related nodes → the [overview grid](overview-view), [constellation graph](graph-network), and [reading view](reading-view) render the `KBGraph`.

**Graph intelligence:** The [graph engine](graph-engine) ranks connections by [edge weight](spec-typed-edges) — structural edges like `contains` rank higher than inferred `mentions`. The [HUD](hud) uses this to show the most relevant [related nodes](hud) for whatever you're reading. [Inline links](spec-inline-link-extraction) in authored content become first-class graph edges automatically.

**Rendering:** The [custom node renderer](node-renderer) draws 2,600+ Fluent UI icons on the HTML canvas. Each node's shape and color is determined by its cluster and the [visual system](visual-system). The [graph network factory](graph-network) handles physics simulation, neighborhood emphasis, and pan/zoom.

**Routing:** Hash-based routing via `react-router-dom` (`#/`, `#/graph`, `#/node/:id`). No server-side routing required.

**Key dependencies:**

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `react` / `react-dom` | UI framework (v19) |
| `react-router-dom` | Client-side routing |
| `vis-network` / `vis-data` | Graph visualization |
| `@octokit/rest` | GitHub API client |
| `gray-matter` | YAML frontmatter parsing |
| `marked` | Markdown → HTML rendering |
| `yaml` | Configuration file parsing |

## Roadmap

The [graph provider architecture](spec-providers-overview) is the next major evolution — replacing the current monolithic pipeline with pluggable providers for files, git, GitHub, and external services. Key specs:

- **[Node mapping](spec-node-mapping)** — how files become nodes, with configurable `nodemap.yaml`
- **[Graph store](spec-graph-store)** — SQLite-backed graph persistence with provider interface
- **[Views and projections](spec-views)** — filtered views, on-demand expansion, and external providers
- **[Multi-layer identity](spec-multi-layer-identity)** — same entity recognized across providers

For supplying organizational data from an external pipeline, see the [Work-Graph Vocabulary](docs/work-graph-vocabulary.md) and the [BYO People Feed contract](docs/byo-people-feed.md) — the supported way to feed `person` descriptors (e.g. from a Microsoft Graph org snapshot) that pass validation and render in the bespoke person view.

The [link assessment](spec-link-assessment) tool already provides graph health analysis — orphan detection, broken references, coverage gaps.

## Releases & versioning

Releases are cut as immutable git tags (`vX.Y.Z`) with matching GitHub Releases.
Host repos that vendor this template should **pin to a tag**, not track `main`.

- **[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)** — notable changes per release.
- **[docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md)** — template ↔ kbexplorer CLI
  compatibility matrix and the pinning contract (`kbexplorer doctor` treats a
  tag-pinned install as satisfied).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

issues.title: Template scripts/ become thin wrappers over kbx commands (retire ~4,900 LOC of parallel pipeline)
issues.body:
Parent: #463 (engine-extraction epic). Closes the third head of the duplication: template `scripts/` (18 scripts, ~4,915 LOC) vs cli `src/lib/` vs the engine.

## Problem

- `scripts/generate-manifest.js` (785 LOC) was forked into cli `src/lib/manifest.js` (568 LOC) and they have **diverged**; cli `src/lib/content-model.js` (525 LOC) parallels `src/engine/content-model/`.
- Once the CLI adopts the real engine (anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#226), `kbx` becomes the single Node pipeline, and the template's scripts should stop reimplementing it.

## What

Audit each script and classify:

| Script | Disposition |
|--------|-------------|
| `generate-manifest.js` (785) | replace with `kbx generate`/manifest command backed by the engine's `FileSystemSource` + sources; the npm `prebuild` hook calls kbx |
| `validate-graph.js`, `check-manifest-drift.js`, `assess-graph.js` | thin `kbx validate` / drift-gate wrappers (pattern already proven by `kbx search-index --check`) |
| `derive-content.js`, `compare-content.js`, `enrich-context.js` | `kbx derive`/`kbx compare` equivalents via the engine's content-model builder |
| `audit-runtime-graph.mjs`, `audit-visual.mjs`, `capture-review.mjs`, `verify-visual.mjs`, `probe-*.mjs`, `explore-dtu.mjs`, `smoke-real-repos.mjs` | genuinely template/visual/e2e concerns — KEEP local, but any graph-building inside them goes through the engine package, not private reimplementation |
| `generate-icon-manifest.js` | keep (asset concern) |

Each replaced script becomes ≤ ~30 LOC: parse args → shell out to `kbx …` (the repo already depends on the CLI: `kb:dev`/`kb:build`/`kb:generate` npm scripts exist).

## Acceptance

- `npm run prebuild`, `validate`, `validate:drift`, `assess`, `derive`, `compare` produce byte-identical artifacts to before (manifest, validation reports), now via kbx.
- Net LOC in `scripts/` drops by thousands; no script contains its own frontmatter/graph/content-model implementation.

## Verify

```
npm run prebuild && git diff --exit-code src/generated/
npm run validate && npm run validate:drift
npm test && npm run build:local
```

Blocked by: anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#226 (kbx must be engine-backed first)
Blocks: (none — final cleanup)

issues.title: Agent-scriptable engine API: loadKnowledgeBase + query/traverse helpers + script recipes docs
issues.body:
Parent: #463 (engine-extraction epic). This is the north-star deliverable: a coding agent must be able to write a 5–10 line Node script against `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine` to load → query → traverse → emit, with no browser and no app.

## Public API surface (to implement/document in the engine repo)

```ts
// entry "."
export async function loadKnowledgeBase(
  config: KBConfig,
  opts: { source: RepoSource; env?: EngineEnv; store?: GraphStore;
          providers?: GraphProvider[]; transforms?: GraphTransform[];
          hooks?: { onRepoData?(d: RepoData): RepoData } }
): Promise<KBGraph>
// (today's signature is loadKnowledgeBase(source, config) — normalize to config-first with an options bag; keep a deprecated overload during migration)

export { ProviderRegistry, defineProvider re-export, DEFAULT_TRANSFORMS,
         orchestrate, orchestrateWithTransforms, buildGraph }

// NEW: pure query/traverse helpers over KBGraph (new module src/query.ts)
export function getNode(g: KBGraph, id: string): KBNode | undefined
export function findNodes(g: KBGraph, pred: (n: KBNode) => boolean): KBNode[]
export function neighbors(g: KBGraph, id: string, opts?: { relation?: Relation; direction?: 'in'|'out'|'both' }): KBNode[]
export function related(g: KBGraph, id: string): KBNode[]          // graph.related index
export function subgraph(g: KBGraph, ids: string[], opts?: { hops?: number }): KBGraph
export function shortestPath(g: KBGraph, from: string, to: string): KBEdge[] | undefined

// entry "./sources"
export { ManifestSource, GitHubApiSource } and a NEW FileSystemSource(rootDir)  // Node-only; reads content/ + config.yaml from disk — the piece the CLI (cli#226) needs

// representation stays consumer-side: json-ld / llm-context targets already consume pure KBGraph
```

Everything promise-based; all I/O behind the injected `source`/`env`/`store` (dependency-injectable, so agents can stub them).

## Script recipes (ship as `docs/recipes.md` in the engine repo, each runnable)

1. Load a KB from a manifest file and print node/edge counts.
2. Load from a local content dir (`FileSystemSource`) and list all nodes of `entityType: 'person'`.
3. Traverse: from a node id, walk `reports-to` edges to print an org chain.
4. Query: find every node whose content mentions X, emit ids + titles as JSON.
5. Mutate/emit: register a one-off inline provider (via `defineProvider`) adding synthetic nodes, rebuild, and write `json-ld` output.
6. Subgraph pack: `subgraph(g, [anchor], {hops: 2})` → llm-context render with a token budget.
7. Diff two builds: load twice (two manifests), diff node id sets.
8. Cache: same load twice with the sqlite store, show second run hits fingerprints.

## Acceptance

- Each recipe runs verbatim with `node recipe-N.mjs` against a fixture KB checked into the engine repo (CI job executes all recipes).
- `query.ts` helpers are pure (graph in → data out), fully unit-tested, and re-exported from the package root.
- README documents the API surface above; TypeDoc or hand-written API reference published in-repo.

## Verify

```
# engine repo
npm test -- query
node docs/recipes/01-load-count.mjs   # ... through 08
```

Blocked by: the module-move task (#472); FileSystemSource can develop in parallel with #473
Blocks: anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#226, `kbx explore` (anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli — see epic #463 sub-issues)

issues.body:
Parent: #463 (engine-extraction epic).

## What

1. Add `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine@^0.1` as a dependency (npm; git pin acceptable only pre-release).
2. Replace moved module bodies under `src/engine/` with re-exports from the package (mirroring how `src/types/index.ts` re-exports core), then progressively update importers to import the package directly and delete the shims. `src/engine/index.ts`'s barrel becomes package re-exports; rendering exports were already removed by #466.

npm install

issues.title: Node-compatible sqlite store: load sql.js wasm without Vite ?url imports
issues.body:
Parent: #463 (engine-extraction epic).

## Problem

`src/engine/store/sqlite-runtime.ts:3` does `import wasmUrl from 'sql.js/dist/sql-wasm.wasm?url'` — a Vite-only asset import. Under plain Node (the CLI's runtime, anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#226) this specifier cannot resolve. This is the last platform coupling inside the store.

## Design

Make wasm location an injectable concern with sane per-runtime defaults:

1. `initSqlJs` accepts `locateFile`. Change `sqlite-runtime.ts` to accept an optional `{ locateFile?: (file: string) => string }` (or `wasmPath?: string`) through the store config (`store/config.ts`, already env-injected per #469).
2. Defaults:
   - **Node**: resolve `sql.js/dist/sql-wasm.wasm` via `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve(...)` inside a `./store/node` helper or lazy dynamic import guarded by `typeof process !== 'undefined'` — keep the node-only bits in a separate module so bundlers can tree-shake.
   - **Browser/Vite (template)**: the template app passes its own `?url`-derived path from app code — the Vite-specific import moves OUT of the engine package into the template's composition root.
3. Add a Node vitest that round-trips the store: init → persist provider results → fingerprint check → reload, in `environment: 'node'` with no Vite.

## Acceptance

- `kbexplorer-engine` contains zero `?url` imports; boundary test exemption removed.
- Store tests pass under plain Node 20 and 22.
- Template still uses the sqlite cache in the browser with no behavior change (`npm test`, store tests green).

## Verify

```
# engine repo
npm test -- store
node --version   # run suite on 20 and 22 in CI
# template
npm test && npm run build
```

Blocked by: the module-move task in this epic (store code must live in the engine repo first; the interface change can be prototyped in-template earlier)
Blocks: anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#226 step 4 (CLI caching)

issues.title: Move src/engine modules into kbexplorer-engine per the disposition table
issues.body:
Parent: #463 (engine-extraction epic). The authoritative module-by-module disposition table lives in the #463 epic body — this task executes its MOVE column.

## Moves (template `src/engine/` → `kbexplorer-engine/src/`)

**Pipeline core:** `loader.ts` (minus app wrappers, per #469), `orchestrator.ts`, `transforms.ts`, `graph.ts`, `parser.ts`, `identity.ts`, `access.ts` (thin re-export of core after anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#68), `safe-markdown.ts` (marked + sanitize-html — Node-safe), `source-edit.ts`, `plugin-loader.ts`, `structured-content.ts` (env-injected per #469), `node-map.ts`/`nodemap.ts` (respect PR #464's structured-node-map rename), `glob.ts` if present.

**Providers:** `providers.ts` (ProviderRegistry) + all of `providers/` — work, authored, authored-rich-markdown, content-model, files, person, structural (post-#467, viewer-name-only), wikipedia, orgchart, `rich-markdown/` (detect + shims), `examples/glossary-provider.ts`.

**Content model:** `content-model/` — builder, schema-reader, types, index, register (post-#467: type registration only, zero React).

**Node types:** `node-types/` (registry + index).

**Sources:** `sources/` — `repo-data.ts`, `manifest-source.ts`, `github-api-source.ts` (post-#469, theme-free).

**Store:** `store/` — config (env-injected), fingerprint, sqlite-graph-store, store-orchestrator, sqlite-runtime (wasm loading reworked by the Node-store sibling task).

**Tests:** every `__tests__` directory and fixture above moves alongside; template keeps only tests for what stays.

**Stays in template (do NOT move):** `src/representation/graph-canvas/` (nodeRenderer, createGraphNetwork, labelLayout, reports-to-layout — post-#466), `demo-entities.ts` (app demo content, post-#467), the thin `loadLocalKnowledgeBase`/`loadRemoteKnowledgeBase` env+theme wrappers (post-#469), all React viewers/theme/views.

## Method

- Move in dependency-ordered slices (parser/identity → providers → orchestrator/loader → sources → store), each slice landing with its tests green in the engine repo, so review stays tractable.
- Preserve git history where practical (subtree/filter-repo or plain copies with a manifest of provenance in the PR description).
- The template keeps compiling throughout by pointing `src/engine/*` shims at the package (full swap is the "template consumes the package" sibling task).

## Acceptance

- All listed modules + tests live in `kbexplorer-engine`, its suite green under plain Node (`vitest run`, node environment).
- Engine repo boundary test green (no react/vis-network/DOM/`import.meta.env`).

## Verify

```

npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm test
```

issues.title: Scaffold @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine: dual browser/Node package (tsup, vitest)
issues.body:
Parent: #463 (engine-extraction epic).

## What

Stand up the new repo `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine`, following the proven sibling patterns (`kbexplorer-core` for tooling, `kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown` for the "standalone package + thin template adapter" extraction playbook).

1. **Repo + package**: `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine`, version `0.1.0`, MIT, same branch-protection/issue-first conventions as the org.
2. **Build**: `tsup` → ESM + CJS + `.d.ts`. Exports map:
   ```jsonc
   {
     ".":          "pure engine: loadKnowledgeBase, orchestrator, transforms, buildGraph, providers, node-types, content-model, identity, parser, query helpers",
     "./sources":  "ManifestSource, GitHubApiSource, RepoSource type (isomorphic fetch only)",
     "./store":    "sqlite provider-result store (sql.js) — separate entry so consumers that skip caching don't pay for the wasm"
   }
   ```
   No top-level `browser`/`node` forks unless the store forces one (see the Node-store task) — the engine body must be runtime-agnostic by construction.
3. **Dependencies**: `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core@^0.5` (npm — blocked on anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#67), `yaml`, `marked`, `sanitize-html`, `sql.js`, `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown` (for the rich-markdown provider adapter). Explicitly forbidden: `react`, `react-dom`, `vis-network`, `vis-data`, anything DOM-touching.
4. **Engines**: `node >=20` (library floor per the engines policy in anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#69).
5. **Tests**: vitest, with **two** test environments in CI: `environment: 'node'` (default) and one jsdom smoke run, proving isomorphism.
6. **Boundary guard from day one**: port the template's static import-scan test — no file may import react/vis-network/DOM globals; no `import.meta.env`; document the single sqlite-wasm exemption until the Node-store task lands.
7. CI: build + typecheck + test on Node 20 and 22.

## Acceptance

- Empty-but-building package: `npm run build && npm test` green, `npm pack` produces a consumable tarball, `node -e "import('@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine')"` works from a scratch dir.

issues.title: Two-way boundary enforcement: engine must not import views/components/representation/theme/React/vis-network
issues.body:
Parent: #465 (P0 cycle-break epic). Locks in the cycle break so it can never regress before or after extraction (#463).

## Problem

The existing guards are one-directional only:
- `src/representation/targets/__tests__/no-engine-import.test.ts` — representation targets → engine
- `src/types/__tests__/no-engine-import.test.ts` — types → engine

Nothing prevents engine → representation/views/React. Every edge this epic cut can silently come back.

## What

Add `src/engine/__tests__/boundary.test.ts`, mirroring the static-scan technique of the existing `no-engine-import.test.ts` (walk files, parse import specifiers, assert none resolve into forbidden trees). Rules:

1. **Engine → app (forbidden):** no file under `src/engine/**` (excluding `__tests__`) may import from `src/representation/**`, `src/views/**`, `src/components/**`, `src/theme/**`, or the bare specifiers `react`, `react-dom`, `vis-network`, `vis-data`.
2. **Engine → platform (forbidden):** no file under `src/engine/**` may contain the token `import.meta.env` (post-#469) or a `?url`/`?raw` Vite import suffix (single allowed exemption: the sqlite wasm shim module, explicitly listed in the test with a comment pointing at #463's Node-store task, until that task removes it).
3. **Representation → engine (extend existing):** broaden the existing representation-side guard from targets-only to all of `src/representation/**` (keeping the documented `spa.tsx` exemption only if #468 proves it still necessary — prefer zero exemptions).

Keep the allow/deny lists as explicit arrays at the top of the test so future exemptions are visible in review.

Optionally also add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` / `import/no-restricted-paths` zone config in `eslint.config.*` for editor-time feedback — the vitest static scan remains the authoritative gate.

## Acceptance

- Test fails if anyone re-adds any of the removed imports (verify by temporarily re-adding one and watching it fail).
- CI green with no exemptions beyond the documented sqlite-wasm one.

## Verify

```
npm test -- src/engine/__tests__/boundary.test.ts
npm test
npm run lint
```

issues.title: Inject env config and hoist theme merging out of engine loaders/sources
issues.body:
Parent: #465 (P0 cycle-break epic). Cuts cycle edge 5 (engine → Vite platform + app theme).

## Problem

Engine files reach into the Vite app platform, which breaks under plain Node (a hard blocker for #463's dual browser/Node package):

| File | Coupling |
|------|----------|
| `src/engine/local-loader.ts:113` | reads `import.meta.env.VITE_KB_LOCAL` directly |
| `src/engine/structured-content.ts:37,51` | `env: EnvLike = import.meta.env` default parameter |
| `src/engine/store/config.ts:8,20` | `env = import.meta.env` default parameter |
| `src/engine/local-loader.ts:24` | imports `mergeExternalTheme`, `parseExternalTheme` from `../theme/externalTheme` |
| `src/engine/sources/github-api-source.ts:40` | imports `applyExternalThemeFile` from `../../theme/externalTheme` |
| `src/engine/store/sqlite-runtime.ts:3` | `import wasmUrl from 'sql.js/dist/sql-wasm.wasm?url'` — Vite-only specifier (full Node fix tracked under #463's store task; here just isolate it behind one module boundary) |

## Design

1. **Env injection.** Define `interface EngineEnv { [key: string]: string | boolean | undefined }` in one place (e.g. `src/engine/env.ts`). Every function that today defaults to `import.meta.env` takes an explicit `env` argument threaded from the composition root; the *app* passes `import.meta.env` where it constructs the loader/store. Remove all `import.meta.env` literals from `src/engine/**` (they may remain in app-side wrapper code).
2. **Theme hoisting.** Theme merge is a representation concern. Give `loadKnowledgeBase`/the loaders an optional post-load hook (e.g. `hooks?: { onRepoData?(data: RepoData): RepoData }` or a returned raw theme file the app applies). Concretely: `local-loader.ts` and `github-api-source.ts` stop importing `theme/externalTheme`; instead they surface the external-theme file content (it is just a retrieved resource) and the app-side wrapper (`src/` composition root or a thin `src/theme/apply-external.ts`) calls `mergeExternalTheme`/`applyExternalThemeFile`.
3. Loader split: keep thin app wrappers `loadLocalKnowledgeBase`/`loadRemoteKnowledgeBase` that read `import.meta.env`, apply theme, and delegate to the pure engine entry point.

## Acceptance

- `grep -rn "import.meta.env" src/engine --include='*.ts'` → zero hits
- `grep -rn "theme/" src/engine --include='*.ts'` → zero hits
- Local mode (`VITE_KB_LOCAL=true`) and remote mode boot identically; external theme still applies (existing theme tests + `src/representation/__tests__/theme-colors.test.ts` green).

## Verify

```
npm test
npx tsc -b
npm run lint
npm run build && npm run build:local
```

issues.title: Move node-layer/type lookups onto graph data; representation stops importing engine/node-types/registry
issues.body:
Parent: #465 (P0 cycle-break epic). Cuts cycle edge 3.

## Problem

`src/representation/graph-layers.ts:9` imports `resolveNodeLayer` from `../engine/node-types/registry` — a live engine registry lookup at render time. After extraction (#463) the registry lives in another package and representation must consume **pure graph data only** (the invariant `no-engine-import.test.ts` already enforces for json-ld/llm-context targets).

## Design

1. The engine stamps the resolved layer onto each node at build time: in `buildGraph()` (`src/engine/graph.ts`) or a final orchestrator step (`src/engine/orchestrator.ts`), set `node.layer = resolveNodeLayer(node)` for every node. Resolution semantics unchanged (entityType first, then source.type, fallback 'file').
2. Add the field to the data contract: `KBNode.layer?: 'file' | 'content' | 'work'` (confirm the exact `NodeLayer` union from `src/representation/styles.ts`). This is an **additive** change to `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` `src/graph.ts` — coordinate with the One-contract epic in kbexplorer-core; until core ships it, extend locally via the template's type re-export layer (`src/types/index.ts`).
3. `src/representation/graph-layers.ts`: `getNodeLayer(node)` becomes `return node.layer ?? 'file'` — delete the registry import.
4. Audit other representation/app files for `node-types/registry` imports (`grep -rn "node-types" src/representation src/views src/components`) and convert them the same way.
5. Keep the registry itself inside `src/engine/node-types/` — it moves to the engine package later; only its *consumption from representation* is removed.

## Acceptance

- Golden fixtures: `layer` now appears in serialized output — regenerate goldens via `npm run golden:update` in the same PR and review the diff (should be strictly additive `layer` fields).

issues.title: Invert viewer registration: providers declare viewer names; the app maps names → React components
issues.body:
Parent: #465 (P0 cycle-break epic). Cuts cycle edge 4 (engine → React .tsx components).

## Problem

Engine code imports React components and calls `registerViewer()` directly:

- `src/engine/providers/structural-provider.ts:23-25` — imports `registerViewer`, `WorkflowView`, `ActionView` from `../../views/viewers/*`
- `src/engine/content-model/register.ts:13-20` — imports `registerViewer` + `PersonView`, `SquadView`, `WorkstreamView`, `MissionView`, `PriorityView`, `CycleView`, `OrgView`
- `src/engine/demo-entities.ts:15-18` — imports `registerViewer`, `PersonView`, `SquadView`, and `buildSampleRichMarkdownNode` from `../views/rich-markdown/sample-document`

The viewer registry (`src/views/viewers/index.ts`) is already keyed by string name (`registerViewer('person', PersonView)`), so the inversion is purely about **who calls it**.

## Design

1. Providers/engine emit only a viewer NAME string. Where engine code today calls `registerViewer('x', XView)`, it instead records `viewer: 'x'` in the node-type registration (`src/engine/node-types/registry.ts` — add an optional `viewer?: string` field to the registered type descriptor) and/or on node data.
2. The app shell owns the name → component map. Create `src/views/viewers/builtin-map.ts` exporting a single `registerBuiltinViewers()` that performs every `registerViewer('workflow', WorkflowView)` etc. call currently scattered in engine code (names: workflow, action, person, squad, workstream, mission, priority, cycle, org — confirm exact keys from the current calls). Call it once from the app composition root (where the SPA boots, e.g. `src/main.tsx` or the spa target setup).
3. `src/engine/demo-entities.ts`: the demo *data* (including the rich-markdown sample node) is app demo content — either move demo-entities.ts out of `src/engine/` entirely (preferred; it is not engine logic) or strip its viewer/sample-document imports and inject the sample node from the app.
4. Resolution stays as-is: representation-side components call `resolveViewer(name)`; unresolved names fall back to `GenericStructuredView`.

## Acceptance

- `grep -rn "views/" src/engine --include='*.ts' | grep -v __tests__` → zero hits
- `grep -rn "registerViewer" src/engine` → zero hits
- Every entity type renders with the same viewer as before (spot-check person/squad/workflow nodes in the SPA; existing viewer tests green).

## Verify

```

npx tsc -b
npm run lint
```

issues.title: P0 Epic: Break the engine↔representation cycle
issues.body:
## Why P0

`src/engine/` and the representation/app side import each other, so the engine cannot be extracted (#463) until every cycle edge is cut. These edges are **verified in code today**:

| # | Edge | Evidence |
|---|------|----------|
| 1 | engine → representation | `src/engine/createGraphNetwork.ts:14-15` imports `../representation/views` (GraphLayoutMode) and `../representation/styles` (getEdgeStyle, resolveStyleColor, emphasisEdgeStyle) |
| 2 | representation → engine | `src/representation/views.ts:9` imports `../engine/reports-to-layout` (projectReportsToTree) |
| 3 | representation → engine | `src/representation/graph-layers.ts:9` imports `../engine/node-types/registry` (resolveNodeLayer) |
| 4 | engine → React views | `registerViewer(...)` + direct `.tsx` component imports in `src/engine/providers/structural-provider.ts:23-25`, `src/engine/content-model/register.ts:13-20`, `src/engine/demo-entities.ts:15-18` |
| 5 | engine → app platform | `import.meta.env` in `src/engine/local-loader.ts:113`, `src/engine/structured-content.ts:37,51`, `src/engine/store/config.ts:8,20`; `../theme/externalTheme` imports in `src/engine/local-loader.ts:24` and `src/engine/sources/github-api-source.ts:40` |

Rendering-flavored files misfiled under `src/engine/` (vis-network/DOM-coupled — they stay with the template, NOT the future engine package): `nodeRenderer.ts` (2,956 LOC), `createGraphNetwork.ts` (876), `labelLayout.ts` (154), `reports-to-layout.ts` (202).

The existing guard (`src/representation/targets/__tests__/no-engine-import.test.ts`) only checks representation targets → engine. Nothing guards engine → views/representation; this epic adds the reverse guard.

## Sub-issues

Tracked as native sub-issues of this epic:
1. Move rendering-coupled modules out of `src/engine/` (cuts edges 1 and 2)
2. Invert viewer registration to name-based (cuts edge 4)
3. Move node-layer lookups onto graph data (cuts edge 3)
4. Inject env + hoist theme merge out of engine loaders/sources (cuts edge 5)
5. Two-way boundary enforcement test (locks it all in)

issues.title: Epic: Extract src/engine into a standalone Node-safe @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine package
issues.body:
## Problem

`src/engine/` (~13,000 LOC: sources/, 9 providers, sqlite store via sql.js, orchestrator, loader, transforms, node-types, content-model) is the only real graph-orchestration implementation in the kbx ecosystem, yet it is trapped inside a Vite/React app. Consequences, all verified:

- **kbexplorer-cli cannot depend on it** and hand-rolled a parallel pipeline: `src/lib/graph-builder.js` (182 LOC, self-described "lightweight… the full graph is built by the template's engine in the browser"), `src/lib/graph.js` (346 LOC — a **second** independent CLI graph loader feeding the MCP/affordances layer), `frontmatter.js` (187, third duplicate in `commands/links.js` — cli#227), `manifest.js` (568, a diverged fork of this repo's `scripts/generate-manifest.js`, 785), `content-model.js` (525, parallels `src/engine/content-model/`), `precedence.js` (212), `access-label.js` (270).
- **Semantic search silently indexes a different graph than the SPA renders**: `kbx search-index` builds via `graph-builder.js` (content/*.md only — none of the engine providers' nodes), while the SPA's lexical index (`src/search/useSearchIndex.ts`) is built over the FULL engine graph. Three parallel graph builders, two different search corpora. Tracked: anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#230.
- The CLI barely uses core (only `buildEdgeId`, `mapRelation`, `formatContentHash`) — the real engine is simply unreachable from Node.
- This repo's own `scripts/` (18 scripts, ~4,915 LOC) reimplement pipeline pieces a `kbx` backed by the engine should own.

Some kbx users will never run a web-hosted instance; a fully offline Node engine is a first-class requirement.

## The cycle that blocks extraction (P0 — epic #465)

The engine and the representation/app side import each other. Verified edges: `engine/createGraphNetwork.ts:14-15` → `representation/{views,styles}`; `representation/views.ts:9` → `engine/reports-to-layout`; `representation/graph-layers.ts:9` → `engine/node-types/registry`; `registerViewer()` + React `.tsx` imports in `engine/providers/structural-provider.ts`, `engine/content-model/register.ts`, `engine/demo-entities.ts`; `import.meta.env` + `theme/externalTheme` couplings in `local-loader.ts`, `structured-content.ts`, `store/config.ts`, `sources/github-api-source.ts`. **Epic #465 (sub-issues #466–#470) must close before module moves start.**

> **Correction to the earlier investigation in this issue's history:** `labelLayout.ts` (154 LOC) and `reports-to-layout.ts` (202 LOC) were classified PURE_NODE_SAFE. They are pure *computationally*, but they are rendering-layout concerns consumed only by the canvas/views — they STAY with the template's representation layer (moved to `src/representation/graph-canvas/` by #466), alongside `nodeRenderer.ts` (2,956) and `createGraphNetwork.ts` (876). The portable engine ships **zero** layout/rendering code.

## Disposition table (authoritative)

| Module(s) | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `loader.ts`, `orchestrator.ts`, `transforms.ts`, `graph.ts`, `parser.ts` (726), `identity.ts`, `safe-markdown.ts` (marked+sanitize-html, Node-safe), `source-edit.ts`, `plugin-loader.ts`, `structured-content.ts`, `node-map.ts`/`nodemap.ts` (post-PR #464 rename), `remote-loader.ts` (source construction only) | **MOVE** → `kbexplorer-engine` |
| `providers.ts` + `providers/**` (work, authored, authored-rich-markdown, content-model, files, person, structural†, wikipedia, orgchart, rich-markdown detect+shims, examples/glossary) | **MOVE** († after #467 strips viewer imports) |
| `content-model/**` (builder, schema-reader, types, register†) | **MOVE** († after #467) |
| `node-types/**` (registry) | **MOVE** (layer resolution stamped onto node data at build — #468) |
| `sources/**` (repo-data, manifest-source, github-api-source†) | **MOVE** († after #469 theme hoist) |
| `store/**` (config†, fingerprint, sqlite-graph-store, store-orchestrator, sqlite-runtime‡) | **MOVE** († env-injected #469; ‡ wasm loading reworked for Node, #473) |
| `access.ts` | **MOVE as thin re-export** — canonical policy hoists to core (anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#68) |
| `nodeRenderer.ts`, `createGraphNetwork.ts`, `labelLayout.ts`, `reports-to-layout.ts` | **STAY** → `src/representation/graph-canvas/` (#466) |
| `demo-entities.ts`, viewer name→component map, theme merge hooks, `loadLocal/RemoteKnowledgeBase` env wrappers | **STAY** in template (app shell) |
| cli `graph-builder.js` + `graph.js` (both parallel graph builders), `frontmatter.js`, `manifest.js`, `content-model.js`, `precedence.js` dup logic, `access-label.js` dup logic | **DELETE** after cli adopts the engine (cli#226, cli#227, cli#230) |
| template `scripts/generate-manifest.js` + pipeline scripts | **DELETE/THIN** → kbx wrappers (#476) |

## Package design

`@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine` — new sibling repo; tsup → ESM+CJS+d.ts; vitest run in both node and jsdom environments; engines `node >=20`; deps: `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core@^0.5` (npm — core#67), `yaml`, `marked`, `sanitize-html`, `sql.js`, `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown`. Forbidden by a day-one boundary test: react, react-dom, vis-network, vis-data, DOM globals, `import.meta.env`.

Exports map: `.` (loadKnowledgeBase, orchestrator/transforms/buildGraph, ProviderRegistry, providers, node-types, content-model, identity, parser, **new pure query helpers** — getNode/findNodes/neighbors/related/subgraph/shortestPath), `./sources` (ManifestSource, GitHubApiSource, **new Node-only FileSystemSource**), `./store` (sqlite store, wasm path injectable).

Scriptable API (north star — a coding agent writes 5–10 line scripts: load → query → traverse → mutate/emit):

```ts
import { loadKnowledgeBase, findNodes, subgraph } from '@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine';
import { FileSystemSource } from '@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-engine/sources';
const graph = await loadKnowledgeBase(config, { source: new FileSystemSource('./content') });
const people = findNodes(graph, n => n.entityType === 'person');
```

Promise-based throughout; all I/O behind injected `source`/`env`/`store`. Eight runnable recipes ship in the engine repo's docs (#475).

North-star consumers, explicitly: the template SPA, agent-authored scripts, `kbx explore` (cli#229), **`kbx search-index` + the CLI affordances layer** (cli#230 — semantic search index and SPA lexical index must be built from the SAME `KBGraph`, or a documented projection of it, with a drift check).

Viewer inversion contract: providers declare viewer **names** in node data / node-type registrations; the app shell maps names → React components (#467). Boundary enforced **both directions** by static tests (#470 here, mirrored in the engine repo).

## Sub-issues (native)

Phase order: #471 scaffold → #472 module moves → #473 Node store → #474 template consumes → #475 scriptable API/recipes → cli#226 adoption → cli#230 search/affordances on the real graph → cli#229 `kbx explore` → #476 scripts become kbx wrappers.

*(Native blocked-by relations are not exposed by the tooling used here; these Blocked-by/Blocks body lines are the source of truth.)*

issues.title: Feature: copilot/AnchorFirst surface should honor node.display (code/diagram/rich-markdown/table), not fall back to GenericStructuredView
issues.body:
The `copilot` target's `AnchorFirstView` renders node content via `resolveViewer()` (keyed by `entityType`/`@type`) — a **separate pipeline** from `ReadingView`'s `node.display` switch (`code`/`diagram`/`rich-markdown`/`table`) that the `spa` target uses. So display-mode nodes (e.g. a `display: rich-markdown` doc, or a Mermaid `display: diagram` node) fall back to `GenericStructuredView`'s generic key/value dump inside the **copilot canvas surface**, instead of rendering as prose/diagram the way the SPA does.

Flagged honestly (out-of-scope-there) in the shell PR #454 (#412); also recorded as a symptom in the post-mortem #445 ("AnchorFirstView's fallback renders node.data/JSON-LD, not prose — a plain authored/prose node anchored in a conversation can render as 'No structured data' instead of its actual content"). This issue is the actionable fix.

### Grounding (file:line)
- `src/representation/targets/copilot-home/AnchorFirstView.tsx` — the `resolveViewer()` path.
- `src/views/ReadingView.tsx:339-389` — the live `node.display` switch (incl. inline Mermaid) the copilot surface does NOT reuse.
- `src/views/viewers/registry.ts:4-61` (registry) + `GenericStructuredView` (`:98-136`) — the generic fallback that wins today.

### Acceptance
- A node with `display: rich-markdown` (and one with `display: diagram`) anchored in the copilot surface renders as rich content / SVG diagram, matching `ReadingView` — not a key/value dump.
- e2e assertion in the copilot surface (not just a unit test on the registry).

Part of #426 (embedded-block rendering + lenses). Refs: flagged in #454; symptom in #445.

issues.title: Bug: per-retrieval affordances are computed by Sources but never reach the render path (blocks #411)
issues.body:
## Summary

The core **Source / Resource / Affordance** contract is fully implemented and unit-tested on both `Source` implementations, but **the graph-loading path never consumes it** — it loads via `source.getRepoData()` + providers, not `source.retrieve()`. As a result, the per-retrieval affordances that Sources compute (`read` / `comment` / `close` / `merge`, `staging-area` links) **never reach `KBNode`s or the viewers**, and `KBNode` has no field to hold them anyway.

This is the same *shape* of defect the post-mortem already recorded for access labels in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#49` ("computed on nodes… but nothing reads it before rendering") — a core contract that is built + tested but not adopted by its real consumer. It was simply missing from the ledger. **This blocks #411** (affordance-aware node launchpad): there is no real affordance data to render today.

## Evidence (verified `file:line`)

**Affordances ARE implemented and tested:**
- `ManifestSource.retrieve()` → `affordances: ['read']` — `src/engine/sources/manifest-source.ts:92,102`
- `GitHubApiSource.retrieve()` → real per-retrieval affordances: worktree `['read','write','stage']` (`github-api-source.ts:195`), staging-area link (`:199`), issue `['read','comment','close']` (`:230`), pull-request `['read','comment','close','merge']` (`:241`), release `['read']` (`:252`)
- Unit tests assert them — `src/engine/__tests__/sources.test.ts:38,45-46,75-76,97`
- Both Sources are instantiated by the app: `new ManifestSource(...)` (`src/engine/local-loader.ts:343`), `new GitHubApiSource(...)` (`src/engine/remote-loader.ts:28`)

**…but the render path never consumes that surface:**
- `loadKnowledgeBase(source, config)` builds the `KBGraph` from **`source.getRepoData()`** via the `ProviderRegistry` — `src/engine/loader.ts:97,99-130`. It **never calls `source.retrieve()`**.
- The only callers of `retrieve()` are the source's own internal `get()` and the tests — no user-facing/render path.
- `KBNode` has no `affordances`/`links` field — `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` `src/graph.ts:202`+ (fields: `id, title, cluster, content, rawContent, …, identity?`). `affordances`/`links` live only on `Resource` — core `src/source.ts:66,71`.
- Representation targets only *read* the pure `KBGraph` (grep-confirmed zero node-field mutation in `src/representation/`, per #445), so affordances must be carried onto the node/graph **at load time** to be renderable by any target (spa / json-ld / llm-context / copilot).

**CLI/canvas path is the same story:** the loopback `/manifest` serves raw `authoredContent` strings (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` `src/lib/manifest.js:548`); the CLI never calls core `retrieve()` either.

## Impact

- **#411** has no per-retrieval affordance data to render. Any launchpad built today would be rendering hardcoded/synthesized data, not real affordances — which is precisely the failure mode #411's acceptance criteria try to forbid.
- More broadly: the Phase-4 Source/Resource/Affordance investment (#318, #319, #320, #322; core `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#5`) is currently inert from the user's perspective.

## Remediation direction (not prescribing the final design)

One of:
- **(a) Carry it at load time** — have the loader/providers thread each node's per-retrieval `affordances` + `links` onto the `KBGraph`. Requires an additive optional field on core `KBNode` (its own `kbexplorer-core` issue, issue-first) — and note that lands inside the core-contract audit in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#49`.
- **(b) Fetch live** — expose affordances via a loopback endpoint the canvas queries on demand (works only behind the CLI server, honors the situational nature).

Decide (a) vs (b) before building #411's rendering.

## Related

- Built the (now-unconsumed) surface: #318, #319, #320, #322, `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#5`
- Sibling "core contract built but unadopted" findings: `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#49` (access/redaction unenforced; identity-addressing unadopted), #445
- Umbrella post-mortem: `anokye-labs/kbexplorer#102`
- Blocks: #411 (epic #407)

issues.title: Bug: copilot canvas's Constellation zoom-out is the decorative hero, not an explorable graph
issues.body:
## What's wrong

The `copilot` Representation target's `/constellation` route (the zoom-out from the anchor-first home view, #408) renders `HomePage`:

```tsx
// src/representation/targets/copilot.tsx
<Route path="/constellation" element={<HomePage graph={graph} config={config} />} />
```

`HomePage` is the **SPA's landing hero**, not an explorable constellation. Its only graph visual is `ConstellationHero` - a decorative band fixed at `height: '35vh'` with physics disabled after a single `fit()` call (`network.setOptions({ physics: { enabled: false } })`, `src/components/ConstellationHero.tsx`). It has no `interactive: true`, so no drag-pan / scroll-zoom, and its only click affordances are "Explore the Graph" / "Start Exploring" buttons that just navigate to `#/node/readme` - they don't select nodes in the graph itself.

The **real** explorable force-directed network (drag-pan, scroll-zoom, click-to-select) only exists inside `HUD.tsx` (the minimap + its expanded-map overlay). The embeddable canvas mount (#406) deliberately strips the HUD to stay headless, so inside the `copilot` target there is currently **no route that renders an actual interactive constellation**. Clicking "Constellation" from the anchor-first view gets a cramped, non-interactive band - not the zoom-out the anchor-first view's own doc comment promises ("the constellation is demoted to an optional zoom-out").

## Expected

`/constellation` in the `copilot` target should render a full-viewport, interactive force-directed graph - reusing the same `createGraphNetwork` engine helper the HUD uses, mounted with `interactive: true`, and with node clicks re-anchoring the panel (`navigate('/node/<id>')`) rather than doing nothing / just linking to a fixed node.

## Verified fix (built and confirmed working)

A `ConstellationView` component (~94 lines) that:
- Mounts `createGraphNetwork({ container, graph, isDark, interactive: true, fitOnStabilize: true, onNodeClick: (id) => navigate(''/node/''+id), auditSlot: ''copilotConstellation'' })` full-bleed (`position: absolute; inset: 0`).
- Renders a thin header bar ("<- Back", node/edge counts) matching the anchor-first view's chrome.
- Swaps the one route in `copilot.tsx`:
  ```diff
  -<Route path="/constellation" element={<HomePage graph={graph} config={config} />} />
  +<Route path="/constellation" element={<ConstellationView graph={graph} config={config} />} />
  ```

Verified via a headless Playwright probe against a local build: canvas grows from the hero's fixed 280px to the full panel size (900x700 in the probe), header reads real node/edge counts (e.g. "172 nodes . 640 links . click a node to open it"), clicking a node navigates to `/node/<id>`, zero console errors.

## Scope
- Additive: only the `/constellation` route element changes; `HomePage`/`ConstellationHero` (still used by the full-page SPA landing) are untouched.
- Add a Playwright assertion that `/constellation` renders a full-size interactive network (not the fixed-height hero) - e.g. assert canvas height tracks the viewport, not a fixed `35vh`-derived pixel value.

issues.title: Run `tsc -b` in PR CI and make test + typecheck required checks
issues.body:
## Problem
Pages/PR CI runs `npm test` (vitest) + `npx vite build`, but never `tsc -b` — so `npm run build` can be broken while CI is green (this is exactly how PR #443 broke `main` and the breakage shipped in the v0.4.0 tag). The branch-protection ruleset requires only `dependency-review` / `check-linked-issue` / `pr-title`; neither tests nor typecheck are required to merge.

## Fix
1. Add `tsc -b` (or `npm run build`) to the PR CI workflow.
2. Make the test + typecheck checks **required** in the ruleset.

_From the 2026-07-01 ecosystem review (anokye-labs/kbexplorer#102)._

No fixed layout seed; a live UX bug that shipped until discovered incidentally while debugging unrelated CI flakiness. Already fixed by #419 — noted here to confirm the fix is on main and add a seed-stability test.

Titled as a trivial `@types/node` patch bump, but the merged diff rewrites HUD-collapse state, changes date-formatting logic in two engine files, and bumps a cache-invalidation constant — none disclosed in the title.

Search queries sent to a configurable `VITE_SEARCH_SERVICE_URL` with zero new test coverage; the PR's own body admits deduplication logic "couldn't be tested."

issues.title: Post-mortem detail: template findings (THE root identity-divergence matrix, dead cross-provider merge machinery, sanitization inconsistency, decorative constellation)
issues.body: ## Context One of four per-repo detail issues supporting anokye-labs/kbexplorer#102 (read first for the verified timeline + honest account). Self-contained. No fixes authorized yet. ## THE ROOT FINDING — AF-003: 5 divergent id/identity computation patterns across providers, feeding a dead cross-provider merge mechanism **Full matrix (11 sources, 4 distinct patterns):** - **(a) separate id + urn identity:** AuthoredProvider (bare slug id, `urn:content:`), FilesProvider (`urn:file:`), WorkProvider (`urn:issue:N`/`urn:pr:N`/etc), PersonProvider (`urn:person:`), StructuralProvider (`urn:structural:`). - **(b) COLLAPSED id===identity:** `AuthoredRichMarkdownProvider` (sourced from `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown` v0.1.0, `src/lib/rich-markdown.js:759-766`: `const node = { id: identity, ..., identity }`) AND, independently and natively, `content-model/builder.ts` (`emitNode` L258, `EdgeResolver.stub` L325, via `buildUrn()` in schema-reader.ts) — the SAME collapse, authored in-repo, removing any "third-party package" excuse. - **(c) missing entirely:** WikipediaProvider, OrgChartProvider, glossary-provider example (`assignIdentity()` has no case for `source.type:'external'`). - **(d) 5th variant:** rich-markdown demo fixture `sample-document.ts:139-153` sets `id` but omits `identity` entirely. **The bug is asserted-as-correct, not merely missed:** `authored-rich-markdown-provider.test.ts:73` — `expect(nodes[0].identity).toBe(nodes[0].id)`. Someone looked at this exact collapsed shape and wrote a passing test asserting it, at some point in this repo's history. **Root cause:** `assignIdentity()` (engine/identity.ts) has no case for content-model/rich-markdown/external source types, so those providers rolled their own ad hoc logic — because kbexplorer-core shipped a dedicated identity-addressing library (`buildAddress`/`buildPersonAddress`, a 3-PR epic) that this repo NEVER ADOPTED, building `engine/identity.ts` as a fully independent parallel reimplementation instead. Full detail in kbexplorer-core's companion issue. **Root-root cause — why nobody ever noticed:** the entire cross-provider identity-merge mechanism (`buildIdentityIndex`/`shareIdentity`, engine/identity.ts) is DEAD CODE — zero production callers, grep-confirmed, only its own unit test uses it. The ONE place that reads `.identity` for its documented purpose, `representation/graph-layers.ts` `filterGraphToLayer('content')` (wired into the LIVE, user-reachable "Docs" view in the HUD view switcher — not a hidden path), is structurally dead-on-arrival: exhaustively checked every identity-assignment site — file-sourced nodes ALWAYS get `urn:file:`, content nodes NEVER do, so the lookup can never hit in any real invocation. The ONE place a matching pair exists is a hand-crafted test fixture built to unit-test the pure function in isolation. The real file-tree deduplication users actually experience in that view comes from a completely different mechanism (`isContentTreeNode()`'s path-prefix check) — the identity-merge branch does nothing, anywhere it was ever wired up. **This reframes the remediation entirely:** the question is not "which shape should win" — it's whether cross-provider identity-linking is a real requirement at all, since the one place it was built for has never worked. If yes: unify on core's `buildAddress`, one shared helper every provider calls, with a real integration test. If no: delete `buildIdentityIndex`/`shareIdentity`/the graph-layers.ts merge branch and stop documenting `identity` as a cross-representation key. ## Other findings, most severe first ### HIGH — AF-010: Inconsistent internal sanitization standard across two comparable untrusted-markdown paths (proven executable, not theoretical) `structural-provider.ts:44-74` builds a dedicated defensive Marked instance (escapeHtml + DANGEROUS_URL_SCHEME guard) EXPLICITLY because its output reaches `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. `authored-rich-markdown-provider.ts:85` renders equally-untrusted repo content (any `.md` with `display: rich-markdown`) with the plain, unguarded `marked` import, which reaches `ReadingView.tsx:421` (`root.innerHTML = html`). Proven by executing the pinned `marked@18` on a payload — `onerror`/`onload`/`javascript:` all survive unescaped. Broadened scope: `parser.ts`, `work-provider.ts`, `person-provider.ts`, `local-loader.ts` ALL currently use the same unguarded `marked.parse` for repo/PR/issue-sourced content — the fix needs to be a shared renderer applied everywhere, not just the one path. Positive control: the SVG block-renderer path (mermaid/dot/ics/canvas) IS safe, confirmed via full trace — only ever ``, never innerHTML'd. ### HIGH — AF-019: No cross-provider id-collision detection; graph.ts internally disagrees with itself about collision resolution `orchestrator.ts` `collectProviderNodes` -> `graph.ts` `buildGraph` has ZERO cross-provider id-collision detection. `buildGraph` returns the raw concatenated `nodes` array (duplicates intact), while `buildEdges` internally resolves targets via `new Map(nodes.map(n=>[n.id,n]))` (last-write-wins) — a first-match-wins vs last-match-wins split brain the moment any two providers collide on an id. Only `StructuralProvider` + `demo-entities.ts` self-guard, and only within their own output. The one known cross-provider collision (Authored vs AuthoredRichMarkdown) was patched with a one-off skip-guard, not a systemic fix. ### HIGH — AF-023: Constellation zoom-out is decorative, not explorable (independently confirmed twice) Both `copilot.tsx`'s `/constellation` route and `AnchorFirstView`'s "Constellation" button resolve to `HomePage`, whose only graph visual (`heroCanvas`) is `createGraphNetwork({interactive:false, pointerEvents:none, opacity:0.35})` inside a 40-50vh hero strip — decorative background, not an explorable graph. Confirmed independently both by a live discovery this session (which produced an uncommitted local fix — a proper full-viewport interactive ConstellationView) and by this dedicated audit tracing the code path from scratch. ### HIGH — AF-026: Dual, disconnected JSON-LD builders in the ONE target whose entire job is emitting JSON-LD `StructuralProvider`/`ContentModelProvider` call core's `buildJsonLd()` to populate `node.jsonld` (full envelope incl. `ldProps` like `ruleCount`, `schemaVersion`, `nativeType`, `lifecycle`). The `json-ld` REPRESENTATION TARGET (`representation/targets/json-ld.ts` `buildGraphJsonLd`) calls `buildJsonLd()` AGAIN from scratch, only reads `node.jsonld?.['@type']` back out, never merges `ldProps`/`node.data`. Every custom LD property a provider computed is silently dropped from the actual exported document. Two fully-isolated, fully-tested contracts (`jsonld-contract.test.ts` vs `json-ld.test.ts`), zero integration test connecting them. ### MEDIUM — AF-011: 5th identity variant + overstated claims in docs/release-notes `sample-document.ts` omits identity entirely (5th pattern, see matrix above). Separately: `AnchorFirstView`'s fallback (`GenericStructuredView`) renders `node.data`/JSON-LD, not prose — a plain authored/prose node anchored in a conversation can render as "No structured data" instead of its actual content. `#444`'s release notes describe the canvas mount as "mounts the constellation" when `#443` made anchor-first the actual registered default by that same release's HEAD. ### MEDIUM — AF-020: Epic closed as "complete" while its own tracked sub-issue remains open Epic `#401` closed complete while sub-issue `#405` (full Fluent design-token surface) remains OPEN and the shipped host-theme adapter only covers typography/corner-radius, not density/spacing/stroke-width. ### LOW — AF-021, AF-022: known/dismissed review comments shipped anyway `#432` requires Node >=22 but GitHub Pages CI still runs Node 20 (a deferred review comment, never circled back). `#438` (constellation polish) shipped hard-coded pixel values in new legend rows; a Copilot review flagged this, was explicitly dismissed "to match adjacent rows," and merged anyway — this repo's own AGENTS.md has a "no pixels for sizing" rule that this reviewed-and-merged code violates. ### LOW / VERIFIED — positive controls Representation targets (spa/json-ld/llm-context/copilot) do not mutate the pure KBGraph — grep-confirmed zero node-field assignment in src/representation/. Canvas bootConfig parsing (#442) is clean — verified field-by-field, no prototype-pollution vector, no CSS-injection escalation. All 4 declared rich-markdown block kinds have registered renderers.
