issues.title: Hierarchy/DAG layout representation: force-directed constellation is the wrong view for tree-structured graphs
issues.body:
When the graph is **hierarchical** (a Program → Epic → Feature → Task tree, or any dependency DAG), the force-directed constellation dissolves the structure into a radial hairball: the parent/child spine is invisible because every edge is an equal-weight spring, and the 6 relation types all render at the same visual weight so structural edges don't dominate cross-cutting ones.

The kbexplorer thesis is **open representations per content shape**. A hierarchy/DAG wants a layout built for it, not the associative constellation.

### Proposal
Add a **layered tree/DAG layout** as a selectable representation (or a layout mode within the graph view), with:
- **Top-down layered placement** (e.g. Program → Epic → Feature → Task) using a DAG/Sugiyama-style layout.
- **Structural edges as the skeleton** (solid, weighted) with the other relation types dimmed/toggleable, so the spine reads first.
- **Labels that don't truncate** at the current level of detail.
- **Focus + collapse**: click a node to focus its subtree; collapse/expand branches instead of rendering all nodes at full strength.

### Why separate from #408
#408 makes the *canvas* default to an anchor-first neighbour view (still associative). This issue is about a **structural** layout for inherently hierarchical content — complementary, not the same.

### Acceptance
- A hierarchical/DAG graph renders top-down with a visible parent/child spine.
- Structural vs. cross-cutting relations are visually ranked.
- Subtree focus + branch collapse work.
- Selectable per graph/content shape (does not replace the constellation for associative graphs).

### Motivating artifact
The kbexplorer Epic→Feature→Task issue tree rendered as a constellation hairball on the live showcase (https://anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer/).

Relates to #39, #408, #147.

issues.title: Constellation rendering quality: node overlap, label collision/truncation, edges not clipped, no visual-identity legend
issues.body:
The force-directed constellation has visual-craft defects that show up even at very low node counts (detail slider at minimum, ~5 nodes), independent of layout/structure concerns. These make the view feel unpolished and hard to read.

### Observed (repro: on the live showcase https://anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer/, open the constellation, zoom in / lower the detail slider to minimum)
1. **Nodes overlap each other.** Collision/repulsion does not enforce a minimum gap, so node bodies physically stack even when only a handful are visible.
2. **Labels collide *and* truncate simultaneously.** Labels are placed at a fixed offset with no collision avoidance — adjacent labels overwrite each other (e.g. `kbexplore` / `kbexplor` / `Execution plan:…` piled together) while also being cut off. Worst of both: unreadable and ambiguous.
3. **Edges route straight through node bodies.** Edges are not clipped to the node border — a link passes behind/through the selected node instead of terminating at its edge.
4. **No legend for the visual identity.** Amber-outlined containers vs. glowing-blue selection vs. circular nodes encode meaning (container / selected / issue) with nothing telling the user what each shape/colour means.

### Acceptance
- Minimum inter-node spacing enforced; no body-on-body overlap at default zoom.
- Label placement avoids collisions (offset/anchor selection or hide-on-collide), and labels at the current zoom level are not truncated when space allows.
- Edges clip to node borders (no draw-through).
- A legend (or hover affordance) explains node shape/colour semantics; or the encoding is simplified so it's self-evident.

### Out of scope
Layout choice for hierarchical content — tracked separately (the "hierarchy/DAG layout" feature). This issue is purely rendering quality of the existing constellation.

**Environment:** live showcase (https://anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer/), vis-network constellation representation.

Relates to #39.

issues.title: Release v0.3.0 — rich-Markdown rendering + authored ingestion
issues.body: Cut `v0.3.0` carrying the rich-Markdown slice: rendering (#426/#427) + authored ingestion (#431/#432). The showcase (anokye-labs/kbexplorer#14) pins a template tag and needs this release to bump off `v0.2.0`. Bumps `package.json` 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0 + CHANGELOG.

issues.title: Authored rich-Markdown integration: ingest authored docs into rich-md nodes
issues.body:
## Problem

The merged rich-Markdown **rendering** (#427) detects + renders nodes carrying `node.data.richMarkdown.blocks`, but nothing in the engine turns an **authored** Markdown file into such a node. So the renderer never fires on real authored content — only via the `?demo=richmd` sample injection.

## Approach

Wire the published provider package `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown` (pin `#v0.1.0`) — specifically its **pure, browser-safe `./lib` `ingestRichMarkdown`** (no `fs`) — into the engine:

- Add the package as a template dependency (`github:…#v0.1.0`).
- New `AuthoredRichMarkdownProvider` + shared `isRichAuthoredMarkdown` predicate (opt-in via `display: rich-markdown` frontmatter) that runs `ingestRichMarkdown` over the inline `authoredContent` and **adapts** the package's block/node shape (`{lang,content,contentHash,span}`) to the template contract (`{kind,source,hash,range}`), sets `content = marked.parse(body)`, and keeps the core `buildAddress` identity.
- Skip-guard in `AuthoredProvider` so rich docs aren't double-emitted.
- Register in `loader.ts`; bump `CACHE_VERSION`.
- Browser shims for the package's `node:crypto`/`node:path` imports, aliased in `vite.config.ts` only (vitest keeps real builtins; `node:fs` is never bundled).
- Tests proving an authored doc with mermaid + dot blocks renders as a rich-md document (frontmatter facts, live mermaid, graceful fallback); existing authored/Mermaid/golden tests stay green.

Refs: anokye-labs/kbexplorer#14, anokye-labs/kbexplorer#93. Follows #427.

After merge the template needs a tagged release (next minor, e.g. `v0.3.0`) carrying both #427 and this, since the showcase pins a template tag.

issues.title: Task: Launch + document the search service (finalize Phase 7 search integration)
issues.body:
Relates to the master search epic `#344` and the Phase 7 backlog `#363`. System epic: `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search#5`.

## What

Close the last gap in the SPA search integration — make it possible to actually **run** the search service the app talks to, and document the wiring:
1. Add a dev script (or a documented one-liner) that starts the search server, e.g. `npx @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search serve --dir .search --port 7700` (now shipped — `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search#6`), or `kbx search-serve` once available (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`).
2. Document `VITE_SEARCH_SERVICE_URL` (default + how to point it at the local service) in the README and/or `.env.example`.
3. Verify `useSemanticSearch.ts`'s `{ query, limit, graphRanking: true }` → `{ results, suggestions }` round-trip against the real server — the server now honors `graphRanking` and returns `suggestions`.
4. Finalize Phase 7 (`#363`).

## Why

`useSemanticSearch.ts` + `SearchPalette.tsx` already exist and point at `VITE_SEARCH_SERVICE_URL`, but **nothing starts that server** and the env var is undocumented, so the feature can't be exercised end-to-end from a clean clone.

## Scope boundaries

- **In:** dev script + docs + end-to-end verification; closing `#363`.
- **Out:** building the search engine itself (lives in `kbexplorer-search`).

## Success definition

From a clean clone with checked-in `.search/` artifacts, a contributor can start the server and use the search palette against live, graph-ranked results following only the README.

## Related

- Master search epic: `#344`
- Phase 7 backlog: `#363`
- System epic: `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search#5`
- Service entrypoint shipped: `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search#6`

issues.title: Bug: preserve typed and directional parallel edges in graph builds
issues.body:
## What
Preserve multiple typed or directional relationships between the same two nodes when building graph edges.

## Why
`buildEdges()` currently deduplicates by an unordered pair of endpoint IDs, so the first edge between two nodes wins and later relationships are dropped even if they have a different relation, type, or direction. This loses graph semantics exactly where structured content is trying to express richer relationships.

## Scope
- Change edge identity/deduplication to include relation and direction where the contract treats them as meaningful.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and golden-output reviewability.
- Ensure related-neighbor ranking still behaves intentionally when multiple edges connect the same nodes.

## Acceptance
- Two nodes can be connected by more than one relationship when relation/type/direction differs.
- Opposite-direction relationships are not collapsed into one undirected edge unless explicitly modeled that way.
- Existing graph determinism tests or goldens are updated with reviewable diffs.

Relates to anokye-labs/kbexplorer#9.

issues.title: Feature: render fenced diagram blocks in ReadingView
issues.body:
## What
Render fenced `diagram` blocks in the reading view instead of showing the placeholder text and raw source only.

## Why
Authored knowledge often uses diagrams to explain architecture, flows, and relationships. The parser already classifies diagram blocks, but the renderer stops at "Diagram rendering coming soon", which makes authored content look broken during adoption.

## Scope
- Add a real renderer for supported diagram content, starting with Mermaid if that is the intended block language.
- Preserve raw-source fallback/error display for unsupported or invalid diagrams.
- Cover both local manifest and remote/runtime modes because this is a representation concern.

## Acceptance
- A fenced diagram block renders visually in `ReadingView`.
- Invalid diagrams fail visibly and retain source text for debugging.
- Existing code/table/tree/file-list block behavior is unchanged.

Relates to anokye-labs/kbexplorer#9.

issues.title: Feature: make structured-content directory configurable
issues.body:
## What
Allow repositories to configure the structured descriptor directory instead of requiring a top-level `content-model/` path.

## Why
The reader already accepts a directory-name parameter, but the build path does not expose a configuration surface. During adoption, this turns repository layout into a hidden hard requirement and makes otherwise-valid structured content invisible.

## Scope
- Add a documented config field for the structured content directory/path.
- Thread the configured value into manifest generation and content-model loading.
- Preserve the current `content-model/` default for backwards compatibility.
- Include validation or diagnostics when the configured path is missing.

## Acceptance
- A repo can place structured descriptors outside top-level `content-model/` and have them appear in the local manifest.
- Existing repos using `content-model/` continue to work unchanged.
- The setting is visible in docs/config examples and suitable for CLI validation.

Relates to anokye-labs/kbexplorer#9.

issues.title: Refresh stale visual baselines + reconcile the ocean theme in AGENTS.md
issues.body:
The DTU audit (#394) surfaced two related visual/theme follow-ups:

**P1 — Stale L5 visual-regression baselines.** `visual-regression.yml` (L5) fails on every nightly: all 64 surfaces in `review/baselines/` drift 2–6% against committed baselines. The drift is uniform across surfaces, indicating benign global rendering drift (font/anti-aliasing) as the UI evolved — not a single regression. The baselines need a deliberate refresh, captured on the ubuntu CI runner via `workflow_dispatch -f update_baselines=true`, then committed.

**P3 — `ocean` theme vs AGENTS.md doc gap.** Visual baselines cycle 4 themes (dark/light/sepia/ocean) while `AGENTS.md` documents 3. Not a bug: `content/config.yaml` ships `ocean` as a named F2 theme variant and `content/themes/extra-themes.yaml` adds forest/sandstone via F5; `scripts/review-surfaces.json` lists `[dark, light, sepia, ocean]`. Fix is a doc reconciliation only — no theme code/config changes.

Refs #394

issues.title: Feature: conversation-shaped shell reusing node viewers
issues.body:
The narrow (~400px) side-panel shell the other three features render into:
vertical rhythm, host design tokens, and reuse of the node-type viewers
(`src/views/viewers/*`). No full-page HUD, no favicon takeover. Part of #407
(bespoke `copilot` target).

## What exists today (verified) — mostly delivered; this issue formalizes the rest

- `EmbeddableApp` (#406) already renders headless: no HUD / favicon / dock
  padding, `minHeight: 100vh; width: 100%`, `data-kbx-surface="canvas"`, theme via
  `useCanvasTheme('inherit-host')` + `IsDarkContext`.
- `AnchorFirstView` (#408) already reuses `resolveViewer(node)` (the open viewer
  registry — never rebuilt) and lays out with Fluent tokens + spacing.
- **Not yet done:** a documented, reusable shell/layout primitive (spacing scale,
  section rhythm, max-width column, scroll/overflow behavior) that #409–#411
  target consistently, plus an explicit audit that no full-page chrome leaks into
  the canvas entry.

## Scope (template)

- Extract/define the shell as a small primitive (e.g. `CanvasShell`) wrapping the
  `copilot` target's `<Routes>` (`copilot.tsx`): consistent vertical rhythm, a
  ~400px-friendly column, **host tokens only** — no re-mirrored CSS vars (the
  audit flagged re-mirroring host vars elsewhere; `inherit-host` already provides
  them).
- Audit the canvas entry (`canvas.html` / `EmbeddableApp`) for any full-page HUD /
  favicon / dock remnants and assert their absence.
- Ensure the reused viewers render correctly in the narrow column: overflow,
  wrapping, long titles, and code / Mermaid blocks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A documented `CanvasShell` (or equivalent) wraps the copilot routes;
      #409–#411 render inside it.
- [ ] Playwright/visual test at ~400px width: no HUD, no favicon, no horizontal
      overflow; host light + dark tokens honored.
- [ ] Node-type viewers (Mission / Decision / Person / rich-markdown) render
      legibly in the narrow column.
- [ ] No re-mirrored theme vars — all tokens come from the host theme
      (`inherit-host`); asserted or documented.

## Out of scope

- Agent actions (#409), click → chat (#410), affordances (#411). This is
  layout/shell only.

## Dependencies / ordering

No hard dependencies — **foundational**. Should land first so #409–#411 target a
stable shell.

issues.title: Feature: affordance-aware node launchpad
issues.body:
Turn each node's viewer into a launchpad by surfacing the Source layer's
**per-retrieval affordances** (`read` / `comment` / `close` / `merge`,
`staging-area` links) as actionable items — "open issue", "view PR", "jump to
staging area". Affordances are situational, so render only what the current
retrieval carries. Part of #407 (bespoke `copilot` target).

## What exists today (verified) — and the prerequisite gap

- **Core already models this precisely.** `kbexplorer-core` → `src/source.ts`:
  `Resource { href, kind, affordances: Affordance[], links: ResourceLink[] }`;
  affordances are per-retrieval / situational (advisory `possibleAffordances` on
  the `Source`, authoritative list on each `Resource`);
  `STAGING_AREA_REL = 'staging-area'`; helpers `hasAffordance()` and
  `stagingAreaLink()`. The open `Affordance` union already names
  `comment` / `close` / `merge` as examples.
- **But `KBNode` does NOT carry `affordances` or `links`.** `KBNode`
  (`kbexplorer-core` → `src/graph.ts`) has `source`, `sourceId?`, `sourceRefs?`,
  `evidence?`, `identityClaims?`, `linkedRefs?`, `derivation?` — **none** of them
  the situational `Resource.affordances` / `links`. The manifest the template
  renders therefore has **no affordance data on the node today.**
- Consequence: this is a load-bearing **data-path prerequisite**. The affordances
  must be threaded from the `Resource` onto the node/manifest (or fetched live)
  before the launchpad can render anything real. **Do not ship a launchpad that
  renders a hardcoded / per-type / aspirational action list** — that is exactly
  the "designed in isolation, never wired to the real consumer" trap.

## Scope — two parts

### 1. Data path (prerequisite; core + CLI manifest)
Decide and record **one**:
- **Baked**: thread the retrieval's `affordances` + `links` onto the node in the
  generated manifest as additive optional fields (e.g. `node.affordances?`,
  `node.links?`). Simple for the static showcase; snapshots the affordances at
  generate time. Likely needs a small additive `KBNode` field in core —
  coordinate with the identity/provenance owners (E1, `anokye-labs/kbexplorer#13`).
- **Live**: expose a loopback endpoint that returns a node's current affordances
  on demand. Honors the situational nature but only works behind the CLI server.

### 2. Rendering (this issue, template)
- In the node viewers / `AnchorFirstView`, render an **affordance bar**: map
  `read` → open the source `href`; `comment` / `close` / `merge` → the matching
  action; a `staging-area` link → "jump to staging area".
- Render **only** the affordances present on the current retrieval; empty → no
  bar (no placeholder).
- Route actions through the shared consent model (see #410): read-only → direct
  `/affordance/:name`; mutating (`close` / `merge`) → agent chat turn.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A node whose retrieval carries `['read','comment']` shows exactly those two
      controls; a node with no affordances shows no launchpad.
- [ ] A staged resource surfaces its `staging-area` link as a navigable item.
- [ ] Affordance data comes from real retrieval data (manifest field or endpoint),
      **not** a static per-type table — asserted by a test that a node without
      affordances renders nothing.
- [ ] Mutating affordances route via the agent (no direct mutating POST from the
      iframe).

## Out of scope

- The agent action verbs (#409).
- The click → chat plumbing (#410) — reused here, not built here.
- Designing new Source adapters or the affordances they advertise.

## Dependencies / ordering

The **data-path prerequisite (part 1)** blocks the rendering half — and may need a
small additive core field. Consent routing is shared with #410. After the #412
shell; reuses #409 / #410 plumbing.

issues.title: Feature: bidirectional click to chat
issues.body:
Make the panel feed the conversation: a click in the canvas ("pin as anchor",
"what derives from this?", "show affected") becomes the next chat turn, so the
agent runs the right `kbx_*` tool → `executeAffordance` → mutation → `/events`
back to the panel. The surface becomes **bidirectional** — it shapes the next
turn, not just displays. Part of #407 (bespoke `copilot` target).

## What exists today (verified)

- The reverse direction (agent → panel) is #409; this issue is **panel →
  conversation**.
- The CLI companion **`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#195` "Click→chat seam (Lane B)"
  is OPEN** and owns the CLI half: "turn iframe intents into agent chat turns via
  the SDK message seam, so the agent picks the right `kbx_*` tool →
  `executeAffordance` → mutation → SSE back to the panel." This template issue
  owns the **iframe UX + the intent POST**.
- **The iframe has no privileged host bridge** (create-canvas contract). Panel →
  conversation therefore goes: iframe → HTTP POST to a loopback CLI endpoint →
  the CLI's SDK message seam posts the turn. The template alone cannot inject a
  conversation turn.
- `AnchorFirstView` already renders clickable node cards/chips, but they only
  navigate `#/node/<id>` today — no conversation feedback.

## Scope (template)

- Add per-node action controls in the node viewers / `AnchorFirstView`: **"Pin as
  anchor"**, **"What derives from this?"**, **"Show affected"** (an extensible
  list, not hardcoded to three).
- On click, POST an intent to a loopback endpoint the CLI exposes (defined with
  `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#195`), e.g. `POST /chat-intent { intent, nodeId,
  prompt? }`. **Do not mutate the graph directly from the iframe.**
- Reflect the round-trip: after the agent acts, the panel updates via the #409
  `/events` path (e.g. re-anchor). Show a pending → acknowledged state on the
  control.

## Consent routing (must honor)

Mirror the do-seam consent model:
- **Read-only** intents ("what derives", "show affected" = queries) MAY map to a
  direct read-only `/affordance/:name` POST.
- **Mutating** intents MUST route through the agent chat turn — never a direct
  mutating POST from the iframe.

## Contract (proposed)

`POST /chat-intent` body `{ intent: 'pin' | 'derives' | 'affected' | string,
nodeId: string, prompt?: string }` → `{ ok: true }`. The CLI (#195) translates it
to a chat turn / tool call. This issue owns only the client call + the optimistic
UI; the SDK message seam is `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#195`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clicking a node's "What derives from this?" produces a real chat turn
      (verified in-app) that the agent answers with the corresponding `kbx_*`
      tool.
- [ ] "Pin as anchor" re-anchors the panel via the #409 round-trip.
- [ ] Mutating intents never issue a direct mutating `/affordance` POST from the
      iframe (unit/integration assertion).
- [ ] Graceful no-op + a visible hint when the `/chat-intent` endpoint is absent
      (older CLI).

## Out of scope

- Declaring the agent-facing `actions[]` (#409).
- The CLI SDK message seam (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#195`).
- Rendering the source-affordance catalog (#411, which reuses this routing).

## Dependencies / ordering

Blocked by **#409** (the SSE round-trip) and **`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#195`**
(the SDK message seam). After the #412 shell.

issues.title: Feature: agent action surface (anchor/expand/trace/filter)
issues.body:
Define the canvas `actions[]` the agent invokes (via `invoke_canvas_action`) to
steer the panel — `anchor`, `expand`, `trace`, `filter` — and wire each to update
the embeddable view over the loopback `/events` SSE stream. These are
agent/host-facing verbs (the agent drives; the panel reflects the conversation),
not auto-rendered chrome. Part of #407 (bespoke `copilot` target).

## What exists today (verified against `main` / template v0.4.0)

- **SSE transport is shipped.** `GET /events` on the loopback server emits
  `ready`, `graph-updated {nodes[]}`, and `anchor {nodeId}`
  (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` → `src/extension/canvas-server.js`, `SSE_EVENTS`).
  Domain events flow through an injected `subscribe(instanceId, onEvent)` seam
  whose **default is a no-op (heartbeat only)** — real triggers are a documented
  follow-up (`docs/canvas-loopback-contract.md`).
- **The `/affordance/:name` do-seam is shipped** (mutations route through
  `executeAffordance`; consent + provenance enforced at the core).
- **The canvas `actions[]` were NOT built.** `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#194`
  (CLOSED) was titled "Canvas actions (anchor/expand/trace/filter) …" but
  delivered only `/events` + `/affordance/:name`. `buildCanvasOptions()` in
  `src/extension/canvas.js` declares **no `actions[]`**, and no
  `anchor`/`expand`/`trace`/`filter` handler exists anywhere in the CLI (verified
  by grep — the only `anchor` is the SSE event constant). **This issue is now the
  sole home for the agent action surface.**
- **No template-side SSE consumer exists.** `EmbeddableApp` (#406) loads a baked
  local manifest (`useKnowledgeBase` → `loadLocalKnowledgeBase`) and never opens
  an `EventSource`, so the panel cannot yet react to a pushed event.

## Scope — two coupled halves

### CLI companion (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`) — declare + emit
- Add `actions: [...]` to `buildCanvasOptions()` (`src/extension/canvas.js`):
  `anchor`, `expand`, `trace`, `filter`, each with a JSON-Schema `inputSchema` and
  an `async handler(ctx)` (`ctx = { instanceId, input, host, … }`).
- Replace the no-op `subscribe` default with a real per-`instanceId` event bus so
  a handler can push an SSE frame to that panel's open `/events` stream.
- This is the unbuilt half of the closed #194 — **file/track as a CLI companion
  issue** (do not silently reopen #194).

### Template (this issue) — consume + apply
- Open one `EventSource(<origin>/events)` in `EmbeddableApp` (or a `useCanvasEvents`
  hook) on mount; `<origin>` derives from the boot config's `searchServiceUrl`.
- Map each event to a view mutation on the `copilot` target (`copilot.tsx` +
  `copilot-home/AnchorFirstView.tsx`):
  - `anchor {nodeId}` → navigate `#/node/<id>` (re-anchor `AnchorFirstView`).
  - `expand {nodeId}` → raise that neighbor's expanded state (or bump `maxExpanded`).
  - `trace {from,to}` → render the path between two nodes (new lightweight section).
  - `filter {cluster}` → constrain the neighborhood/constellation to a cluster.

## Contract decision (must be made + documented)

The SSE event vocabulary is currently frozen to `graph-updated` / `anchor`. For
`expand` / `trace` / `filter`, choose **one** and record it in
`docs/canvas-loopback-contract.md`:
- **(recommended)** extend `SSE_EVENTS` with named `expand` / `trace` / `filter`
  events — a deliberate, versioned contract addition (not a silent one); or
- express them as an `anchor` event plus a client-side view parameter.

Proposed action input shapes: `anchor {nodeIds: string[]}`, `expand {nodeId}`,
`trace {from, to}`, `filter {cluster}`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `list_canvas_capabilities({ canvasId: 'kbexplorer' })` returns the four
      actions with their schemas.
- [ ] `invoke_canvas_action({ instanceId, actionName: 'anchor', input: { nodeIds:[id] } })`
      re-anchors the live panel (visible in the iframe), verified end-to-end
      against the real CLI loopback server.
- [ ] `expand` / `trace` / `filter` each produce their documented view change.
- [ ] `docs/canvas-loopback-contract.md` updated to reflect any new event names;
      existing `anchor` / `graph-updated` semantics unchanged.
- [ ] The template SSE consumer degrades safely (no console errors, no crash) when
      `/events` is a bare heartbeat (older CLI / no-op seam).
- [ ] Unit tests: the event → view-state reducer, and the CLI handler emits the
      expected SSE frame.

## Out of scope

- Panel → conversation / click-to-chat (that's #410).
- Surfacing Source-layer affordances (#411).
- The full-page `spa` route tree.

## Dependencies / ordering

Builds on the shipped `/events` transport and the shell (#412). **Precedes #410
and #411** (both reuse this action + SSE plumbing). The CLI companion (declare
`actions[]` + real `subscribe` bus) must land with or before the template
consumer.

issues.title: Feature: anchor-first home view (neighbor-anchored, not constellation)
issues.body: Default canvas view is **not** the constellation. Render the conversation's anchor node(s) + their weight-ranked neighbors, reusing `graph.related` and the `llm-context` greedy-expansion logic. Relevant-but-unexpanded neighbors render as navigable `kg://` chips. Constellation becomes an optional zoom-out, not the landing. Part of #407 (bespoke `copilot` target).

issues.title: Epic: bespoke copilot Representation target (agent-driven, anchor-first)
issues.body:
**This is the destination surface for Copilot — not a port of the `spa` target.** A new `copilot` `Representation` consuming the same pure `KBGraph`, designed for an **agent-driven, conversation-anchored** context instead of human-driven full-viewport exploration.

Program epic: anokye-labs/kbexplorer#8. De-risking/shared infra: #401.

### Why bespoke (not reuse spa.tsx)
- The SPA assumes the **human** navigates (drag the force graph, browse). In Copilot the **agent** is a first-class actor (`invoke_canvas_action`) — the agent steers, the panel reflects the conversation.
- A force-directed constellation needs a wide canvas + mouse; next to chat it's a ~400px column.
- The SPA is read-only exploration; it ignores the Source layer's per-retrieval **affordances** (open issue, view PR, staging-area) — the actionable stuff a repo-backed session wants.

### What it shares vs. doesn't
**Reuses:** pure `KBGraph`, node-type **viewers** (`src/views/viewers/*` — Mission/Decision/Person etc.), `kg://` identity + relations, `graph.related` + `llm-context` expansion logic, the loopback search service.
**Does NOT reuse:** the react-router route tree, constellation-as-landing, full-page HUD/favicon.

### Sub-issues
- [ ] Anchor-first home view (anchor node(s) + weight-ranked neighbors; constellation is an optional zoom-out)
- [ ] Agent action surface (`anchor` / `expand` / `trace` / `filter` canvas actions)
- [ ] Bidirectional click → chat (pin anchor, "what derives from this?", "show affected")
- [ ] Affordance-aware node launchpad (surface Source affordances as actions)
- [ ] Conversation-shaped shell (narrow side panel, host tokens, reuse viewers)
- [ ] DECISION: repo placement / viewer reuse (new target here vs. extracted Representation package vs. CLI-extension-local)

### Depends on shared infra from #401
Host→Fluent theme adapter (#405), embeddable mount (#406), presentation-token contract (anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#15). The theming work is shared because the reused viewers are Fluent; only "host the full SPA route tree" is throwaway scaffolding.

issues.title: Feature: embeddable headless mount + inherit-host visual mode
issues.body: Add a headless/embeddable entry for the `spa` route tree (no full-page chrome/favicon) plus an `inherit-host` visual mode that defers to host theme. Enables hosting in a loopback iframe (Copilot canvas) reusing constellation/grid/reading/HUD + node viewers. Part of #401.

issues.title: Feature: surface full Fluent design knobs (fonts, radius, density, spacing)
issues.body: Surface far more of Fluent's design choice through `config.yaml`/themes: font families & sizes, corner radius, density/spacing, stroke widths — not just brand/neutral colors. Goal: hosts restyle deeply without editing the submodule, and these flow into a presentation-token contract. Part of #401.

issues.title: Feature: host CSS-var to Fluent theme adapter
issues.body: The SPA themes only from Fluent token names (`themeModule`, external YAML, `clusterTokens`). A canvas host mirrors **semantic** vars (`--background-color-default`, `--text-color-*`, `--font-sans/mono`, true-color). Add an adapter mapping host vars -> Fluent `Theme` so the SPA inherits the app's look with no fork. Part of #401.

issues.title: Feature: nodeRenderer host theme-source bridge (replace isDark bool)
issues.body: `nodeRenderer.ts` paints cluster-color hex + a binary `isDark` flag. For host-themed canvases it should read theme-source/foreground/background from CSS vars, not a boolean. Wire cluster + label colors through resolved tokens so nodes adapt to host theme. Part of #401.

issues.title: Feature: Detokenize styles.ts colors (theme-driven edges/relations/layers)
issues.body:
Edge/relation/node-layer colors in `src/representation/styles.ts` are hardcoded hex (`#a0adb8`, `#e8a854`…). They ignore the active theme, so a canvas host's tokens (or any non-default theme) can't recolor the constellation/legend.

Resolve colors from theme tokens (Fluent CSS vars / true-color tokens) with the current hex as fallback. Keep the data-driven legend behavior. Part of #401.

issues.title: Epic: Copilot canvas representation target (host-themeable, embeddable)
issues.body:
Make the SPA renderable as a **host-themed, embeddable** target so it can be hosted in a GitHub Copilot canvas (loopback iframe) — a NEW `Representation` target, not a fork. Investigation confirms the SPA is already CSS-var driven (Fluent v9 tokens, scoped cluster/page overrides) and search is wired via `VITE_SEARCH_SERVICE_URL`, so reuse is cheap. The blockers are theming and embeddability.

### Gaps (sub-features)
- [ ] Detokenize `styles.ts` (edge/relation/layer colors are hardcoded hex)
- [ ] `nodeRenderer.ts` theme-source bridge (uses cluster hex + `isDark` bool)
- [ ] Host-token → Fluent theme adapter (`--background-color-default`/`--text-color-*`/`--font-*`)
- [ ] Surface full Fluent design knobs via config (fonts, corner radius, density, spacing)
- [ ] Embeddable headless mount + `inherit-host` visual mode

### Why
Enables a Copilot-bespoke panel reusing constellation/grid/reading/HUD + node viewers, and is the first step toward multiple alternative UX surfaces over the same pure graph.

Tracks: kbexplorer-core presentation-token contract + kbexplorer docs epic.

issues.title: fix(dtu): L3 gitea e2e app boot 500s — generated manifest module missing under playwright.gitea.config.ts
issues.body:
## Summary

With the DTU Gitea seed `listPulls` 404 now fixed (#396), the L3 live-Gitea e2e lane (`dtu-gitea.yml` → `playwright.gitea.config.ts`) reaches app bring-up — where the Vite dev server **500s** and the app never boots, so every `e2e/gitea` spec fails.

## Root cause

- `playwright.gitea.config.ts` serves the app with a **bare Vite dev server**: `node ./node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js --port … --strictPort`, in **remote/repo-aware mode** (it sets `VITE_GH_API_BASE` → the Gitea adapter but **not** `VITE_KB_LOCAL`).
- `src/engine/local-loader.ts` statically imports `../generated/repo-manifest.json`. Vite's import-analysis resolves this static-string dynamic import at **transform time**, regardless of mode.
- `src/generated/repo-manifest.json` is **gitignored** (`src/generated/.gitignore`) and is produced **only** by `scripts/generate-manifest.js`, which normally runs via the `prebuild` npm script before `vite build`. A **bare `vite` dev server never runs `prebuild`**, so in a fresh CI checkout the file is **absent** →

  ```
  Failed to resolve import "../generated/repo-manifest.json" from "src/engine/local-loader.ts". Does the file exist?
  ```

  (HTTP 500). The app fails to boot, so all gitea specs fail. This was previously **masked** by the seed 404 (pre-existing, not a regression).
- L2 (static twin, `playwright.config.ts`) is unaffected: it serves `vite preview` of a **production build**, and `github-pages.yml` runs `generate-manifest.js` + `vite build` first, so the import is bundled. Only L3's bare-dev path lacks manifest generation.

## Fix (minimal; L3 stays REMOTE)

Generate the manifest module **before** the Vite dev server transforms `local-loader.ts`, by running `node scripts/generate-manifest.js` from `twins/gitea/global-setup.ts` (Playwright runs `globalSetup` before webServers start; applies to CI and local `npm run test:e2e:gitea`).

- Does **not** set `VITE_KB_LOCAL` — the app stays remote-mode against the live Gitea twin, so the mutate → refresh assertions stay meaningful. The generated manifest exists only to satisfy Vite's import resolver; it is never consumed at runtime in remote mode.
- Does **not** use `/* @vite-ignore */` (that would break L2/production local-mode bundling, where the manifest must be bundled + consumed).
- `generate-manifest.js` is offline-tolerant (gh/git calls are best-effort) and its output is gitignored, so it always writes a valid manifest and does not affect seed.mjs's `git add -A` snapshot.

## Verification

- Reproduced + fixed locally via Vite's programmatic `transformRequest('/src/engine/local-loader.ts')`: manifest **absent** → `Failed to resolve import … repo-manifest.json`; manifest **present** → transform OK.
- `npm test` → 740 pass; `npm run lint` → 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings).

Refs #394

issues.title: Fix DTU Gitea seed listPulls 404 (revives L3/L6 nightly)
issues.body:
## Problem

`npm run dtu:seed` fast-fails **100% of the time since ~2026-06-13**, taking down two nightly lanes with one root cause:

- **L3** live-Gitea e2e (`dtu-gitea.yml`) — 🔴 100% fail
- **L6** exploratory-agent stage (`explore-dtu.yml`) — 🔴 100% fail

Both fail at the same spot:

```
[seed] FAILED: listPulls failed: 404 ... /api/swagger
```

First failing call: `twins/gitea/seed.mjs:69` (`seedSourceEditPr`) → `listPulls` → `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` (`twins/gitea/gitea-client.mjs:118`). Issue-seeding succeeds earlier in the same run, so the repo exists.

## Root cause

Gitea guards `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` with `mustAllowPulls`, which returns the **generic API NotFound** (body references `/api/swagger`) when `CanEnablePulls()` is false. `CanEnablePulls() = !IsMirror && !IsEmpty`.

The seed creates the repo with `auto_init: false`, so it is born `is_empty = true`. `snapshotPushMain` force-pushes a working-tree snapshot to `main` to make it non-empty, but in the containerized CI Gitea the `is_empty` DB flag is **not reliably cleared** before `seedSourceEditPr → listPulls` runs → deterministic 404. Issues don't require a non-empty repo, which is why they succeed first.

## Fix (minimal, within `twins/gitea/`)

1. Create the repo with `auto_init: true` so it is born non-empty via Gitea's **in-process** repo init (independent of any push hook) → Pull Requests unit enabled from creation. `snapshotPushMain` still force-pushes the working-tree snapshot over the initial commit, so `main` mirrors the real repo exactly.
2. Add a `waitForRepoReady` poll after the push that asserts the repo reports `empty === false` and the default branch is resolvable **before** any pulls operation — turning a silent 404 into a clear, actionable error and absorbing any async settle.
3. Justify the pinned `gitea/gitea:1.24` image tag.

No assertions weakened (holdout discipline preserved — the fix makes the repo genuinely pull-ready rather than masking the failure).

## Verify

Revive both lanes and confirm they get past `dtu:seed`:
`gh workflow run dtu-gitea.yml` and `gh workflow run explore-dtu.yml`, then watch the runs.

Refs #394 (P0 — Fix the Gitea seed `listPulls` 404).

issues.title: DTU integration testing is bit-rotted: all nightly jobs (Gitea L3 / visual L5 / exploratory L6) 100% red since ~2026-06-13
issues.body:
## Summary

A read-only audit of the Digital Twin Universe (DTU) found that **integration testing is effectively not happening in CI**. Only the hermetic PR gate (unit + static-twin e2e — both touch no external services) is green. **Every nightly integration/visual/exploratory job has failed 100% of the time since its inception (~2026-06-13)** and has apparently gone unwatched. The recent Epic #298 decoupling did **not** cause this — the twin seam is intact; the rot is operational.

## Evidence — per-workflow real CI status

| Layer | Workflow | Trigger | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 unit (incl. `twins/gitea/__tests__/adapter.test.mjs`, 27 tests) | PR gate | push/PR | ✅ green (hermetic) |
| L2 static-twin e2e (`playwright.config.ts` + `twins/github/`) | `github-pages.yml` | push/PR | ✅ green |
| **L3 live Gitea e2e** (`playwright.gitea.config.ts`) | **`dtu-gitea.yml`** | dispatch + nightly `30 4 * * *` | 🔴 **100% fail (16/16)** |
| L4 full-loop (CLI↔DTU↔app, `playwright.full-loop.config.ts`) | **none (#269 open)** | manual only | ⚪ no CI |
| **L5 visual regression** | **`visual-regression.yml`** | dispatch + nightly `15 5 * * *` | 🔴 **100% fail (15/15)** |
| **L6 exploratory-agent** (`scripts/explore-dtu.mjs`) | **`explore-dtu.yml`** | dispatch + nightly ~06:00 | 🔴 **100% fail (15/15)** |

## Root causes

- **L3 + L6** fast-fail at `npm run dtu:seed` → `listPulls failed: 404 ... /api/swagger`. First failing call is `seed.mjs:69` (`seedSourceEditPr`) → `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` (`gitea-client.mjs:118`). Issue-seeding succeeds first, so the repo exists but either the git snapshot push (`snapshotPushMain`) hasn't landed a branch before pulls are queried, or the Gitea route/version drifted. **One fix unblocks both L3 and L6.**
- **L5** fails `verify:visual` — **64 surfaces at 2–6% diff** (hud-docked/hud-expanded/node-selected/overview/reading × dark/light/ocean/sepia × desktop/mobile). **Stale baselines**, not infra.
- **L4** has no CI at all (#269 still open); it only runs manually and defaults to `FULL_LOOP_SUBSTRATE=static` (the `gitea` substrate is explicitly deferred), and it requires the CLI cloned as a sibling.

## Seam check (good news)

The Phase 0–6 Source refactor (#376) preserved the twin interception seam: `src/api/github.ts:57` still honors `VITE_GH_API_BASE`; `GitHubApiSource` routes through the same `../../api` fetch helpers and introduced no new endpoints; `twins/` was untouched by the refactor and L2 (static twin) is green — proving the app↔twin request surface still matches.

## `kbexplorer-pilot-fixture` — orphaned & obsolete

`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-pilot-fixture` (private, "dress rehearsal", CLI #56) was **re-scoped on 2026-06-13** to run the rehearsal against the **Gitea DTU instead of a real repo**; the issue states the fixture is "obsolete and slated for deletion." It was never deleted, is **referenced nowhere** in the org (`gh search code "pilot-fixture"` → empty), and the Gitea seed is built from the **template's own working tree**, not the fixture. Net: a drifted orphan. Its retirement also left the **"test against a real GitHub repo" leg with no replacement** — the `GitHubApiSource` path is now twin-only.

## Prioritized recommendations

- [x] **P0 — Fix the Gitea seed `listPulls` 404** (`seed.mjs:69` / `gitea-client.mjs:118`): ensure `snapshotPushMain` lands a branch before pulls are queried, or pin the Gitea route/version. Revives **both L3 and L6**. ✅ Fixed in #396 (Closes #395) — `dtu:seed` now passes in both lanes (L6 green; L3 past seed). See comment below re: a separate, pre-existing L3 app-staging blocker.
- [x] **P0 — Fix the L3 app-boot 500** (`playwright.gitea.config.ts` serves a bare `vite` dev server, and `src/engine/local-loader.ts` statically imports the gitignored `src/generated/repo-manifest.json`, which Vite resolves at transform time → a fresh CI checkout 500s and the app never boots, failing every `e2e/gitea` spec): write a minimal static **stub** manifest via committed script `twins/gitea/ensure-manifest-stub.mjs` (idempotent — only if absent), chained ahead of `vite` in the gitea webServer command so the import resolves before Vite's first transform (race-free; fully offline — no `gh` calls). L3 stays REMOTE-mode, so the stub is never read at runtime (the app sources from the live Gitea twin) and the mutate→refresh assertions stay meaningful. ✅ Fixed in #399 (Closes #397), hardened in #400 — verified green end-to-end via `dtu-gitea.yml` run [28326794414](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/actions/runs/28326794414): `[seed] seed complete`, no `Failed to resolve import` (transient pre-transform error eliminated), e2e/gitea specs 10 passed / 2 skipped (the 2 skips = documented remote content-model gap, cf #265).
- [ ] **P0 — Failure visibility:** the nightlies have alerted no one in 2+ weeks. Add notification-on-failure (or treat them as gating) so red ≠ silently ignored.
- [ ] **P1 — Refresh stale visual baselines** (`visual-regression.yml` `update_baselines=true`, human-reviewed), then confirm L5 goes green. Also reconcile the **4 captured themes (dark/light/ocean/sepia)** vs the **3 documented in AGENTS.md (dark/light/sepia)** — `ocean` is undocumented or a stray baseline.
- [ ] **P1 — Wire L4 full-loop into nightly (close #269)** with `FULL_LOOP_SUBSTRATE=static` first; enable the deferred `gitea` substrate once P0 lands for a true core+cli+template+Gitea end-to-end.
- [ ] **P2 — Add scheduled cross-real-repository smoke:** run `GitHubApiSource`/CLI against a few small real public repos of varied shape (empty / no-releases / large / monorepo) with a read-only token, to catch real API drift the twins can't model.
- [ ] **P2 — Resolve `kbexplorer-pilot-fixture`:** execute the documented decision to delete/archive it, **or** repurpose+refresh it as the controlled target for the real-repo smoke above and wire it explicitly. *(Deletion is a human decision — not done autonomously.)*
- [ ] **P3 — Add a twin-coverage contract assertion** that enumerates the endpoints `GitHubApiSource` fetches and fails if `twins/` doesn't cover them, so future Source surface growth can't silently bypass twin interception.

## Method

Read-only: `gh` CLI run-history + local file reads + targeted `vitest`. No files or issues modified during the investigation.

cc: this surfaced during the Epic #298 close-out audit. P0/P1 items keep our ability to do thorough cross-real-repo + full multi-user simulation testing.

issues.title: ci: bot-merged PRs to main don't trigger GitHub Pages deploy (live site goes stale)
issues.body:
## Problem

The auto-merge workflow merges agent PRs via the REST API using `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub suppresses workflow triggers from `GITHUB_TOKEN`-initiated pushes (anti-recursion), so the `Deploy to GitHub Pages` workflow — which fires `on: push: branches: [main]` — never runs for bot merges.

Result: every auto-merged PR (Phases 2/3/4: #374/#375/#376) is on `main` but **not deployed**. The live site at https://anokye-labs.github.io/kbexplorer-template/ is stale (last deploy was a human-merged commit).

## Fix

`workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` are the documented exceptions to the `GITHUB_TOKEN` recursion rule — they DO trigger runs. So:

1. `auto-merge.yml`: after a successful merge to `main`, dispatch the Pages workflow (`createWorkflowDispatch` on `github-pages.yml`, ref `main`). Gate on `merged > 0` so we only deploy when main actually changed. Add `actions: write` permission.
2. `github-pages.yml`: allow the `build`/`deploy` jobs to run on `workflow_dispatch` (currently gated to `push` only).

Avoids keying Pages on the auto-merge `workflow_run` (which would mutually re-trigger, since auto-merge already listens for "Deploy to GitHub Pages").

## Acceptance

- A bot merge to `main` results in a Pages deploy of the new HEAD with no human action.
- No infinite trigger loop.
- Human merges still deploy via the existing `push` trigger.

issues.title: fix(auto-merge): updateBranch uses stale list sha instead of fresh head
issues.body:
The auto-merge workflow passes the stale list-time `pr.head.sha` to `pulls.updateBranch` when bringing a `behind` PR up to date. It should use the freshly-fetched `detail.head.sha`, otherwise the update 422s if the branch moved between the `list` and `get` calls. (The `merge` call intentionally keeps `pr.head.sha` as a TOCTOU guard.)

Found by Devin Review on anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core#2; fixing in all three repos in lockstep.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` updateBranch uses `detail.head.sha`

issues.title: ci: trigger auto-merge via workflow_run (check_suite unreliable)
issues.body:
## Problem
`auto-merge.yml` was triggered by `check_suite` + `schedule`, but on a newly-added workflow those did not fire reliably (0 sweep runs observed for ~15 min), so agent PRs were not auto-merged and still required a manual click.

## Goal
Trigger the sweep reliably and event-driven via `workflow_run` on completion of the gating check workflows, keeping `schedule` as a backstop and `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs.

## Scope
- Replace the `check_suite` trigger with `workflow_run` listing the gating check workflows (`dependency-review`, `linked-issue`, `pr-title`; template also `Deploy to GitHub Pages`).
- No change to the merge logic itself.

issues.title: ci: auto-merge should update behind branches under strict status checks
issues.body:
## Problem
Agent-authored PRs (Devin, Copilot) sit open waiting for a human to click merge, even when all required checks are green and 0 approvals are required. Agents are not permitted to merge into `main` directly.

## Goal
Add a lightweight auto-merge workflow that automatically squash-merges agent-authored PRs once they satisfy the repo ruleset (required status checks + conversation resolution). GitHub enforces the gate server-side, so a red or unresolved PR can never be merged by this automation.

## Scope
- Add `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`.
- Trigger on `check_suite` completion + a periodic `schedule` sweep + manual `workflow_dispatch`.
- For each open, non-draft PR to `main` authored by an allowlisted agent bot, attempt a squash merge; on failure (checks pending/unresolved threads) skip quietly.
- No change to branch protection / rulesets.

## Out of scope
- Merge queue / Copilot-specific dispatch (the heavier anokye-labs/plugins Auto-Flow pattern).

issues.title: Feature: Phase 7 — Template SPA semantic search integration (backlog)
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Integrate the kbexplorer-search service with the kbexplorer-template SPA, enabling
semantic search from the Ctrl-K palette and HUD search buttons.

## Why
Makes semantic search feel native in the visual explorer — the existing text search
in the palette would be augmented with semantic results from the search service.

## Scope
- Connect the search palette (Ctrl-K) to the search service API when configured.
- Display semantic results alongside existing text matches.
- Navigate to the matched node on selection.
- Config flag in config.yaml: `features.semanticSearch: true` + service URL.
- Graceful degradation: if the service is unavailable, text search works as before.

## Acceptance

issues.title: Feature: Phase 6 — Graph-aware ranking and related-node suggestions (backlog)
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Enhance search results with graph-aware ranking signals and related-node suggestions.
A search hit for a node should also surface its neighbors, parent, and cluster siblings
as contextual suggestions.

## Why
Graph-aware search is the differentiator: results know their place in the knowledge
graph, not just their text similarity. This enables "explore around this result" UX.

## Scope
- Boost results whose neighbors also match the query (graph proximity signal).
- Include related nodes in SearchResult (top-3 neighbors by edge weight).
- Cluster-coherence bonus: results in the same cluster as other hits rank higher.
- Hierarchy-aware snippets: include parent node title in snippet context.

## Acceptance
- A query that matches a node AND its parent ranks higher than an isolated match.
- Related-node suggestions are relevant and come from the graph, not just text similarity.

**Blocked by:** F4 (needs the base query engine).

issues.title: Feature: Phase 5 — Localhost search service (HTTP API)
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
A lightweight HTTP server that serves semantic search results from checked-in artifacts.
Runs locally during development or as a deployable service in production.

## Why
Enables real-time semantic search during development (alongside `kbexplorer dev`) and
provides a deployable API endpoint for hosted search.

## Scope
- HTTP server (Node.js, no framework dependency — use `node:http` or minimal fastify).
- `POST /search` endpoint: `{ query, limit?, cluster?, entityType?, minScore? } → SearchResult[]`.
- `GET /health` endpoint: service status + index metadata.
- Loads artifacts at startup; auto-reloads on file change (dev mode).
- CORS headers for localhost development.

## Acceptance

- Health endpoint reports model name, unit count, and dimensions.

issues.title: Task: Add optional FAISS index for fast k-NN search
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F4 — Vector index loading + semantic query engine

## Scope
Create `src/faiss-engine.ts` (optional, peer dependency):
- Use `faiss-node` as an optional peer dependency.
- Build a FAISS IndexFlatIP (inner product for normalized vectors) from artifact vectors.
- `FaissSearchEngine` implements the same `SearchEngine` interface.
- Auto-detect: if faiss-node is available, use it; otherwise fall back to pure-JS.
- The FAISS index is built at startup from the portable artifact vectors — it is NOT

## Validation criteria
FAISS engine returns identical results to pure-JS engine (same ranking order).

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: FAISS and pure-JS engines return the same top-5 results for a given query
- [ ] Test: when faiss-node is not installed, the fallback engine is used without error

issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F4 — Vector index loading + semantic query engine

## Scope
Create `src/search-engine.ts`:
- `createSearchEngine(artifacts: EmbeddingArtifact, provider: EmbeddingProvider): SearchEngine`
- `SearchEngine.search(query: string, opts?: { limit?, cluster?, entityType?, minScore? }): Promise<SearchResult[]>`
- Embed the query via the same provider used for indexing.
- Compute cosine similarity against all vectors (brute force for pure JS).
- Return top-k results mapped to SearchResult objects with full metadata from units.
- Apply optional filters (cluster, entityType, minScore threshold).

issues.title: Feature: Phase 4 — Vector index loading + semantic query engine
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Implement the query engine that loads checked-in artifacts, builds an in-memory vector
index, embeds incoming queries, and returns ranked `SearchResult` objects.

## Why
This is the index consumption role. The engine must be fast (sub-100ms for typical
knowledge bases) and return kbexplorer-native results with full graph metadata.

## Scope
- Load artifacts from disk (units.json + vectors.json).
- Build an in-memory vector index (FAISS via faiss-node, or a pure-JS fallback for
  portability).
- Query: embed the query text → k-nearest-neighbor search → map to SearchResults.
- Filters: by cluster, by entity type, by score threshold.
- Pure-JS cosine similarity fallback for environments without native FAISS.

## Acceptance
- Query returns top-k results ranked by relevance.
- Cluster/type filters work correctly.
- Fallback mode works without FAISS native binary.

**Blocked by:** F3 (needs serialized artifacts to load).

issues.title: Task: Implement drift detection gate (--check mode)
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate

## Scope
Create `src/drift.ts`:
- `checkDrift(artifactDir: string, graph: KBGraph, config: SearchConfig): DriftResult`
- Re-extracts SearchUnits from the current graph (no embedding API call).
- Compares extracted units against committed `units.json` (by canonical stringify).
- Compares content hash against `index-meta.json.contentHash`.
- Returns `{ fresh: boolean, staleUnits: string[], missingUnits: string[], extraUnits: string[] }`.
- Exits non-zero when units diverge OR content hash mismatches.
- Never calls the embedding provider — purely deterministic.

## Validation criteria
Drift detection is purely offline and catches stale artifacts.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: check with fresh artifacts returns { fresh: true }
- [ ] Test: check after adding a node returns { fresh: false, missingUnits: [...] }
- [ ] Test: check after modifying node content returns { fresh: false, staleUnits: [...] }
- [ ] Test: no network calls are made during check

issues.title: Task: Implement artifact writer with deterministic serialization
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate

## Scope
Create `src/artifacts.ts`:
- `writeArtifacts(dir: string, units: SearchUnit[], vectors: EmbeddingVector[], config: SearchConfig): void`
- Writes three files to `dir/`:
  - `index-meta.json`: `{ version: 1, model, dimensions, unitCount, contentHash, generatedFrom }`
  - `units.json`: SearchUnit[] with sorted keys, sorted by unitId.
  - `vectors.json`: EmbeddingVector[] sorted by unitId, vectors as number arrays.
- All JSON uses `canonicalStringify`: sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline.
- `readArtifacts(dir: string)`: deserialize back.
- `computeContentHash(graph: KBGraph): string`: SHA-256 of the canonical graph.

## Validation criteria
Write + read round-trip is byte-identical; hash is deterministic.

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Test: writeArtifacts then readArtifacts returns identical data
- [ ] Test: two writes of same data produce byte-identical files (diff returns empty)
- [ ] Test: computeContentHash on same graph returns same hash
- [ ] Test: index-meta.json contains correct unit count and model name

issues.title: Feature: Phase 3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Define the on-disk artifact format for checked-in search state, implement deterministic
serialization, and provide a CI-grade drift detection gate.

## Why
The repository owns the semantic search corpus. Artifacts must be deterministic (identical
input → byte-identical output), reviewable in PRs, and verifiable in CI. This is the
same principle behind `kbexplorer derive --check` — the search equivalent.

## Scope
- Artifact file format: `search-artifacts/` directory containing:
  - `index-meta.json`: version, model, dimensions, unit count, content hash.
  - `units.json`: SearchUnit array (no vectors — readable, reviewable).
  - `vectors.json`: EmbeddingVector array (or a binary format for large indexes).
- Deterministic serialization: sorted keys, stable array order, no timestamps.
- Drift detection: `--check` flag that compares committed artifacts against a fresh
  extraction (without calling the embedding API) and exits non-zero on mismatch.
- Content-hash computation for the source graph (so artifacts know what they were built from).

## Acceptance
- Write + read round-trip produces byte-identical artifacts.
- `--check` detects when content changed but artifacts are stale.
- `--check` passes when artifacts are fresh.

**Blocked by:** F2 (needs embedding generation to produce the artifacts).

issues.title: Task: Implement batch embedding generator with content-hash caching

Create `src/embed.ts`:
- `generateEmbeddings(units: SearchUnit[], provider: EmbeddingProvider, opts?): Promise<EmbeddingVector[]>`

- Compute SHA-256 hash of each SearchUnit.text; if a previous artifact has the same

- Rate limiting: configurable delay between batches (default 100ms).
- Progress callback for CLI integration.

- [ ] Test: re-running with identical units and a cached artifact makes 0 embed() calls
- [ ] Test: changing one unit text re-embeds only that unit
- [ ] Test: progress callback fires with correct counts

issues.title: Feature: Phase 2 — Pluggable embedding provider + batch generation
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

Implement the embedding provider abstraction and a default OpenAI provider, plus
batch embedding generation that converts SearchUnits into EmbeddingVectors.

## Why
Embedding generation must be pluggable — different teams use different models (OpenAI,
Cohere, local Ollama, etc.). The abstraction lets the artifact format stay stable while

issues.title: Feature: Phase 1 — KBGraph → SearchUnit extraction pipeline
issues.body:
**Parent epic:** E-search-tmpl — Semantic search companion module

## What
Implement the extraction pipeline that converts a `KBGraph` (nodes, edges, clusters)
into an array of `SearchUnit` objects — the atomic searchable entities.

## Why
The search module must understand the kbexplorer content model deeply, not just treat
nodes as raw text. SearchUnits carry graph-aware metadata (cluster, hierarchy, connections,
entity type, identity URN) so that search results can be placed back into the graph.

## Scope
- Parse KBNode content (rawContent markdown) into searchable text.
- Chunk long nodes into multiple SearchUnits with configurable max-token limits and overlap.
- Enrich each SearchUnit with graph context: cluster, parent, connections list, entity type.
- Handle all NodeSource types (authored, structured, derived, issue, file, etc.).
- Deterministic output: same graph → same SearchUnits (stable ordering, no randomness).
- Unit tests with fixture graphs.

## Acceptance
- A KBGraph with 20+ nodes produces correctly-shaped SearchUnits.
- Long nodes are chunked; short nodes produce a single SearchUnit.
- Graph metadata (cluster, connections, parent) is correctly propagated.
- Output is deterministic (two runs on the same input → identical output).

**Blocked by:** F0 (needs the core types and package skeleton).

issues.title: Epic: Semantic search companion module (kbexplorer-search)
issues.body:
## What
kbexplorer defines a structured knowledge graph: authored markdown nodes, frontmatter
metadata, clusters, hierarchy, relationships, and source-aware content. This Epic creates
a companion `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search` module that understands that model and turns
it into a semantic search corpus — without making the visual graph app or the core CLI
responsible for vector-search infrastructure.

The module has two complementary roles:

1. **Index production** — reads the kbexplorer content model, derives searchable units from
   the graph (SearchUnits), generates embeddings via a pluggable provider, and writes
   checked-in search artifacts (embeddings, index metadata, node-to-vector mappings).
   These artifacts become part of the repository — they travel with branches, PRs, reviews,
   releases, and deployments.

2. **Index consumption** — loads the checked-in artifacts, builds an efficient vector index
   (FAISS or similar), embeds incoming queries using the same configured model, and returns
   kbexplorer-native results: node IDs, titles, paths, clusters, snippets, scores, and
   graph-aware context.

The repository owns the semantic search corpus; the service only provides query execution.
Embeddings and mapping files are durable, reviewable build outputs tied to the exact
version of the kbexplorer graph.

## Why
Search results should be graph-aware — they know node identity, cluster membership,
hierarchy, authored connections, source citations, and page structure. A query for
"how does audit validation work?" should return the relevant kbexplorer node, its
relationship to nearby concepts, and enough metadata to place the result back into the
graph. This makes semantic search feel native to kbexplorer rather than bolted on.

The design also fits the development workflow: a contributor changes content, runs the
search index builder, commits both content and updated search artifacts. CI verifies
artifact freshness. A hosted service deploys directly from repository state.

## Adopted model / approach
- Separate `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search` npm package in a new repo.
- Consumes `KBNode`/`KBGraph`/`KBConfig` types from kbexplorer-core (or inlined
  initially until kbexplorer-core is published).
- Pluggable embedding providers (OpenAI, local models, configurable).
- Checked-in artifacts are deterministic (sorted keys, no timestamps, content-hash keyed).
- FAISS (via faiss-node or similar) as the default runtime index, but the design does not
  depend solely on a native binary index as the only source of truth.
- Phased delivery: extraction → embedding → artifacts → query engine → CLI → service.

## Scope boundaries
- In: the search module repo, its core types, extraction pipeline, embedding provider
  abstraction, artifact format, query engine, CLI commands, and localhost service mode.
- Out: kbexplorer-template UI integration for search results (future work),
  kbexplorer-core dependency (tracked by sibling Epic in template),
  production hosted service infrastructure (backlog).

## Success definition
A contributor can: (1) point kbexplorer-search at a kbexplorer content directory,
(2) generate deterministic search artifacts, (3) commit them alongside content,
(4) query semantically and receive graph-aware results with node IDs, clusters, and
scores, (5) run a CI drift gate that verifies artifacts match the current graph.

## Children
Features F0–F7 below. Relates to `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` sibling Epic
(CLI command integration).

issues.title: Task: Slot SQLite graph store between providers and engine (cache/incremental)

## Scope
Implement the SQLite store behind a flag: persist provider output, reuse on unchanged
inputs, recompute incrementally. Backlog — schedule after phases 0–6.

## Validation criteria
With the store on, a no-change rebuild hits cache and the resulting graph is

issues.title: Epic: Phase 7 — Graph store / incremental compute (optional)
issues.body:
## What
Slot the already-spec'd SQLite graph store (`spec-graph-store`) between providers and the
engine as an **optional**, flag-gated cache / incremental-recompute layer — now that sources,
engine, providers, and representations are decoupled (Phases 0–6, all merged + live).

## Why
Performance + incremental rebuilds: a no-change rebuild should reuse cache rather than
re-deriving the whole graph. Explicitly **backlog / optional** — it was never on the
decoupling critical path, which is why it is its own Epic rather than a phase Feature.

## Adopted model
A pure `GraphStore` **interface** in `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` (content-hash keyed), a
SQLite-backed implementation in the template behind an **opt-in flag** (default off → zero
behavior change), and an incremental path that invalidates on source/provider/config hash
changes. The store sits providers → [store] → engine; the engine stays pure.

## Scope boundaries
- IN: store contract, SQLite adapter, cache key derivation, incremental reuse/invalidation, golden parity guard.
- OUT: distributed/remote caches, multi-tenant stores, query layers, anything user-visible in the SPA.

## Success definition
With the store enabled, a no-change rebuild reuses cache and the resulting `KBGraph` is
**byte-identical** to the non-store path (Phase 0 goldens unchanged); with the store disabled,
behavior and output are unchanged.

## Children
- F7.1 — `GraphStore` interface + cache-key contract (core)
- F7.2 — SQLite-backed store behind an opt-in flag (template)
- F7.3 — Incremental recompute + golden parity guard

**Blocked by:** Phases 0–6 (Epic E1 #298) — satisfied.

issues.title: Task: Add the neighbor-anchored `llm-context` representation (§4B)
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F6 — Representation registry

## Scope
Implement `llm-context` per §4B: always anchored on one or more context node URIs;
emit each anchor's full content + nearest neighbors ranked by the existing edge-weight
scoring up to a token budget; emit **navigable `kg://` links** for relevant-but-unexpanded
neighbors. Never emit the whole graph. Deterministic Markdown; `maxTokens` bounds only the
neighborhood expansion.

## Validation criteria
Golden test: identical graph + anchor → byte-identical Markdown; output contains
navigable `kg://` links and never the full node set; budget caps expansion (anchors always
present).

## Evidence-based completion criteria
- [ ] Deterministic llm-context golden test green
- [ ] Test: output is anchored (subset of graph) with `kg://` navigation links
- [ ] Test: `maxTokens` bounds expansion while keeping anchors

issues.title: Task: Add the `json-ld` representation from the pure KBGraph
issues.body:
**Parent feature:** F6 — Representation registry

issues.title: Epic: Decouple kbexplorer subsystems & enable pluggable providers/representations
issues.body:
## What
Today the three subsystems — system-of-record + providers, the resource-graph-engine,
and the representation/rendering subsystem — are entangled: two fat loaders duplicate
~150 lines of post-processing, there is no first-class system-of-record abstraction,
3rd-party providers cannot actually load (hardcoded plugin switch), representation
styling is baked into core data types, and the SPA is the only output format. Target: a
clean 4-layer pipeline — **Sources → Providers → Engine (pure `KBGraph`) → Representation
registry** — backed by a shared `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` contracts package, so
authors can bring their own local or 3rd-party providers, sources, and representations
without forking core.

## Why
Extensibility is the headline goal: "people should be able to use this and pull in their
own local or 3rd party providers." Decoupling the subsystems is the prerequisite.

## Adopted model / approach
- Shared contracts live in a **separate repo/package** `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core`.
- **Affordances are per-*retrieval* and situational** (see §4A of the plan): a source
  declares a possible universe; each retrieved resource carries the affordances allowed
  *now* + hypermedia links. Staging area is a first-class linked resource. **Git ≠ GitHub.**
- Provider loading is **local-ES-module-first**, then 3rd-party npm.
- `llm-context` representation is **neighbor-anchored & navigable** — never the whole graph.
- Each phase keeps graph output **byte-identical** until a seam is intentionally flipped.

## Scope boundaries
- In: phases 0–6 in the template (engine/providers/representation are here).
- Out: CLI-side adoption (Epic in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`); optional graph store (F7, backlog);
  the net-new docs+showcase repo content beyond standing it up (Feature: docs).

## Success definition
A third party can register a local ES-module provider and a custom representation via
config, render `--as json-ld|llm-context`, and the self-repo graph is byte-identical to
the Phase-0 golden snapshot at every step until a seam is deliberately flipped.

## Children
Features F0, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5a, F5b, F6, F7, F-docs below.
Relates to `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` sibling Epic (CLI adoption).
