issues.title: Feature H: First-class service + decision kinds (viewers + edge rules)
issues.body:
**Gap H.** A services monorepo's core entities include **services** (repo service → owning team, ServiceTree id, catalog-info path, repo path) and **decisions** (ADRs). Neither has a bespoke kind/viewer today — both fall back to `GenericStructuredView`. The spine kinds in `src/engine/content-model/register.ts` cover person/squad/workstream/mission/priority/cycle/org/team/system-of-record only.

**Decision: build first-class kinds** (not the doc-only fallback path).

### Scope
- Register `service` + `decision` as spine kinds in `register.ts` (open node-type + viewer registries — no core union edits).
- Add `ServiceView` + `DecisionView` in `src/views/viewers/` (className-styled, SSR-safe), bound via `registerContentModelTypes()`.
- Add edge rules in `content-model/schema/edges.yaml`:
  - `service` `owned-by` → team; `service` `tracked-in` → system-of-record.
  - `decision` `decided-by` → person; `decision` `affects` → workstream/mission.
- Add example entity files under `content-model/services/` and `content-model/decisions/`, plus conventions/lifecycle entries.
- Viewer-registry + spine-viewer unit tests.

### Acceptance
- A `service` node renders ownership + a ServiceTree/catalog link.
- A `decision` node renders deciders + context.
- Achieved without core edits (per the open node-type registry); all FK edges resolve and pass `validate`/`derive --check`.

_Implementation targets `main`. Part of the kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness epic (#273)._

issues.title: Feature C: Navigable people / org-chart (PersonView links + reports-to tree layout)
issues.body:
**Gap C (top template priority for our adoption).** kbexplorer has a `person` kind, `reports-to`/`leads` edges and a `PersonView`, but the people/org-chart experience is bring-your-own: `PersonView` renders `manager`/`reports-to` as **plain text**, and there is **no reports-to tree layout** for navigating a hundreds-person org.

The `person-manager → reports-to` foreign-key edge already exists in `content-model/schema/edges.yaml`, so this is primarily **view-layer** work plus a documented contract for feeding person descriptors from an external (MS Graph) pipeline.

### Sub-tasks
- **C1** — make `PersonView` `manager` / `team` / `reports-to` **navigable graph links** (reuse the existing `NodeLink` pattern; resolve target to the person node id/URN).
- **C2** — add a **reports-to tree layout** that scales to a hundreds-person org.
- **C3** — document the supported **BYO person-descriptor / derived-JSON-LD** feed contract so an external pipeline can supply `person` nodes that pass validation.

### Acceptance
- A hundreds-person org renders as a navigable reports-to tree.
- `PersonView` reporting line is clickable and opens the manager's node.
- Reorg/provenance feeding is documented against a stable, validated contract.

_Implementation targets `main`. Part of the kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness epic (#273)._

issues.title: Epic: kbexplorer-template adoption-readiness for gaming-microsoft/personalization
issues.body:
Tracking epic for the **template-side** changes needed to adopt kbexplorer as the org-knowledge foundation in the EMU services monorepo `gaming-microsoft/personalization`.

Source: the consolidated adoption-gaps draft (gaps A–H). This epic covers only the **[template]**-tagged gaps — **B, C, E, F, H**. CLI-only gaps (A `validate`, D `init --yes`, G EMU CI recipe) live in `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` and are referenced only as cross-repo blockers.

### Reconciliation against current `main` (the gaps doc is partly stale)
- **B — content-model schema files & vocabulary**: now **largely shipped** on `main` (`content-model/` tree at repo root: `teamops.yaml`, `schema/{conventions,edges,lifecycle}.yaml`, `index/context.jsonld`, `index/vocabulary.jsonld`, entity files; plus `docs/work-graph-vocabulary.md`). Remaining template work is verify-and-close; the `init --content-model` scaffolder is CLI-side.
- **C — navigable people / org-chart**: **OPEN**. `PersonView` renders `manager`/`reports-to` as plain text; no reports-to tree layout. The `person-manager → reports-to` FK edge already exists in `schema/edges.yaml`, so this is view-layer work.
- **E — release tags / version**: **OPEN/partial**. Template `package.json` is still `0.0.0`; only a single repo tag `v0.1.0` exists.
- **F — host-root in vendored installs**: tracked by **#220**. `detectHostRoot()` exists but fails for vendored layouts; land an env/config-driven mechanism.
- **H — `service` + `decision` kinds**: **OPEN**. Not registered (`register.ts` has person/squad/workstream/mission/priority/cycle/org/team/system-of-record only); no `service`/`decision` viewers or edge rules. Decision: build first-class kinds.

### Children
- Feature C — navigable people/org-chart (sub-tasks C1 PersonView links, C2 reports-to tree layout, C3 BYO person-feed contract docs)
- Feature H — first-class `service` + `decision` kinds (viewers + edge rules)
- Feature F — config/env-driven host-root (**#220**)
- Task E — version bump + tagged release + CLI↔template compatibility matrix
- Task B — verify content-model schema-config satisfies the template side; close residual

_Implementation targets `main`. Filed to coordinate ahead of adoption in `gaming-microsoft/personalization`._

issues.title: Remove unused gray-matter dependency (js-yaml Moderate advisory)
issues.body:
`gray-matter` (a direct dependency) bundles `js-yaml@3.14.2`, which is flagged by [GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68) — a Moderate quadratic-complexity DoS. There is no patched 3.x release (everything <= 4.1.1 is vulnerable).

`gray-matter` is not imported anywhere in the codebase, and `yaml`@^2 is already a dependency for any future frontmatter parsing. Removing `gray-matter` eliminates the transitive `js-yaml` 3.x and clears the advisory.

issues.title: Wire the full-loop scenario (layer 4) into a nightly CI job
issues.body:
**Gap surfaced while writing `TESTING.md` (#258).**

Layer 4 of the test pyramid — the full-loop scenario (`e2e/full-loop/actor-regen-render.spec.ts`, run via `npm run test:e2e:full-loop` / `playwright.full-loop.config.ts`) — currently runs **only manually/locally**. No scheduled workflow invokes it:

- `dtu-gitea.yml` (nightly 04:30 UTC) runs only `npm run test:e2e:gitea` (layer 3).
- `visual-regression.yml` and `explore-dtu.yml` cover layers 5 and 6.

So the full-loop never executes in CI, and regressions in the actor→twin→CLI-regen→app-render→verify path would not be caught nightly.

### Options
1. Extend `dtu-gitea.yml` to also run `npm run test:e2e:full-loop` after the gitea suite (shares the Podman bringup; cheapest).
2. Add a dedicated nightly workflow for the full-loop.

Option 1 is likely simplest since the substrate/bringup overlaps. Note the full-loop's default substrate is `static` (`FULL_LOOP_SUBSTRATE=static`); the live-Gitea substrate is still deferred, so wiring it nightly may also be a good moment to wire the gitea substrate.

`TESTING.md` documents this as "tracked separately" and points here.

Part of the testing system established in epic #254.

issues.title: Remote/runtime mode does not ingest the content-model (work-graph nodes absent without a CLI manifest)
issues.body:
Surfaced by the work-graph DTU scenarios (#256 / PR #264).

`loadRemoteKnowledgeBase()` (src/engine/remote-loader.ts) registers `new ContentModelProvider(null)` — a no-op — so in **remote/runtime mode** the content-model (work-graph vocabulary: team/workstream/priority/person/system-of-record from #232) is **not fetched or rendered**. Those nodes only appear in **local-manifest mode** (the CLI writes them into the manifest).

Impact: a runtime-mode deployment (app fetching live from GitHub in-browser, no CLI-built manifest) shows issues/PRs/releases but NOT the organizational layer. Two `.fixme` specs in e2e/gitea/workgraph-mutations.spec.ts document this and can be un-fixme'd when the remote fetch path lands.

Fix: implement a remote content-model fetch (read content-model/ files from the repo via the GitHub API / adapter) and pass a populated `ContentModelProvider` in the remote loader, mirroring the local loader. Relates to the work-graph epic #232.

issues.title: Exploratory-agent harness: scheduled agent sessions probe the DTU and open spec PRs
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. Formalize the README's exploratory-agent playbook into a runnable/scheduled harness: bring the DTU up, launch agent session(s) with the probing prompt, have them mutate via actors, find gaps, and open human-reviewed e2e/gitea spec PRs (never auto-committed; assertions in specs, never twins). A workflow_dispatch + nightly entry point that the orchestrator can fire.

issues.title: TESTING.md: the test pyramid + CI orchestration + holdout discipline
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. A single TESTING.md (superseding/linking DTU.md) defining the whole pyramid: unit (vitest/node:test) -> static-twin fast e2e (PR gate) -> live-DTU scenarios (nightly) -> full-loop (nightly) -> visual regression -> exploratory-agent. For each layer: what it covers, what twin it uses, where it runs (PR vs nightly vs manual), and the holdout rule. Reconcile the two repos' CI so the split is explicit and consistent.

issues.title: Visual-regression gate: capture-review baseline diff per theme × surface
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. Turn the capture-review harness (scripts/capture-review.mjs + BEAUTY.md) into a regression gate: maintain committed baseline screenshots (or hashes/SSIM) per surface x theme, diff new captures against them, fail on meaningful drift, and surface a visual report artifact. Optionally drive captures from twin states so visual + data are tested together. Defines what's a PR gate vs nightly.

issues.title: Work-graph DTU scenarios: team/workstream/release mutations reflected on refresh
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. Extend the live-twin scenario suite (e2e/gitea/) beyond issues/PRs to the org layer shipped in #232: an actor edits content-model/teams/*.yaml or workstreams/*.yaml (via the edit-source actor) or cuts a release, and the app reflects the new/changed team, workstream, release, or person node on refresh. New actors as needed (e.g. cut-release). Assertions in specs only.

issues.title: Full-loop deployment scenario: actor → twin → CLI regen → app render → verify
issues.body: Part of the comprehensive testing epic. The single scenario that exercises the real deployment shape end-to-end: a DTU actor mutates the Gitea twin (open issue / cut release / edit team.yaml), the CLI regenerates the manifest **from the twin** (depends on the CLI↔DTU seam, cli repo), the app builds+renders that manifest, and a verify step asserts the mutation is reflected. Lives in e2e/gitea/ (or a new e2e/full-loop/) under the holdout rule. Depends on the CLI↔DTU seam.

issues.title: Epic: Comprehensive testing system — DTU spine across CLI, app, and visual surfaces
issues.body:
## Why

The DTU foundation is live on main: a static GitHub fixture twin (`twins/github/`, the fast PR gate) and a stateful Gitea live twin (`twins/gitea/`, Podman + GitHub→Gitea proxy on `VITE_GH_API_BASE`, scripted actors, nightly). `DTU.md` states the ambition: **local behavioral clones of every external service**, with the **holdout rule** (specs are the holdout set; never code to them).

Today that spine only validates the **app** (browser, remote mode). The **CLI** pipeline (`init/generate/derive/manifest/build`) shells out to `gh` directly and is tested only by unit injection + the static mock — never against the live, mutating twin. There is no **full-loop** test (twin mutates → CLI regenerates → app renders → verify), and the project's other external dependencies — **agent runtimes** (copilot/claude) and **MCP servers** (ADO, SharePoint) — have no twins at all, despite being the backbone of the local-first regeneration the work-repo deployment depends on.

## Outcome

A test pyramid where every external service has a twin and every surface (CLI, app, visual) is exercised against it — the same way a real deployment runs — with a clear PR-gate vs nightly vs exploratory split, all under the holdout discipline.

## The matrix (service × surface)

| Service \ Surface | Unit | App e2e | CLI pipeline | Full loop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub | ✅ | ✅ static + ✅ live Gitea | 🔴 (no twin path) | 🔴 |
| Agent runtime (copilot/claude) | ✅ inject | n/a | 🔴 twin | 🔴 |
| MCP (ADO/SharePoint) | 🔴 | n/a | 🔴 twin | 🔴 |

## Layers (sub-issues)
1. **CLI ↔ DTU seam** [cli] — configurable GitHub API base/auth so the CLI fetches from the Gitea adapter (hermetic) AND a GHE host (real enterprise). Keystone; unblocks the dress rehearsal (cli #56) and the real deployment.
2. **Full-loop deployment scenario** — actor mutates twin → CLI regenerates manifest from twin → app renders it → verify reflects the mutation. The end-to-end the real deployment IS.
3. **Work-graph DTU scenarios** — actor edits team.yaml/workstream.yaml or cuts a release → app reflects the new team/release node on refresh (extends issue-lifecycle/pr-and-merge to the org layer shipped in #232).
4. **Agent-runtime twin** [cli] — deterministic fake agent CLI so derive/generate fuzzy paths run hermetically in full-pipeline tests, not just unit injection.
5. **MCP server twins** [cli] — fake ADO board + SharePoint-docs MCP servers so MCP-preflight + derive against work-item/doc sources are exercised hermetically (the work-repo deployment's real dependencies).
6. **Visual-regression gate** — wire capture-review + BEAUTY.md into a baseline-diff check (per theme × surface), tied to twin states; catch visual regressions.
7. **TESTING.md — the pyramid + CI orchestration** — formalize what runs on PR (unit + static-twin fast gate) vs nightly (live DTU + full-loop + visual) vs exploratory; codify the holdout discipline across all twins.
8. **Exploratory-agent harness** — formalize the playbook: a scheduled/triggerable job that launches agent sessions against a running DTU to probe edge cases and open spec PRs (human-reviewed; assertions in specs, never in twins).

CLI-side layers (1, 4, 5) are tracked as issues in anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli and linked here.

issues.title: Constellation legibility: orphan ring, unreadable labels at default zoom, duplicated legend
issues.body: Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 4, Graph: 2). Disconnected nodes ring the layout like noise (orphan ring); node labels are unreadable at default zoom; the in-canvas cluster legend duplicates the HUD cluster list. Explore: orphan shelf/cluster gutter instead of scatter, label LOD tied to zoom + degree, single source of truth for the legend. Relates to #53 (WebGL renderer) and #39 (rich graph views).

issues.title: Placeholder MAP minimap box renders empty on every reading surface
issues.body: Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 3, States: 2). The bottom-left minimap region renders as an empty bordered box labeled MAP on every reading/overview capture. Render the minimap content, lazy-render with a designed loading state, or remove the box until it has content. Principle 5: no placeholder ships.

issues.title: Theme-invariant accents: node icons and source badge keep dark palette on sepia/light
issues.body: Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 2, Theme: 2 / Color: 2). Cluster-colored node icons, the related-rail icons, and the 'Authored - <file>' source badge do not re-ramp per theme: on sepia the pale-blue badge on cream paper falls below readable contrast and the cold accents break the paper-and-ink treatment. Acceptance: per-theme accent ramps (or token-driven recolor) for node icons, rail icons, and badges; AA contrast verified on all three themes.

issues.title: Mobile HUD collapse failure: controls overlap title bar at 390px
issues.body:
Standard-of-beauty wave-1 finding (#239, BEAUTY.md SS4 finding 1, Responsive: 1). At 390x844 the bottom-dock controls (Theme/Dock/Aa/Width) overlap the node-title bar, the MAP button truncates at the left edge, and the RELATED rail collides with the controls panel. The HUD needs a mobile reflow: collapse to a single rail with expand-on-demand, or stack controls behind a sheet. Acceptance: no overlap/truncation at 390x844 in 
pm run capture:review output; touch targets >=40px.

issues.title: BEAUTY.md: the experiential quality standard, rubric, and wave-1 assessment
issues.body: Part of the standard-of-beauty epic #239. Deliverable: BEAUTY.md — principles, 0-4 scoring rubric across seven dimensions, review protocol (capture -> frontier-model image review -> scored assessment -> remediation issues), and the wave-1 assessment. Lands with the capture script PR.

issues.title: Bump uuid to 13.0.1 to fix Dependabot alert #7 (CVE-2026-41907)
issues.body:
## Summary

Dependabot alert [#7](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/security/dependabot/7) (moderate severity) flags `uuid@13.0.0` in `package-lock.json` — [GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq) / CVE-2026-41907: missing buffer bounds check in `v3()`/`v5()`/`v6()` when a caller-provided `buf` is passed, allowing silent partial writes (CWE-787).

`uuid` is a transitive (peer) dependency of `vis-data`/`vis-network`. First patched version: **13.0.1**, which is within the existing `^13.0.0` peer range, so this is a lockfile-only bump.

## Plan

- Bump `uuid` to 13.0.1 in `package-lock.json` (`npm update uuid`)
- Run `npm test` and the build to confirm nothing breaks
- PR closes this issue and resolves the alert

issues.title: Canonical review screenshot capture across views, themes, and states
issues.body:
Part of the standard-of-beauty epic.

## What

A reproducible capture script (Playwright, building on the repo's existing visual-test machinery) that produces the canonical review surface set:

- Views: home/landing, constellation graph, reading view (long-form node), card grid/overview, HUD expanded + collapsed + docked variants, search palette (once it exists), source editor dialog.
- Themes: dark, light, sepia (+ at least one config-defined brand theme).
- States: cold load, node selected w/ neighborhood emphasis, cluster collapsed, detail-slider extremes.
- Output: `review/screenshots/<view>--<theme>--<state>.png` at 1440×900 and 390×844 (mobile), deterministic naming, one command (`npm run capture:review`).

These are review artifacts (gitignored or CI artifacts), not committed fixtures. The set definition lives in a small manifest file so the beauty review can enumerate coverage.

issues.title: Epic: Standard of beauty — agentic design review + experiential quality bar
issues.body:
## Why

kbexplorer's structural quality has gates (graph validation, assessment scoring, link health). Its **experiential quality has none** — nothing assesses whether the thing is beautiful: typography rhythm, color and contrast across themes, motion, graph readability, information hierarchy, the feel of moving resource-to-resource. For a sensemaking tool, beauty is not cosmetic; it is load-bearing — visual clarity IS comprehension.

This epic establishes a **standard of beauty**: an explicit, opinionated quality bar, an agentic review process that assesses the real rendered product against it (screenshots, not source), and a stream of driven improvements.

## Scope (sub-issues)
1. **Canonical screenshot capture** — reproducible script capturing the agreed surface set (all views × all themes × key states) for review input.
2. **BEAUTY.md — the standard** — the written bar: principles, per-surface criteria, scoring rubric, and the review protocol. Authored from an actual frontier-model design review of the captured surfaces, not invented in the abstract.
3. **Remediation wave 1** — issues filed from the first assessment, worked through the normal pipeline.

The standard then becomes a recurring gate: future UI PRs cite it, and periodic re-assessment keeps drift visible.

issues.title: Landing mode config: reading-first with collapsed graph
issues.body:
Part of the reader-first UX epic (Phase 2).

## What

A config-selectable landing experience that leads with content, not the constellation:

```yaml
# config.yaml
landing:
  view: reading        # reading | overview | graph (default today: graph/home)
  node: <id>           # optional: a specific node (e.g. the team home page); default = README/home node
  graph: collapsed     # HUD starts collapsed to its rail; one click expands
```

## Deliverables
- Config schema + wiring: initial route + HUD initial state honor the block; user preference (localStorage) wins after first interaction.
- The graph remains one gesture away: collapsed HUD shows the rail with the search button and an expand affordance.
- Deep links still work (hash routes unchanged).
- Tests: config parsing, initial-state logic, an E2E for "lands on reading view with collapsed HUD".

issues.title: Search: build-time index + HUD search button + Ctrl-K palette
issues.body:
Part of the reader-first UX epic (Phase 2). The single most-requested missing affordance: there is no search anywhere in kbexplorer.

## What

Client-side search over all nodes, served from a build-time index — no backend, consistent with the static secret-free architecture.

## Deliverables
- **Index**: built into the manifest (or a sibling `search-index.json`) at generate/build time — id, title, type, cluster, headings, body text (tokenized/trimmed). Runtime mode falls back to indexing loaded nodes in-memory. Use a tiny client lib (minisearch or comparable, license-compatible) or hand-rolled inverted index — justify the choice in the PR.
- **UI**: a search button in the HUD + global Ctrl-K (and `/`) command palette: type → ranked results (title match > heading > body) with type/cluster badges → Enter navigates to the node in reading view; arrow keys navigate results. Fluent v9 components, all three themes, keyboard-trap-free, accessible (combobox/listbox semantics).
- Works in both local-manifest and runtime-GitHub modes.
- E2E coverage (Playwright) for open-search→type→navigate, plus unit tests for ranking.
- Result cap + perf budget: index build adds <2s to build; palette opens <100ms on a 500-node graph.

issues.title: Epic: Reader-first UX — search + content-first landing
issues.body:
## Why (Phase 2 of the work-repo deployment)

Feedback and the target UX agree: the graph must not be in people's faces. People should land on content, navigate resource-to-resource, and reach for the graph (collapsed at the side) and search when they need them. Search does not exist at all today.

## Scope (sub-issues)
1. **Search** — build-time index in the manifest + HUD search button + Ctrl-K command palette.
2. **Landing mode** — config to make reading view the landing experience with the graph collapsed into the HUD by default.

issues.title: Person nodes: first-class people aggregating their active work
issues.body:
Part of the work-graph vocabulary epic (Phase 1).

## What

People as first-class nodes. Today authors/assignees are strings on issue/PR nodes; coworker visibility ("what is Adwoa working on?") needs a person node aggregating: authored/assigned open PRs and issues, team membership (from team.yaml), and recent activity.

## Deliverables
- `person` node type; identity = GitHub login, displayName overridable by content-model person files.
- Derived edges: person → assigned/authored issues & PRs (from existing work data — no new API calls), person → team (when descriptors exist).
- Synthesis rule: person nodes materialize when (a) a person descriptor exists, or (b) login appears as author/assignee on ≥1 active item — keep the graph from exploding with drive-by contributors (threshold/config).
- OrgChart provider enrichment optional, not required.
- Reading view: a person page listing their active work as navigable links.
- Tests.

issues.title: Release nodes: node type, edges to shipped PRs/issues, reading view
issues.body:
Part of the work-graph vocabulary epic (Phase 1). Companion to the kbexplorer-cli release-ingestion feature.

## What

Release nodes in the graph: each GitHub release becomes a node (tag, name, date, notes summary) with edges to the PRs/issues it shipped (parsed from release notes references) and to the repository node.

## Deliverables
- `release` node type in the engine (types, WorkProvider or new provider path) consuming releases from the manifest (CLI side ingests via `gh release list` — see the cli issue) and from the GitHub API in runtime mode.
- Edges: release → repository; release → referenced PRs/issues (#N parsing, same approach as issue cross-references).
- Reading view renders release notes markdown; cluster/visual defaults ("Releases" lane).
- Layer filtering: releases belong to the Work view.
- Tests per existing provider test patterns.

issues.title: Work-graph entity schema: team/workstream/priority/person/system-of-record descriptors
issues.body:
Part of the work-graph vocabulary epic (Phase 1).

## What

Define and implement the YAML descriptor schema for organizational entities in the content-model engine (F2): `team`, `workstream`, `priority`, `person`, `system-of-record`.

## Deliverables

- **Schema proposal first**: a `docs/work-graph-vocabulary.md` (or content-model schema addition) PR with the YAML shapes + example files, reviewed before implementation. Example direction:

```yaml
# content-model/teams/graph-platform.yaml
kind: team
id: graph-platform
name: Graph Platform
members: [adwoa, kwame]
workstreams: [kb-explorer]
```

```yaml
# content-model/workstreams/kb-explorer.yaml
kind: workstream
id: kb-explorer
name: KB Explorer
priority: p1
team: graph-platform
systems-of-record:
  - { name: "ADO board", url: "https://..." }
```

- Content-model builder support: these kinds produce nodes + derived edges (member-of, owns, has-priority, tracked-in), with the same source-of-truth editability PR #205 gave entity files (the `sourceFile` affordance should light up on them).
- Validation with actionable errors (unknown kind, dangling references) surfaced through the existing graph-validation gate.
- Cluster/visual defaults so the organizational layer reads as its own region of the graph.
- Hermetic tests following the content-model builder test patterns.

## Non-goals
Release ingestion (separate sub-issue), live person-activity aggregation (person nodes sub-issue).

issues.title: Epic: Work-graph vocabulary — teams, workstreams, priorities, releases, people
issues.body:
## Why (Phase 1 of the work-repo deployment)

The target deployment is a work repository where people need sensemaking over **active PRs, work items, releases, workstreams, priorities, and what coworkers are doing**. Issues/PRs/commits/branches already ingest, but the *organizational layer* — the thing that turns repo activity into a navigable map of work — has no vocabulary: no team, workstream, priority, release, person, or system-of-record node types.

The F2 content-model pipeline (schema-driven YAML/JSON entity files under `content-model/`, Epic #147) is exactly the right substrate. The host work repo will enforce consistency with YAML descriptor files; those descriptors ARE the contract this epic defines.

## Outcome

Drop `team.yaml` / `workstream.yaml` / release data into a repo and the graph grows an organizational layer: a workstream node links to its priority, its team, its active PRs and issues, its releases; a person node aggregates their authored/assigned work. Resource-first navigation works across it (click a teammate → their workstream → its open PRs).

## Scope (sub-issues)

1. **Work-graph entity schema** — YAML descriptor shapes for `team`, `workstream`, `priority`, `person`, `system-of-record` in the content-model engine, with derived edges (member-of, owns, prioritized-as, tracked-in).
2. **Release nodes** — ingestion in kbexplorer-cli (`gh release list` → manifest) + release node type + edges to PRs/tags here.
3. **Person nodes** — promote people from author/assignee strings to first-class nodes aggregating their active work, optionally enriched by the existing OrgChart provider.

Design constraint: schema-first. The descriptor shapes must be reviewable by humans, enforceable in the host repo, and stable across template upgrades (coordinate with kbexplorer-cli#42 capability/protocol work).

issues.title: Docs: mention the HUD theme palette chooser alongside the `t` shortcut
issues.body: Following the new HUD theme palette chooser (#221 / PR #222), several content docs still describe theme switching as `t`-cycle only. Update the theming/getting-started/HUD docs to mention the palette menu so users discover the clickable chooser.

issues.title: Add a visible theme chooser (palette menu) to the HUD
issues.body:
The dynamic theme system (built-in dark/light/sepia plus config `theme.themes`, external-file themes, and JS-module themes) is currently only reachable through the `t` keyboard shortcut. The HUD exposes just three hardcoded dark/light/sepia buttons, so named/custom themes have no visible affordance and users don't discover them.

**Ask:** add a clickable theme chooser — a paint-palette icon in the HUD that opens a menu listing every available theme, with the active one indicated, persisting the choice to `kbe-theme`.

issues.title: scripts/generate-manifest.js ignores VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT in vendored installs
issues.body:
## Repro

In a host repo using `kbexplorer init --vendor` (so `.kbexplorer/` lives one level deep inside the host, not as a git submodule):

`
node .kbexplorer/scripts/generate-manifest.js
`

writes a manifest containing the **template's stock content** (37 files starting with `content/app-shell.md`, README `# kbexplorer-template`) rather than the host repo's authored content.

## Cause

`detectHostRoot()` resolves `kbRoot/../..`, which only works for git-submodule layouts (where `.kbexplorer` is two levels deep). In vendored mode that path lands **above** the host repo, the lookup fails, and the script falls back to treating `kbRoot` as the host.

The companion CLI (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`) already passes `VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT=<host>` via env on dev/build, but this script never reads it.

## Suggested fix

At the top of the script:

`js
const hostRoot = process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT
  ? resolve(process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT)
  : detectHostRoot();
`

Falls back to existing behavior for standalone use; honors the explicit env var when the CLI provides it.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, `kbexplorer dev` in a vendored install renders the template's own knowledge base instead of the user's. Discovered while dogfooding kbexplorer on the CLI repo itself.

issues.title: Epic: External theme & branding customization (no submodule edits)
issues.body:
## What
kbexplorer themes are hardcoded in the `.kbexplorer` submodule
(`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`: `THEME_MAP` / `MODES` / the sepia `createLightTheme`
build). Move customization OUT of the submodule so host repos can restyle
colors, fonts, per-page/per-cluster accents, logos, and favicons — primarily via
the `config.yaml` that `parser.ts → loadConfig()` already fetches from the host
repo at runtime.

## Why
Today any restyle requires editing the submodule. Two `theme` fields
(`theme.default`, `theme.font.*`) are already declared in the type +
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` but nothing reads them — the promise exists but is unwired.

## Adopted model / approach
- Transport: `config.yaml theme:` (Option A) is the backbone; dedicated theme
  files (B), raw CSS (C) and JS module (D) are later substitutes/escape hatches.
- Scope axis: global → per-cluster → per-page, always as TOKEN DELTAS layered on
  the active base theme (dark/light/sepia) — never a full theme replacement, so
  the global theme switcher keeps working.
- Assets (logos/favicons) are orthogonal URL refs resolved through the existing
  `resolveImageUrl(source, …)` host-repo path.
- Start simple and grow: 5 phases, each shippable independently.

## Scope boundaries
- In: F1–F5 below (config schema, dynamic theme build, branding assets, scope
  layer, modularization).
- Out: redesigning the visual system / node renderer; theming the vis-network
  canvas internals beyond existing `isDark` usage.

## Success definition
A host repo can change global colors+fonts, set a logo and favicon, and accent
specific clusters/pages from its own `config.yaml` (+ optional assets), with NO
edits to the `.kbexplorer` submodule, verified live via Playwright.

## Children
Features F1–F5 below.

issues.title: F10 — Knowledge-base content refresh for the new node-type engine
issues.body:
## What
Refresh the kbexplorer **authored knowledge-base content** (`content/*.md`) so it documents the open, data-driven node-type engine and **all** the new node types now in the graph. Today only `content/node-types.md` (F1 foundation) is current; the content-model ingestion pipeline (F2), the `.github` structural nodes (F3), the content-model **spine viewers** (Person / Squad / Workstream / Mission / Priority / Cycle / Org), and the new **skill** node type are undocumented in the wiki.

## Why
The wiki is itself a kbexplorer graph; it should reflect the system it ships. New contributors — and the graph's own self-description — currently can't discover how nodes are typed, ingested, or rendered. The engine code, tests, and a sample `content-model/` exist; the authored content has not caught up.

## Scope (pages)
- [ ] **content-model-ingestion.md** — the 5-pass `ContentModelProvider` (schema reader -> discovery -> node emission -> edge resolution -> assembly), `@type`-driven kind (never path), URN/CURIE resolution, safe no-op behavior, and the build wiring (`generate-manifest.js` -> `manifest.contentModel`).
- [ ] **structural-nodes.md** — `StructuralProvider`: `.github` workflows / actions / issue+PR templates / CODEOWNERS / dependabot / funding **plus the new `skill` (`SKILL.md`) node**, each linked to the `repo-meta` repository node via `structural` edges; the bespoke viewers (WorkflowView / ActionView / SkillView / GenericStructuredView).
- [ ] **Update `node-types.md` + `ui-node-types.md`** — enumerate the full registry: person, squad, workstream, mission, priority, cycle, org, workflow, github-action, skill, dependabot/funding/codeowners/templates. Explain the viewer registry keyed by `@type` and the open `NodeSource`/`DisplayMode` unions.
- [ ] Wire `connections:` frontmatter so the new pages join the **engine** cluster graph (no orphan nodes; every node within 3 hops of the hub).
- [ ] A short **sample content-model** note pointing at the committed `content-model/` starter directory.

## Approach
Use the kb content pipeline (`/kb:generate` -> kb-architect -> kb-writer) or author directly. Keep frontmatter native (id/title/emoji/cluster/connections). Dark-mode Mermaid for the pipeline diagrams.

## Acceptance / Evidence
- New pages render as nodes in the running app (local mode), within 3 hops of the hub, no orphans (`npm run validate` passes).
- Screenshots of the `content-model-ingestion` and `structural-nodes` pages rendered through the reading view.
- `tsc -b` = 0, `npm run lint` = 0 errors, `vitest` green, `vite build` green.

---
Relates to Epic #147 (E1). Follows F1 #148 / F2 #149 / F3 #150. The `skill` node type + a sample `content-model/` landed on branch `hoopsomuah/explore-node-types`.

issues.title: Bug: Baseline tsc/lint debt on main (blocks release readiness)
issues.body:
## What
`tsc -b` and `npm run lint` are RED on `main` (pre-existing, NOT introduced by recent work). Discovered during F1 (#148 / PR #171): ~52 `tsc` errors and ~40 lint errors across **untouched** files (unused imports, `enum`/`erasableSyntaxOnly`, missing `@types/node` in the test tsconfig, etc.).

## Why
F4 (#151) is "Integration validation & **release readiness**." A repo whose typecheck and lint gates are red cannot honestly claim release readiness, and every downstream Feature (F2/F3) inherits a red baseline, making "is it my change or pre-existing?" triage harder. This is real debt that should be burned down on a `main` that already includes the F1 foundation.

## Scope
- Make `npx tsc -b` exit 0 across the repo (fix or correctly suppress the ~52 errors; add `@types/node` to the test tsconfig if that is the right fix).
- Make `npm run lint` exit 0 (~40 errors: unused imports, enum/erasableSyntaxOnly, etc.).
- Do NOT change runtime behavior; this is hygiene only.

## Validation
- `npx tsc -b` exits 0.
- `npm run lint` exits 0.
- `npm test` (vitest) and `npx vite build` remain green (no regressions).

## Evidence
- Paste before/after error counts for both `tsc -b` and `lint`.
- CI `test` check green on the PR.

Relates to PR #171. Blocks F4 (#151).

pullRequests.title: refactor(engine): rename node-map to structured-node-map to resolve naming collision
pullRequests.body:
## Problem
The engine had two visually-confusable subsystems:
- `nodemap.ts` / `nodemap.yaml` (no hyphen, #41) — maps repo files/dirs/globs → file/content `KBNode`s.
- `node-map.ts` / `node-map.yaml` (hyphenated, F3/#166) — maps structured config files (JSON/YAML) → typed JSON-LD `KBNode`s.

Both were already distinguished elsewhere in the code via `StructuredNodeMap`/`structuredNodeMapRaw`/`parseStructuredNodeMap`, but the newer subsystem's **file names** and its `applyNodeMap` function still lagged behind that convention — hence the confusion.

## Fix
Renamed the newer (F3/#166) subsystem to match its existing naming convention:
- `node-map.yaml` → `structured-node-map.yaml`
- `src/engine/node-map.ts` → `src/engine/structured-node-map.ts`
- `src/engine/__tests__/node-map.test.ts` → `src/engine/__tests__/structured-node-map.test.ts`
- `applyNodeMap` → `applyStructuredNodeMap`

Updated every import/call site (`structural-provider.ts`, `engine/index.ts`, `generate-manifest.js`, `github-api-source.ts`, `build-remote-fixture.mjs`), fixed loose prose that ambiguously said "node-map" when referring to the *other* (`nodemap.ts`) subsystem (`repo-data.ts`, `docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md`), and clarified the content docs (`structural-nodes.md`, `node-mapping.md`) that previously cross-linked the two subsystems without disambiguation.

Bumped `CACHE_VERSION` 38 → 39 since the remote-mode fetch path for the structured node map config changed (`node-map.yaml` → `structured-node-map.yaml`), invalidating previously-cached `structuredNodeMapRaw` values.

Left the `nodemap.ts`/`nodemap.yaml` subsystem (#41) and its type names (`NodeMap`, `NodeMapEntry`) untouched — it's the older, established, widely-documented system. Also left `NodeMapRule`/`NodeMapEdgeRule` type names as-is (no collision).

Historical GitHub issue/PR body text baked into golden test fixtures (`tests/golden/**`) still quotes the old `node-map.ts`/`node-map.yaml` names by design — that's a simulated historical record and was intentionally left untouched.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run` — 96 test files / 1051 tests pass

Same for `trace`'s path: each hop is looked up against `graph.nodes` for its title. ### What this PR adds 1. **`expand`**: an unknown id (the tracked, non-blocking `kbexplorer-cli#216` server↔client id-space seam) now logs **one dev-console warning** before being skipped, instead of a silent no-op — so the gap is visible without breaking anything. Doc comments (module-level + `mergeForcedExpansion`) updated to describe the id-resolution contract explicitly. ### Verification - `npx tsc -b` — clean - `npx eslint .` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings only) - `npx vitest run` — 1051/1051 unit tests pass (1049 + 2 new) - `VITE_KB_LOCAL=true npx vite build` + `npx playwright test --project=chromium` — 93/93 e2e pass, including `no console errors on key pages` (the new warnings only fire on genuinely-unknown ids, which don't occur in the app's normal e2e flows) Refs #409. pullRequests.title: Fix NodeIntentBar reset: lint-clean, race-free redesign (follow-up to #410)
pullRequests.body:
## Follow-up to #410 / #459

`kbexplorer-template#459` merged to `main` before a lint issue in its review-thread fix could be addressed on that branch (the branch was deleted at merge). This PR fixes it as a follow-up against `main`.

### The bug this replaces

The version merged in #459 fixed `NodeIntentBar`'s stale per-node state (Devin thread) by resetting state inside a `useEffect`:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  nodeIdRef.current = nodeId;
  setStates({});
}, [nodeId]);
```

This is **functionally correct** (verified: e2e regression test passes) but trips this repo's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` ESLint rule (verified directly: `npx eslint src/representation/targets/copilot-home/NodeIntentBar.tsx` → 1 error). Note: **lint is not part of CI in this repo** (no lint step in any workflow), which is why the PR merged green despite the error — `npx eslint .` only surfaces it locally.

### The fix

Moved the reset to render time (matching the `EmbeddableApp.tsx` `prevLoadedGraph` idiom already used elsewhere in this codebase), which resolves the lint error. That in turn ruled out the ref-based staleness guard (`nodeIdRef.current !== issuedFor`), because writing a ref's `.current` during render trips a *second* lint rule (`react-hooks/refs`, "Cannot access refs during render"). Splitting the ref update into its own effect avoids both rules but reopens a real (if narrow) race: the ref-update effect commits *after* paint, so a stale async response landing in the gap between the render-time reset and the effect flush could pass the staleness check and repaint an already-reset (idle) entry with no further correction.

Final design needs no ref or effect for the guard at all: each per-action state entry is tagged with the `nodeId` it was issued for (`Record<string, {status, nodeId}>`). The staleness check moves into the `postChatIntent(...).then()` callback's own **functional** `setStates` updater, comparing `prev[action.id]?.nodeId` against the `nodeId` captured at click time. React guarantees `prev` is never stale in a functional updater, so this is provably race-free without a ref. The render-time `nodeId` change still does `setStates({})` to clear all entries, which naturally invalidates any in-flight request for the old node (`prev[action.id]` becomes `undefined` post-reset, so the `nodeId` comparison always fails).

### Verification

- `npx tsc -b` — clean
- `npx eslint .` — **0 errors** (3 pre-existing warnings only, unrelated to this file)
- `npx vitest run` — 1049/1049 unit tests pass
- `VITE_KB_LOCAL=true npx vite build` + `npx playwright test --project=chromium` — **93/93 e2e pass**, including the existing `e2e/node-intent-bar.spec.ts` "per-node intent state resets when the panel re-anchors" regression test (unmodified, still on `main` from #459)
- **Adversarial check**: `git stash`'d this fix to temporarily restore the merged (buggy-lint) version, re-ran `npx eslint` directly on it to confirm the error is real (it is), then restored the fix

Refs #410. No functional/behavioral change from what shipped in #459 — same states, same UI, same test coverage passes — this only replaces the internal reset mechanism to be lint-clean and remove the narrow ref/effect race window.

pullRequests.title: Add bidirectional click-to-chat intent bar (#410)
pullRequests.body: ## Summary Closes #410 — bidirectional click→chat: a click in the canvas becomes the next chat turn via `POST /chat-intent`. **Stacked on #409** (base branch `hoopsomuah-agent-actions-409`, not `main`): #410's acceptance criteria require demonstrating the round trip through #409's `useCanvasEvents`/`/events` consumer, which isn't on `main` yet. GitHub will auto-retarget this PR to `main` once #458 merges. ## What's wired + tested (this repo's scope) - **`src/canvas/chatIntent.ts`** — `resolveChatIntentUrl` (mirrors #409's `resolveEventsUrl` origin-derivation) + `postChatIntent`, a defensive client: any non-2xx response or network failure resolves to `{ status: 'unavailable' }`, never throws. This module's **only** network call targets `/chat-intent` — there is no code path here that could issue a direct mutating `/affordance/:name` request, satisfying the consent-routing rule ("mutating intents never issue a direct mutating `/affordance` POST from the iframe") **by construction**, and asserted by e2e test #4 below. - **`src/representation/targets/copilot-home/NodeIntentBar.tsx`** — an extensible action bar (`DEFAULT_NODE_INTENT_ACTIONS`: `pin` / `derives` / `affected` — a plain array, not a hardcoded ceiling of exactly three) with per-action `idle → pending → ok/unavailable` state and a visible hint when unavailable. - Wired into `AnchorFirstView.tsx`: one bar under the anchor's own viewer, one per expanded neighbor card. `chatIntentUrl` threaded through `copilot.tsx`'s `CopilotRenderOptions`/`AnchorRoute`, computed in `EmbeddableApp.tsx` alongside #409's `eventsUrl`. - **Unit tests**: `chatIntent.test.ts` (9 cases — URL resolution incl. malformed `searchServiceUrl`, ok/404/network-rejection outcomes, exact POST body incl. optional prompt) and `NodeIntentBar.test.ts` (4 static-markup structural cases via `renderToStaticMarkup`, matching `CanvasShell.test.ts`'s no-jsdom convention). - **`e2e/node-intent-bar.spec.ts`** (4 cases, chromium + edge, all green): 1. Clicking "What derives from this?" POSTs the exact intent body and flips `pending → ok`. 2. "Pin as anchor" on a neighbor posts the intent, then — via a mocked `/events` `anchor` event reusing #409's already-proven consumer — the panel actually re-anchors on that node. 3. `/chat-intent` returning 404 (older CLI) shows the unavailable hint, zero console errors. 4. Clicking every default action never hits `/affordance/:name`. ## Honest scope note `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli#195` ("click→chat seam / Lane B") is still **open, unimplemented** as of this PR — I checked before writing this. "A real chat turn" per the issue's acceptance criteria can't be verified from this repo alone; there's no live CLI/agent in this test environment. What's proven here is the full template-side contract: the click, the exact POST body, graceful degradation when the endpoint is absent, and the round trip back through #409's SSE consumer once an agent (simulated via mocked `/events`) acts. Once the CLI session lands #195 with a concrete `/chat-intent` request/response shape, this client may need a small follow-up if the shape differs from the proposed `{ intent, nodeId, prompt? } → { ok: true }` contract in #410's issue body. ## Verification - `npm run build` (default) ✅ - `npm run build:local` (e2e's manifest-mode build) ✅ - `npm run lint` ✅ 0 errors, 3 pre-existing warnings (unrelated) - `npm run test` ✅ 933/933 (920 baseline + 13 new) - Full e2e suite (chromium + edge) ✅ 166/166, including the 4 new tests ## Out of scope (per #410's issue body) - Declaring `actions[]` (#409, done). - The CLI SDK message seam (`kbexplorer-cli#195`) — not yet implemented upstream. - Rendering the affordance catalog (#411 — blocked on `#456`, not attempted in this PR per direct instruction from the epic coordinator). ---

pullRequests.title: Agent action surface: SSE /events consumer (#409)
pullRequests.body:
## What
Wires the frozen `/events` SSE contract (`anchor`, `graph-updated`) into the embeddable canvas mount so an agent can drive the panel: `anchor {nodeId}` re-anchors the view, `graph-updated {nodes}` patches the live in-memory graph so it re-renders.

## How
- **`src/canvas/useCanvasEvents.ts`** (new) - pure, DOM-free `resolveEventsUrl` / `applyGraphUpdatedEvent` reducer / `subscribeToCanvasEvents` (injectable `EventSource` factory), plus a thin `useCanvasEvents` hook. Deliberately scoped to only the two **frozen** events per `docs/canvas-loopback-contract.md`.
- **`src/canvas/EmbeddableApp.tsx`** - subscribes via `useCanvasEvents`. `onAnchor` sets `location.hash` (works for both `copilot` and `spa` targets - both mount a `HashRouter`). `onGraphUpdated` patches a new `liveGraph` state, resetting whenever the loaded graph identity changes via React's render-time "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern (not an effect - this repo's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule flagged the effect-based version).

## Deliberate scope limits (honest gaps)
- **`expand`/`trace`/`filter` are NOT wired.** They're proposed in the contract doc but undecided, and the CLI-side companion issue that would declare/emit them hasn't been filed yet. `useCanvasEvents.ts`'s doc comment records this; wiring them later is additive, not a rewrite.
- **`graph-updated` only patches existing nodes by id.** A patch for an unknown id is a clean no-op - it does NOT fabricate a new node, since `KBNode` requires `content`/`connections`/`source`/`cluster` and the contract's terse `nodes[]` payload doesn't specify those. This is a documented, deliberate limitation, not an oversight.

## Tested
- **Unit** - `src/canvas/__tests__/useCanvasEvents.test.ts` (14 tests): `resolveEventsUrl`, the reducer (patch-in-place / ignore-unknown-id / malformed-payload no-op / invalid-entry filtering), and `subscribeToCanvasEvents` (dispatch, error routing, no-handler safety, cleanup) - using a hand-rolled fake `EventSource` (no jsdom needed, matching this repo's existing pure-function test convention, e.g. `useCanvasTheme.test.ts`).
- **E2E** - `e2e/canvas-events.spec.ts` (3 tests x chromium + edge): mocks `/events` via `page.route` with a genuine `text/event-stream` body (no CLI loopback server exists in this repo's own test env), so the real browser `EventSource` parses it exactly as a live server would.
  1. A dispatched `anchor` event actually re-anchors the panel to a dynamically-discovered real neighbor node id.
  2. A `graph-updated` event actually patches the rendered title.
  3. Safe-degrade with **no** `/events` endpoint at all (this repo's own preview/dev server) - asserts no console errors, no crash.
- **Full verification green**: `npm run build` (pass), `npm run lint` (pass, 0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings as baseline), `npm run test` (pass, 920/920 vitest), full `e2e/` suite (chromium + edge) including the pre-existing `canvas-embed.spec.ts` - no regressions.

## Coordination note
Per the cross-repo contract (frozen SSE events only: `anchor`/`graph-updated`), the `expand`/`trace`/`filter` decision is being routed through the creator session coordinating with the sibling `kbexplorer-cli` session. Deferring those pending that relay, per the plan already communicated.

Closes #409

pullRequests.title: Fix: /constellation renders a full-viewport interactive graph, not the decorative hero
pullRequests.body:
## Before / after

**Before:** the `copilot` target's `/constellation` route rendered `HomePage` — the SPA's decorative landing hero. Its only graph visual (`ConstellationHero`) is a translucent, non-interactive band fixed at `height: '35vh'`, physics disabled after a single `fit()`, no `interactive: true`. Clicking a node did nothing; the only affordances were CTA buttons linking to a fixed node (`#/node/readme`). There was no route in the `copilot` target that rendered an actual explorable constellation.

**After:** `/constellation` renders a new `ConstellationView` — a full-viewport, **interactive** force-directed graph, reusing the same `createGraphNetwork` engine helper `HUD`'s expanded-map overlay uses: `interactive: true` (drag-pan, scroll-zoom), `fitOnStabilize: true`, and node clicks re-anchor the panel (`navigate('/node/<id>')`) instead of doing nothing. A thin header (← Back + live node/edge counts) matches the anchor-first view's chrome.

## Scope

Purely additive — only the `/constellation` route element inside `copilot.tsx`'s own `<Routes>` changed. `HomePage.tsx` / `ConstellationHero.tsx` are byte-identical to `main` (still used by the full-page SPA landing and the `homepage` display mode).

## Changes

- **New** `src/representation/targets/copilot-home/ConstellationView.tsx` — the component (header chrome + full-bleed canvas mount).
- **New** `src/representation/targets/copilot-home/mountConstellationNetwork.ts` — the `createGraphNetwork` mounting logic, extracted into its own module so it's directly unit-testable (inject a fake `createGraphNetworkFn` + `navigate`) and so the component file only exports components (`react-refresh/only-export-components`).
- **`copilot.tsx`** — swaps the `/constellation` route element from `HomePage` to `ConstellationView`; removes the now-unused `HomePage` import.
- **`e2e/canvas-embed.spec.ts`** — fixes the now-stale `"Knowledge Clusters"` assertion in the existing #408 zoom-out test, and adds a new spec asserting the canvas fills the panel (not a fixed ~280px/35vh band) and that clicking a node navigates to `/node/<id>`.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Extracts `CanvasShell` (`src/canvas/CanvasShell.tsx`): a documented layout primitive wrapping the `copilot` target's route tree (`/`, `/node/:id`, `/constellation`, `/overview`). Fluid width, no pixel dimensions (`vw`/`%`/Fluent `tokens.*` only, per repo convention — `1px` borders excepted), `overflow-x: hidden` / `overflow-y: auto`, host tokens only — `inherit-host` already supplies `--background-color-default` etc., so no CSS vars are re-mirrored here (a prior audit flagged re-mirroring elsewhere; this doesn't add more).

## Changes

- **`src/canvas/CanvasShell.tsx`** (new): the shell primitive, `data-testid="canvas-shell"` / `data-kbx-shell="canvas"`.
- **`copilot.tsx`**: `renderCopilotSurface()` now wraps `<Routes>` in `<CanvasShell>` — every route in the tree renders inside it.
- **Narrow-column legibility fixes** found while auditing `AnchorFirstView` at ~400px: long anchor/neighbor titles now wrap (`flexWrap` + `overflow-wrap: anywhere`) instead of forcing horizontal scroll; structured-view table keys/values (`reading.css`) wrap long unbroken tokens (ids/urls/hashes) too.
- **Fixed a pre-existing build break** in `copilot.test.ts` (TS2339 from an `as never` cast on `Children.forEach`) discovered while establishing the build baseline — unrelated to this issue but blocking `npm run build`.
- **Unit tests**: `CanvasShell.test.ts` (shell DOM contract) + updated `copilot.test.ts` (unwraps `CanvasShell` when walking routes; asserts the surface's outer element is `CanvasShell`).
- **`e2e/canvas-shell.spec.ts`** (new): Playwright at 400×700, both light and dark `inherit-host` tokens — asserts the shell renders, host tokens are actually honored (not hardcoded — set via `mirrorHostVars` then read back via computed style), no HUD/favicon leak (`[data-testid^="hud-"]` count 0, favicon stays `data:,`), and no horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth <= clientWidth`) both at initial load and after navigating to an expanded neighbor and to the constellation zoom-out.

## Known limitation (honest, out of scope here)

`AnchorFirstView` renders node content via the `resolveViewer()` registry (keyed by `entityType`/`@type`) — a **separate pipeline** from `ReadingView`'s `node.display`-driven switch (`code`/`diagram`/`rich-markdown`/`table`) used by the `spa` target. Rich-markdown/code/diagram-display nodes therefore still fall back to `GenericStructuredView`'s generic key/value dump inside the copilot surface today. Wiring those display modes into `resolveViewer` is real follow-up work — not silently "fixed" here since #412 is scoped to shell/layout only.

pullRequests.title: feat: host CSS-var to Fluent theme adapter + inherit-host mode (#404)
pullRequests.body:
## What

Third of the canvas host-themeability trio under epic #401 — the host CSS-var → Fluent `Theme` adapter, so the SPA inherits a Copilot canvas host's look with **no fork**.

Closes #404

This PR is **independent of #437 (#402/#403)** — it touches different files (`hostTheme.ts`, `useTheme.ts`, `types/index.ts`, the core pin) and is branched from `main`, so it can be reviewed/merged on its own.

### The adapter — `src/theme/hostTheme.ts`
- Reads the semantic host vars named in #404 — `--background-color-default`, `--text-color-*`, `--font-sans`/`--font-mono`, and a true-color accent — with common host aliases (Primer/Copilot) as graceful fallbacks.
- Builds a Fluent `Theme`: neutral background/foreground tokens adopt the host colors; the accent **reseeds the Fluent brand ramp**; fonts adopt the host stacks; base mode (dark/light) is chosen from background luminance. Degrades to `null` (no host theme) when nothing usable is mirrored.
- Pure + injectable reader → fully unit-testable without a DOM.

### Consumes the published contract (core#15, v0.2.0)
- Bumps `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` pin `v0.1.0` → **`v0.2.0`** (what makes `PresentationTokens` importable).
- Folds the host-neutral `PresentationTokens` *intent* knobs (typography size/line-height, corner radius) into the same resolved theme.
- Re-exports `PresentationTokens` + `CANVAS_TARGET` from `../types`.

### Live `inherit-host` mode
- `useTheme.applyConfig` registers the resolved theme under a new `inherit-host` key when host vars are present (null ⇒ no-op), so it joins the selectable set / `t`-cycle and persists. This is the seam the headless embed mount (#406) will drive automatically.

No cached-data shape / localStorage-format change → no `CACHE_VERSION` bump.

## Testing

- **Unit:** `829 passed` (74 files) incl. new `hostTheme.test.ts` (signal reading, alias fallback, neutral/brand/font mapping, luminance base selection, PresentationTokens folding, DOM resolution + SSR-null).
- **Typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Lint:** `eslint .` 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings). **Build:** `vite build` ✓.
- **Visual (Playwright, real Chromium):** injected a host theme onto `:root` (`--background-color-default:#220033`, `--text-color-default:#ffe9b0`, `--font-sans:Georgia`, accent `#ff7ab6`) and selected `inherit-host`. **Zero console errors**; the SPA adopted it end-to-end:
  - `--colorNeutralBackground1` → `#220033`, `--colorNeutralForeground1` → `#ffe9b0`, `--fontFamilyBase` → `Georgia, serif`
  - brand reseeded from accent: `--colorBrandBackground` `#FF469A` (host) vs `#115ea3` (dark)

pullRequests.title: fix: polish constellation rendering (overlap, labels, edges, legend)
pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Fixes the four visual-craft defects in the force-directed constellation (vis-network) called out in #435 — all visible even at very low node counts.

| Defect | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| **1. Node overlap** | Enable `forceAtlas2Based.avoidOverlap: 1` in both the live network and the `computeGraphPositions` minimap pass, enforcing a minimum inter-node gap. |
| **2. Label collision + truncation** | New pure module `src/engine/labelLayout.ts` (`assignLabelPlacements`) does greedy, priority-ordered **anchor selection** (below → above → right → left) with **hide-on-collide** against *all* node bodies (incl. unlabeled) and already-placed labels. The renderer reads a shared mutable `labelState`; labels are **no longer hard-truncated** (full title), and are re-placed after layout settles and on drag. |
| **3. Edges through node bodies** | The custom node's `nodeDimensions` no longer inflates `height` by the label box (`s + 28` → `s`). vis-network clips custom-shape edges to a rectangle derived from `width`/`height`, so the inflated box made edges terminate in the wrong place. Now they clip to the visible node border. |
| **4. No legend for visual identity** | The overlay legend now has a node-identity section explaining shape (circle = topic/issue, rounded-square = container/structure, rounded-rect = document) and the selected glow, alongside the existing cluster/edge keys. |

## Why these levers

- D1 and D3 are fixed through vis-network's own options (`avoidOverlap`, honest `nodeDimensions`) per the issue's preference.
- D2 (label collision avoidance) has **no** native vis-network support, so it's a minimal custom layer: a pure, unit-tested placement function plus a post-layout pass wired into the shared graph factory (so HUD sidebar, HUD overlay, ConstellationHero and HomePage all benefit).

## Verification

**Browser (Playwright vs dev server), introspecting the live network + `labelState`:**

| Detail | Nodes | Node overlaps | Label–label collisions | Label–node collisions | Labels |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| min (issue repro) | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 5 shown, full |
| default | 40 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 13 shown, 3 hidden-on-collide |
| max | 100 | 1 near-tangent pair* | 0 | 0 | 26 shown, 4 hidden |

\* `avoidOverlap` is already at its max (1); a single marginal touch at 100 nodes is far above the "handful of nodes / default zoom" acceptance bar, where spacing is clean.

Dark + light screenshots confirm edges terminating at node borders, full untruncated labels with no collisions, and the new legend.

**CI-equivalent locally:** `tsc -b`, `eslint .` (0 errors), `vitest run` (828 passing, incl. new tests), `vite build` all green.

## Tests added
- `src/engine/__tests__/labelLayout.test.ts` — anchor selection, hide-on-collide, obstacle (unlabeled-node) avoidance, priority ordering, order-independence, no-overlap invariant.
- `src/engine/__tests__/nodeRenderer.test.ts` — `nodeDimensions` equals the drawn shape box (not inflated by the label), locking the edge-clip geometry; label hidden/visible/fallback behavior.

## Notes
- **CACHE_VERSION**: render-only change (physics, label placement, edge geometry, legend); no cached node/edge/localStorage data shape changes → **no bump** (per repo convention).

Closes #435

pullRequests.title: Authored rich-Markdown integration: ingest authored docs into rich-md nodes
pullRequests.body:
## What & why

Closes #431. Refs anokye-labs/kbexplorer#14, #93. Follows #427.

The merged rich-Markdown **rendering** (#427) only fired on the `?demo=richmd` sample — nothing in the engine turned an **authored** Markdown file into a node carrying `data.richMarkdown.blocks`. This wires the published provider package's **pure, browser-safe `./lib`** (`@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown` `ingestRichMarkdown`, no `fs`) into the engine so the renderer fires on real content.

## Approach

- **Dependency:** add `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-provider-rich-markdown` pinned `#v0.1.0`.
- **`AuthoredRichMarkdownProvider`** runs `ingestRichMarkdown` over the inline `authoredContent` the manifest already carries (no filesystem) and **adapts** the package's shape to the template's rendering contract:
  - block `{lang, content, contentHash, span}` → `{kind, source, hash, range}`;
  - `data.richMarkdown` → `{ frontmatter, blocks }` (what `getRichMarkdownDocument` reads);
  - the pure lib's empty `content` → `marked.parse(body)` so the inline prose-fence walk finds the same fences;
  - keeps the core **`buildAddress`** identity minted by the package.
- **Opt-in discriminator:** a doc is ingested iff its frontmatter declares `display: rich-markdown`. A shared `isRichAuthoredMarkdown` predicate lets `AuthoredProvider` **skip** those docs, so each doc is owned by exactly one provider (no double-emit). This deliberately leaves existing authored docs that merely embed a Mermaid fence — and render via the plain prose path — **completely unchanged** (id, identity, display).
- **Browser/node boundary:** `./lib` top-level-imports `node:crypto` (sync `createHash`) and `node:path`. These are aliased in **`vite.config.ts` only** to small browser shims (a dependency-free synchronous SHA-256 that is byte-identical to Node, plus `basename`/`extname`). vitest keeps the real builtins. The package's filesystem `.` export is never bundled — **no `node:fs` in the SPA**.
- Bump `CACHE_VERSION` → 36 (rich-md nodes change id/shape vs the plain path).

## Tests / verification

- New unit tests: provider + adapter (rich-md node, frontmatter facts, mermaid→live / dot→graceful fallback via `planProseFence`, body→HTML), skip-guard partitioning across the two providers, the `isRichAuthoredMarkdown` predicate, and **shim parity** vs `node:crypto`/`node:path`.
- Full suite green (**815 passed**), `tsc -b` clean, eslint clean (only pre-existing warnings), `vite build` succeeds (shims resolve — no `node:` externalization).
- **Browser-verified with Playwright** against a temporary `display: rich-markdown` doc: rich-md document renders, frontmatter fact shows in the structured view, **live Mermaid renders to SVG**, the dot block degrades to raw source, and **zero console errors** (proving the in-browser SHA-256 shim ran — ingestion would have thrown otherwise). Temp fixture removed before commit.

## Follow-up (out of scope here)
After merge, cut the **next minor (e.g. `v0.3.0`)** carrying both #427 and this, so the showcase can bump `TEMPLATE_REF` off `v0.2.0`. The showcase's `content/org/platform.md` must declare `display: rich-markdown` to be ingested.

pullRequests.title: Rich-Markdown rendering with block-renderer registry (#427)
pullRequests.body:
Closes #427.

Renders a rich-Markdown document with **inline embedded blocks**: a block-renderer registry (modeled on the viewer registry), a `RichMarkdownDocumentView` composing frontmatter facts + prose + blocks, reuse of the inline-Mermaid path as the one *live* renderer, and a **pre-built-SVG fallback** that replaces the raw-code display for blocks with no live renderer.

## Acceptance (from the issue) — verified
- ✅ Sample doc renders **frontmatter in the structured view** (reuses `GenericStructuredView`).
- ✅ A **live Mermaid** block renders to SVG (existing inline path, unchanged).
- ✅ `dot` / `canvas` blocks render **via the pre-built-SVG fallback**.
- ✅ **No block falls back to raw code when an SVG exists** (universal SVG fallback in `resolveBlockOutput`; the raw source is tucked into a collapsed `<details>`).
- ✅ **Existing Mermaid tests stay green** (unit `diagram.test.ts` + e2e `display-modes` Mermaid test).

## What's here
- **First step:** bumped `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` to **`github:…#v0.1.0`** (was a pre-tag commit; lockfile now pins `2ce200b`).
- **`src/views/rich-markdown/`** — the pure, node-testable core + thin React layer:
  - `types.ts` — `RichMarkdownBlock` / `RichMarkdownDocument`, `getRichMarkdownDocument(node)`, source hashing/normalization.
  - `registry.ts` — open block-renderer registry (`register`/`resolve`/`has`/`list`/`reset`) + `resolveBlockOutput` (universal pre-built-SVG fallback).
  - `renderers.ts` — built-in `mermaid` (live) + `dot`/`ics`/`canvas` (SVG-preferring) renderers.
  - `plan.ts` — `planProseFence(...)`: Mermaid keeps its live path; other fences match a provider block (by source/hash) and render via the registry.
  - `FrontmatterFacts.tsx`, `RichMarkdownDocumentView.tsx` — the composition.

pullRequests.title: test: refresh visual baselines + seed graph layout; docs: reconcile ocean theme
pullRequests.body:
Closes #414
Refs #394

Two #394 DTU-audit follow-ups (P1 + P3) in one focused PR. Part A grew a small engine fix once the refresh exposed the real root cause (see below).

## Part A (P1) — Refresh the stale L5 visual-regression baselines

`visual-regression.yml` (L5) was failing on every nightly: all 64 surfaces in `review/baselines/` drifted against the committed baselines as the UI evolved.

I refreshed the baselines via the workflow's `update_baselines` path (captured on the **ubuntu** CI runner, never locally — screenshots are font-render-sensitive). But the first verify dispatch still failed on **21 graph-bearing surfaces** (constellation 6–17%, home/hud/reading 0.5–2%), while every pure-content surface passed.

**Root cause (newly discovered):** two ubuntu captures of *identical code* differed by 6–17% on the constellation. The force-directed graph had **no fixed layout seed**, so `vis-network` seeded initial node placement from a fresh RNG on every construction → the stabilized layout differed on every load. A baseline refresh **alone can never green graph surfaces — or the nightly** — because each capture re-randomizes the layout.

**Fix (`fix(engine)` commit):** pin `layout.randomSeed` in `createGraphNetwork` (the live force network + the `computeGraphPositions` minimap helper). Two independent local captures of `constellation--dark` are now **SHA256-identical** (was 6–17% drift) — OS-independent determinism. Positions are computed live (never cached), so **no `CACHE_VERSION` bump** is needed; `vis-network` types `layout` as `any`, so it's type-safe.

I then recaptured the baselines on a **seeded** ubuntu build and re-ran verify:

> ✅ **Green proof — `verify:visual` passed 64/64, 0 over threshold:**
> https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/actions/runs/28387818949

**Nature of the drift (for sign-off):** benign — uniform font/anti-aliasing rendering drift on content surfaces (now eliminated by the refresh) plus run-to-run layout non-determinism on graph surfaces (now eliminated by the seed). **0 dimension mismatches**; no broken layouts.

⚠️ **Large binary diff (64 PNGs) is expected** for a baseline refresh.

🎨 **User-visible side effect:** the seed also makes the rendered graph stable across reloads (it no longer reshuffles each visit). This is intentional and, for a knowledge map, arguably an improvement — flagging it explicitly for review.

## Part B (P3) — Reconcile the `ocean` theme vs `AGENTS.md` (docs only)

The audit flagged that baselines cycle 4 themes (dark/light/sepia/**ocean**) while `AGENTS.md` documented 3. **Not a bug — a doc gap.** Confirmed in code/config:
- `BUILTIN_MODES = ['dark','light','sepia']` (`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`); sepia is a custom `createLightTheme`.
- `content/config.yaml` ships `ocean` (+ `rose`, `midnight`) as named **F2** theme variants; `content/themes/extra-themes.yaml` adds `forest`/`sandstone` via the **F5** `themesFile` and field-merges `ocean`.
- `scripts/review-surfaces.json` lists `[dark, light, sepia, ocean]`.

Updated the `## Themes` note to distinguish **built-in base modes** from **config-added named themes**, and to explain why the review/visual surfaces cycle dark/light/sepia/ocean. **No theme code or config changed.**

## Verification
- `npx tsc -b` clean · `npm run lint` 0 errors · 494 engine/theme/hooks tests green locally.
- Load-bearing proof for Part A is the green `verify:visual` dispatch linked above.

pullRequests.body:
## What

Adds a dedicated `.github/workflows/full-loop.yml` that runs the **layer-4 full-loop deployment scenario** (`npm run test:e2e:full-loop`) on a nightly schedule (**04:45 UTC**) and on `workflow_dispatch`. This closes the L4 nightly-CI gap surfaced by the DTU bit-rot audit (#394), now that L3 (gitea) and L6 (explore) are revived.

## Why a dedicated workflow (not extending `dtu-gitea.yml`)

The full-loop's default substrate is `FULL_LOOP_SUBSTRATE=static` — an in-process mutable GitHub twin, **no Podman, no live Gitea**. Bolting it onto the Podman-based `dtu-gitea.yml` would pay for a container bringup the static substrate doesn't need. A standalone Node + Playwright job is cheaper and more robust. The deferred `gitea` substrate is intentionally **out of scope** (per #269).

## CLI sibling coupling

`e2e/full-loop/global-setup.mts` runs the **real CLI** (`generateManifest()` from `kbexplorer-cli`). `actions/checkout` can't place a repo outside `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so the workflow checks `anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli` out into a workspace subdir and points `KBEXPLORER_CLI_PATH` at it — the exact override `global-setup.mts` documents for CI. The CLI is dependency-free plain JS today; `npm ci` on it is a near no-op kept for forward-compat.

## Workflow shape
- `workflow_dispatch` + `schedule: '45 4 * * *'` (offset: dtu-gitea 04:30 · this 04:45 · visual 05:15 · explore 06:00)
- `permissions: contents: read`, concurrency group with cancel-in-progress
- checkout template → setup-node 22 → checkout CLI → `npm ci` (both) → `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` → run static-substrate full-loop → upload `playwright-report-full-loop` on `always()`

## Docs
Updated `TESTING.md` (pyramid box, Layer 4 "Where it runs", CI orchestration + PR-gate tables) to reflect the new nightly.

pullRequests.title: fix(dtu): static stub manifest (no gh) written before vite for gitea e2e
pullRequests.body:
## What

Follow-up to #399 (which fixed the L3 app-boot 500). This refines the mechanism per Epic-orchestrator guidance: a **static stub** written **before Vite starts**, with no `gh`/GitHub calls.

#399 wrote the stub from `twins/gitea/global-setup.ts`. Two issues with that:

1. **Racy placement → transient error.** Playwright starts the webServers *concurrently with* (in CI, *before*) `globalSetup`, so Vite pre-transforms `src/engine/local-loader.ts` and logs a transient `Failed to resolve import "../generated/repo-manifest.json"` before the stub lands. Specs still pass (Vite self-heals once the file exists), but the error string remains in the dev-server log (a grep false-positive for anyone scanning the nightly lane).
2. An earlier iteration ran `scripts/generate-manifest.js`, which shells out to **`gh`** on every L3 boot — it degrades to empty without `GH_TOKEN`, but adds a network/CLI failure mode to a lane we want reliably green.

## Fix

- New committed, dependency-free script **`twins/gitea/ensure-manifest-stub.mjs`**: writes a minimal `src/generated/repo-manifest.json` (only the required `RepoManifest` fields, empty), **idempotently** (skips when the file already exists, so a real local-mode manifest from `prebuild` is never clobbered). One log line either way.
- **`playwright.gitea.config.ts`**: the Vite webServer command is now `node twins/gitea/ensure-manifest-stub.mjs && node ./node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js …`. Chaining the stub ahead of `vite` is **race-free** — the file exists before Vite's first transform, so the transient error is gone entirely.
- **Reverts** the now-redundant stub-write from `twins/gitea/global-setup.ts` (back to bootstrap + seed only).

Properties: **offline/deterministic** (static stub, no `gh`); L3 stays **REMOTE mode** (no `VITE_KB_LOCAL`), so the manifest is never read at runtime — it exists solely to satisfy Vite's import-analysis resolver. No `/* @vite-ignore */`. Gitignored, so it never enters the seed's `git add -A` snapshot.

## Verification

- `node --check twins/gitea/ensure-manifest-stub.mjs` clean; script write-path + idempotent path both exercised; `vite.transformRequest('/src/engine/local-loader.ts')` → resolves with the stub present.
- `npm test` → **740 pass**; `npm run lint` → **0 errors** (3 pre-existing warnings).
- CI: `dtu-gitea.yml` dispatched against this branch — confirms seed green, **no** `Failed to resolve import` / `Pre-transform error` in the dev-server log, and e2e/gitea specs run (10 passed / 2 skipped — the 2 skips are the documented remote content-model gap, cf #265).

Refs #394

pullRequests.title: fix(dtu): L3 gitea e2e app boot 500s — stub repo-manifest so the dev server boots
pullRequests.body:
## What

The L3 live-Gitea e2e lane (`dtu-gitea.yml` → `playwright.gitea.config.ts`) reaches app bring-up after the seed fix (#396), but the bare Vite dev server **500s** and the app never boots, so every `e2e/gitea` spec fails.

`playwright.gitea.config.ts` serves the app with a **bare** `vite` dev server in **remote mode** (`VITE_GH_API_BASE` set, `VITE_KB_LOCAL` not set). `src/engine/local-loader.ts` statically imports `../generated/repo-manifest.json`, which Vite's import-analysis resolves at **transform time** regardless of mode. That file is gitignored and produced only by `scripts/generate-manifest.js` (normally via the `prebuild` npm script before `vite build`). A bare dev server never runs `prebuild`, so in a fresh CI checkout the file is **absent**:

```
Failed to resolve import "../generated/repo-manifest.json" from "src/engine/local-loader.ts". Does the file exist?
```

L2 (static twin) is unaffected — it serves `vite preview` of a production build where the manifest is generated + bundled. This L3 break was masked until now by the pre-existing seed 404 (#395, fixed in #396).

## Fix

`twins/gitea/global-setup.ts` now writes a minimal **stub** `src/generated/repo-manifest.json` (only the required `RepoManifest` fields, all empty) after bootstrap + seed, **idempotently** (only when the file is absent).

- **Why a stub, not `generate-manifest.js`:** L3 runs the app in **REMOTE mode**, so it sources everything from the live Gitea twin and **never reads the manifest at runtime**. The file only needs to *exist as valid JSON* so Vite's resolver doesn't 500. A stub keeps the harness fully **offline** — no GitHub/`gh` calls (running the live generator would hit GitHub, which L3 doesn't want).
- **Idempotent / non-clobbering:** written only when absent, so a real local-mode manifest (e.g. from `prebuild`) is never overwritten.
- **Snapshot-safe:** the path is gitignored (`src/generated/.gitignore`), so it never enters seed.mjs's `git add -A` snapshot; writing it after seed is belt-and-suspenders on top of that.
- No `/* @vite-ignore */` (would break L2/production local-mode bundling); no change to app code, `local-loader.ts`, or other configs — the change is contained to the gitea harness.

## Verification

- Locally: writing the stub then `vite.transformRequest('/src/engine/local-loader.ts')` → resolves OK (without it → `Failed to resolve import …`). `npm run lint` → 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings). `playwright … --list` → 12 tests in 4 files.
- CI: `dtu-gitea.yml` dispatched against this branch to confirm seed stays green, the app boots, and the e2e/gitea specs run end-to-end.

## Stacking

This branch is **stacked on #396** (the DTU Gitea seed fix); the seed files show in this diff until #396 merges, then auto-clean. This PR's own change is a single file: `twins/gitea/global-setup.ts`.

Closes #397
Refs #394
