name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read
  pull-requests: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Scope concurrency per-ref so PR `test` runs don't cancel each other (a single
# global `pages` group with cancel-in-progress:true killed sibling/main runs
# mid-flight). PR runs supersede older runs of the SAME PR (saves CI minutes);
# different refs never cancel one another. Pushes to main (the only ref that
# deploys) use a distinct group with cancel-in-progress:false, so Pages deploys
# serialize and are never cancelled mid-deployment — preserving the deploy contract.
concurrency:
  group: pages-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci

      # Generate manifest BEFORE typecheck: src/engine/local-loader.ts statically
      # imports the generated src/generated/repo-manifest.json, which is gitignored
      # and absent on a clean checkout. `npm run build`'s `tsc -b` only "worked"
      # locally because npm's implicit `prebuild` hook (also generate-manifest.js)
      # ran first; this workflow invokes `tsc -b` directly, which has no such hook,
      # so a fresh checkout failed `tsc -b` with TS2307 even though #448/#449
      # both looked green with a stale local artifact on disk. Generation is
      # hermetic (local FS/git scan; `gh` calls are best-effort and degrade
      # gracefully without network/token), so it's safe to run this early.
      - name: Generate manifest
        run: node scripts/generate-manifest.js
        env:
          VITE_KB_LOCAL: 'true'
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      # Typecheck: catches breakage `vitest`/`vite build` can miss (#448 shipped
      # in v0.4.0 because tsc -b was never run in this workflow — see #449).
      - name: Typecheck
        run: npx tsc -b

      # Tier 1: Unit tests
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npm test

      # Tier 2: Graph validation
      - name: Validate graph
        run: npm run validate

      - name: Check manifest drift (idempotency)
        run: npm run validate:drift

      - name: Assess graph quality
        run: node scripts/assess-graph.js --gate

      # Build for E2E
      - name: Build
        run: npx vite build
        env:
          VITE_KB_LOCAL: 'true'
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      # Tier 3: E2E tests
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run E2E tests
        run: npx playwright test --project=chromium
        env:
          CI: true

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 14

  build:
    needs: test
    # Deploy on a push to main (human merges) OR an explicit dispatch. The
    # auto-merge workflow dispatches this after a bot merge, because pushes made
    # by GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger the `push` event (anti-recursion). #377
    if: (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci

      - name: Generate manifest
        run: node scripts/generate-manifest.js
        env:
          VITE_KB_LOCAL: 'true'
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Build
        run: npx vite build
        env:
          VITE_KB_LOCAL: 'true'
          VITE_BASE_PATH: /kbexplorer-template/
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Copy index.html to 404.html for SPA routing
        run: cp dist/index.html dist/404.html

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

name: linked-issue

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, labeled, unlabeled]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

concurrency:
  group: linked-issue-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check-linked-issue:
    name: check-linked-issue
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: check-linked-issue
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json
          import os
          import re
          import sys

          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_EVENT_PATH"], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
              event = json.load(handle)

          pull_request = event["pull_request"]
          title = (pull_request.get("title") or "").strip()
          body = pull_request.get("body") or ""
          author = ((pull_request.get("user") or {}).get("login") or "").strip()
          labels = {
              label.get("name")
              for label in pull_request.get("labels", [])
              if label.get("name")
          }

          if author in {"dependabot[bot]", "renovate[bot]", "github-actions[bot]"}:
              print(f"Skipping linked issue enforcement for bot author {author}.")
              sys.exit(0)

          if "no-linked-issue-required" in labels:
              print("Bypass label no-linked-issue-required is present.")
              sys.exit(0)

          text = "\n".join(part for part in (title, body) if part)
          patterns = (
              re.compile(r"(?i)\b(?:close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?|ref(?:erence)?s?|see)\s*:?\s+(?:[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)?#\d+\b"),
              re.compile(r"(?i)https://github\.com/[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+/issues/\d+\b"),
              re.compile(r"(?<![/\w])#\d+\b"),
          )

          if any(pattern.search(text) for pattern in patterns):
              print("Issue reference found in PR title/body.")
              sys.exit(0)

          print(
              '::error title=Linked issue required::Add an issue reference to the PR title or body (for example, "Closes #123" or "#123"), or apply the "no-linked-issue-required" label.'
          )
          sys.exit(1)
          PY
structuralFiles..github/workflows/pr-title.yml:
name: pr-title

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

concurrency:
  group: pr-title-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  pr-title:
    name: pr-title
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: pr-title
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json
          import os
          import re
          import sys

          with open(os.environ["GITHUB_EVENT_PATH"], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
              event = json.load(handle)

          title = (event["pull_request"].get("title") or "").strip()
          if not title:
              print("::error title=PR title required::PR title cannot be empty.")
              sys.exit(1)

          blocked_patterns = (
              re.compile(r"(?i)^\s*\[?\s*wip\b"),
              re.compile(r"(?i)^\s*\[?\s*draft\b"),
              re.compile(r"(?i)^\s*(?:do not merge|dnm)\b"),
          )
          if any(pattern.search(title) for pattern in blocked_patterns):
              print(
                  '::error title=Invalid PR title::Use a descriptive title and avoid empty, WIP, draft, or do-not-merge titles.'
              )
              sys.exit(1)

          print(f"PR title is valid: {title}")
          PY

name: Visual Regression — capture + baseline diff

# Opt-in / scheduled ONLY. Deliberately NOT part of the fast PR gate:
# captures require a full app build + a real browser and produce
# environment-sensitive screenshots that would cause false failures on
# minor font-rendering differences across OS/runner images.
#
# Run it manually to validate a visual-touching change, or let the nightly
# schedule catch drift.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      update_baselines:
        description: 'Promote captures to new baselines (commit the update separately)'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  schedule:
    # Nightly at 05:15 UTC (offset from the DTU job at 04:30).
    - cron: '15 5 * * *'

concurrency:
  group: visual-regression-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  visual-regression:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright (chromium + system deps)
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # Step 1 — build the app in local mode
      - name: Generate manifest
        run: node scripts/generate-manifest.js
        env:
          VITE_KB_LOCAL: 'true'
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Build app (local mode)
        run: npx vite build
        env:
          VITE_KB_LOCAL: 'true'

      # Step 2 — capture fresh screenshots (reuse the dist/ just built).
      # When update_baselines is requested, promote captures in place so the
      # refreshed baselines can be uploaded for a separate human commit.
      - name: Capture review screenshots
        run: npm run capture:review -- --skip-build ${{ inputs.update_baselines && '--update-baselines' || '' }}

      # Step 3 — diff against committed baselines; non-zero exit = regression.
      # Skipped on a baseline-promotion run (nothing to diff against yet).
      - name: Run visual regression check
        if: ${{ !inputs.update_baselines }}
        run: npm run verify:visual

      # Step 3b — on a promotion run, upload refreshed baselines for the
      # maintainer to download and commit deliberately (never auto-committed).
      - name: Upload refreshed baselines
        if: ${{ inputs.update_baselines }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: refreshed-baselines-${{ github.run_number }}
          path: review/baselines/
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # Step 4 — upload artifacts (always, so failures are inspectable)
      - name: Upload screenshots
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: review-screenshots-${{ github.run_number }}
          path: review/screenshots/
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload diff images
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: review-diffs-${{ github.run_number }}
          path: review/diffs/
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload diff report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: visual-diff-report-${{ github.run_number }}
          path: review/visual-diff-report.json
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ignore

files.schema/conventions.yaml:
# conventions.yaml — per-kind storage + mapping.
# `kind` always comes from the entity's `@type`, never from the path below;
# the path is used only to discover files and to detect org (flat vs nested).
typeField: "@type"
idField: id
kinds:
  org:
    path: orgs
    orgScoped: false
  person:
    path: people
    orgScoped: false
    aliasField: alias
  squad:
    path: squads
    orgScoped: true
    companionExt: .md
  workstream:
    path: workstreams
    orgScoped: true
  mission:
    path: missions
    orgScoped: true
  priority:
    path: priorities
    orgScoped: false
  cycle:
    path: cycles
    orgScoped: false
  # ── Work-graph organizational-layer descriptors (#233) ──────
  team:
    path: teams
    orgScoped: true
    aliasField: lead
  system-of-record:
    path: systems-of-record
    orgScoped: false
  # ── Services-monorepo core kinds (#275) ─────────────────────
  service:
    path: services
    orgScoped: false
  decision:
    path: decisions
    orgScoped: false
files.schema/edges.yaml:
# edges.yaml — relationships resolved into the six-relation taxonomy.
edges:
  # alias FK → Person (squad.dri references a person by their alias handle)
  - id: squad-dri
    from: squad
    field: dri
    to: person
    fk: alias
    relation: leads
    description: DRI leads the squad
  # array FK → Person (squad.members is a list of person ids)
  - id: squad-members
    from: squad
    field: members
    to: person
    fk: array
    relation: staffs
    description: Squad staffs member
  # scalar FK → Workstream
  - id: squad-workstream
    from: squad
    field: workstream
    to: workstream
    fk: scalar
    relation: structural
    description: Squad delivers workstream
  # scalar FK → Priority (has-priority relation for descriptor workstreams — #233)
  - id: workstream-priority
    from: workstream
    field: priority
    to: priority
    fk: scalar
    relation: has-priority
    description: Workstream serves priority
  # scalar FK → Person (may be unresolved → stub node)
  - id: person-manager
    from: person
    field: manager
    to: person
    fk: scalar
    relation: reports-to
    description: Reports to
  # composite FK "<cycle>:<squad>" → two edges
  - id: mission-assignment
    from: mission
    field: assignment
    fk: composite
    relation: structural
    composite:
      - to: cycle
        relation: structural
      - to: squad
        relation: structural

  # ── Work-graph descriptor edges (#233) ─────────────────────
  # team.lead → person (alias FK → leads edge)
  - id: team-lead
    from: team
    field: lead
    to: person
    fk: alias
    relation: leads
    description: Team is led by
  # team.members → person[] (array FK → staffs edges)
  - id: team-members
    from: team
    field: members
    to: person
    fk: array
    relation: staffs
    description: Team staffs member
  # team.workstreams → workstream[] (array FK → owns edges)
  - id: team-workstreams
    from: team
    field: workstreams
    to: workstream
    fk: array
    relation: owns
    description: Team owns workstream
  # workstream.team → team (scalar FK → structural back-edge)
  - id: workstream-team
    from: workstream
    field: team
    to: team
    fk: scalar
    relation: structural
    description: Workstream belongs to team
  # workstream.systems-of-record → system-of-record[] (array FK; entries are id strings or { id } objects → tracked-in edges)
  - id: workstream-sor
    from: workstream
    field: systems-of-record
    to: system-of-record
    fk: array
    relation: tracked-in
    description: Workstream tracked in system of record

  # ── Service + Decision edges (Feature H — #275) ────────────
  # NOTE: service/decision are authority-scoped, so a scalar/array FK to an
  # org-scoped target (team / workstream / mission) resolves the target in its
  # default (home) org. Cross-org references would need an explicit org and are
  # out of scope here — the example entities all point at default-org targets.
  # service.team → team (scalar FK → owned-by edge)
  - id: service-owner
    from: service
    field: team
    to: team
    fk: scalar
    relation: owned-by
    description: Service owned by team
  # service.systems-of-record → system-of-record[] (array FK → tracked-in edges)
  - id: service-sor
    from: service
    field: systems-of-record
    to: system-of-record
    fk: array
    relation: tracked-in
    description: Service tracked in system of record
  # decision.deciders → person[] (array FK → decided-by edges)
  - id: decision-deciders
    from: decision
    field: deciders
    to: person
    fk: array
    relation: decided-by
    description: Decision decided by
  # decision affects work — split across two fields because an FK rule has a
  # single target kind; both emit the `affects` relation.
  # decision.affects-workstreams → workstream[] (array FK → affects edges)
  - id: decision-affects-workstream
    from: decision
    field: affects-workstreams
    to: workstream
    fk: array
    relation: affects
    description: Decision affects workstream
  # decision.affects-missions → mission[] (array FK → affects edges)
  - id: decision-affects-mission
    from: decision
    field: affects-missions
    to: mission
    fk: array
    relation: affects
    description: Decision affects mission

derived:
  # squads that deliver the same workstream are aligned (computed, not stored)
  - id: squad-coalignment
    type: shared-target
    via: squad-workstream
    relation: derived
    description: Aligned via shared workstream

deprecated:
  # legacy ownership — resolved but tagged `deprecated`
  - id: squad-legacy-owner
    from: squad
    field: legacyOwner
    to: person
    fk: alias
    relation: deprecated
files.schema/lifecycle.yaml:
# lifecycle.yaml — bands group kinds by how often they change.
bands:
  durable:
    - org
    - person
    - squad
    - workstream
    # Work-graph descriptor kinds (#233) — durable organizational layer
    - team
    - system-of-record
    # Services-monorepo core kinds (#275)
    - service
  per-cycle:
    - mission
    - cycle
    - priority
  per-event:
    # Decisions (ADRs) are immutable point-in-time records (#275)
